Et dedit Dominus Ruth, vt conciperet, &c.
units.tr: In Sarai we must praise the fact that she does not say to her husband, "Give me children, or else I shall die," as Rachel said to Jacob (Genesis 30), but she acknowledges that the power of closing and opening the womb lies in the hands of the Lord, and that to bear children is God's work and gift, not nature's; in accordance with Psalm 113: "He makes the barren woman dwell in the house as a joyful mother of children." And Genesis 30: "God remembered Rachel, and heard her, and opened her womb, and she conceived and bore a son." Likewise Ruth 4: "And the Lord gave Ruth that she should conceive," etc.

units.la: In Abrahamo laude dignum est, quòd vxorem suam ob sterilitatem non despicit. Nam admodum stolidè atque imprudenter agunt, qui vxoribus adscribunt sterilitatem, (quas potius consolari decet, cum sunt steriles, iuxta exemplū Elcanæ, 1.Reg.1.) vel fœcunditatem, quasi nescientes, quòd à naturæ Códitore fiant universa: & quòd neq; coitus, neque aliud quiddam ad procreandos pueros sufficere potest, nisi cooperetur manus superna, quæ naturam ad procreandum excitet. Quæ sanè iustus ille sciens, uxori non imputabat quòd carebant filijs, sed congruuum honorem semper ei tribuebat. Item in Abrahamo laudabilis est fides in expectanda promissione per decè annos in Chanaan: præterea eius mansuetudo erga irritatam vvore[?], & studiû conservandæ pacis in domo.
units.tr: In Abraham it is worthy of praise that he does not despise his wife on account of her barrenness. For they act very foolishly and imprudently who ascribe barrenness or fruitfulness to wives (whom it is rather fitting to console when they are barren, as in the example of Elkanah, 1 Samuel 1), as if they did not know that all things are made by the Creator of nature, and that neither intercourse nor anything else can suffice for the begetting of children unless a hand from above cooperates, stirring nature to procreate. That righteous man, knowing this, did not impute to his wife that they lacked children, but always paid her the honour that was due. Likewise, Abraham's faith is praiseworthy in awaiting the promise for ten years in Canaan; besides, there is his gentleness toward his wife when she was provoked, and his zeal for keeping peace in the house.

units.la: In Agar notanda superbia, & servilis ingenij natura, quæ res prosperas moderatè ferre nequit, & ingratitudo, & impatientia: quæ vitia angelus Domini in ea reprehendit, & contrà humilitatem docuit, atq; animi submissionem. In hoc tamen commendanda est hæc ancilla, quòd angelo interroganti, unde veniret, respondit: A facie Sarae dominę meę ego fugio. Citra odium enim meminit dominæ:neq; dicit, Malè me afflixit, gravia mihi fecit, verbis, minis, impositis servilibus operibus, nec possum ferre molestiam eius, & ideò fugam inij: nihil asperum loquuta est: sed solum seipsam, ut fugitivam accusavit.
units.tr: In Hagar we must note her pride and servile nature, which cannot bear prosperity with moderation, and her ingratitude and impatience; the angel of the Lord rebuked these vices in her and taught the contrary humility and submissiveness of spirit. In this respect, however, this handmaid is to be commended: when the angel asked her whence she had come, she answered, "I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarai." For she mentions her mistress without hatred; she does not say, "She has treated me badly, she has made my life hard with words and threats and servile tasks, and I cannot bear her trouble, and so I have taken flight"; she says nothing harsh, but accuses only herself, as a fugitive.

units.la: Postremò hic etiam apparet afflictionis fructus, & invocationis nominis Domini efsectus. Bonus enim est Dominus sine respectu personarum omnib.invocantib.se. Huic debetur honos, imperium, & potestas in æ-ternum, Amen.
units.tr: Finally, here too appears the fruit of affliction and the effect of calling on the name of the Lord. For the Lord is good, showing no partiality to all who call upon him. To him be honour, dominion and power for ever, Amen.

units.la: CONCIO VI
units.tr: SERMON VI

units.la: Genef. 20.
units.tr: Genesis 20.

units.la: Tprofectus est inde (ex Mabre) Abraham in terram australem, habitauitq; inter Cades, & inter Sur, & peregrinatus est in Gerar. Dixitq; Abraham de Sara uxore sua: Soror mea est: & misit Abimelech rex Gerar, & tulit Saram. Venit autem Deus ad Abimelech in somnio noctis, & dixit ad eum: Ecce tu morieris propter mulierem quam accepisti, est enim marito iuncta. Abimelech vero non accesserat ad eam: & ait: Domine, num quid interficies quoque gentem iustam? An non ipse dixit mihi, soror mea est? cum integritate cordis mei, & cum innocentia manuum mearum feci hoc. Dixitq; ad eum Deus per somnium: Etiam ego novi, quòd in integritate cordis tui feceris hoc, & prohibui etiam ego te, ne peccares in me, atque ideo non permisi ut tangeres eam. Nunc igitur restitue uxorem viro, est enim propheta, & orabit pro te, ut vivas: quòd si non restitueris, scito quòd moriendo morieris et tu & omnia qua habes. ⌣Abimelach itaq; mane cofurgens, vocauit omnes seruos suos, et loquutus est omnes sermones hos in auribus illorum: tinuerunt[?] q; viri illi valde. Et vocauit Abimelach ⌣Abraham, dixitq; ad eum: quid fecisti nobis, & quid peccaui in te, quod induxisti super me & super regnum meum peccatum grande? opera quæ non fieri debent, fecisti in me. Dixitq; Abimelach ad Abraham: quid vidisti quod fecisti rem istam? Respondit Abraham, quia dixi: certe non est timor Dei in loco isto, & interficient me causa uxoris meæ. Sed & vere soror mea est: est enim filia patris mei: tamen si non sit filia matris meæ, & facta est mihi in uxorem. Factum q; est, cum me exulare fecisset Deus de domo patris mei, dixi ad eam: hæc sit pietas tua quam facies mecum: in omni loco ad quem peruenerimus, dices de me, frater meus est. Tulit itaque Abimelach oues & boues, seruos & ancillas, & dedit ⌣Abraham, reddiditq; illi Saram uxorem eius. Et dixit Abimelach: ecce terra mea coram te est, habita ubi tibi commodum visum fuerit. Ad Saram vero dixit: ecce dete dedi mille argenteos fratri tuo, ecce est tibi in velamen oculorum ad omnes qui tecum sunt, & sic cum omnibus reprehensa est. Orauit itaq; Abraham ad Deum: & sanauit Deus Abimelach & uxorem eius, atque ancillas eius, & pepererunt. Nam claudendo repressit Dominus omne vuluam domus Abimelach, ob causam uxoris [?]Abraham.
units.tr: Abraham then set out from there (from Mamre) into the southern land, and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar. And Abraham said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah. But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, "Behold, you shall die because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman." Now Abimelech had not approached her, and he said, "Lord, will you slay even a righteous nation? Did he not himself tell me, 'She is my sister'? And she herself said, 'He is my brother.' I have done this with a clear heart and innocent hands." Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart; and I also kept you from sinning against me, and so I did not allow you to touch her. Now therefore restore the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not restore her, know that you shall surely die, you and all that are yours." So Abimelech rose early in the morning, called all his servants, and told all these words in their hearing; and those men feared greatly. Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me deeds that ought not to be done." And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you see that made you do this thing?" Abraham answered, "Because I thought, surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me for the sake of my wife. And indeed she is truly my sister; she is the daughter of my father, though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife. And when God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, 'Show this kindness to me: in every place to which we come, say of me, He is my brother.'" So Abimelech took sheep and oxen, male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored to him his wife Sarah. And Abimelech said, "Behold, my land is before you; dwell where it seems good to you." But to Sarah he said, "Behold, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your brother; behold, this is a covering of the eyes for you before all who are with you; and so you are vindicated before everyone." Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children. For the LORD had closed fast every womb of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

units.la: 1 Abrahamus & Sara proponuntur fidelibus in exemplum, & nominatim coniugibus Christianis. 1.Pet.3. Etenim propterea iustorum omnium virtutes, spiritus sancti gratia & dispensatione, scripturis sunt traditae, ut nos continuam habentes doctrinam, & ad aemulationem & imitationem iustorum vitam nostram instituamus. Oportet ergo nos scire, quomodo illi se gesserint, quidque illis acciderit. Instituerunt autem vitam suam in hac terra sicut peregrini & advenae: & recte quidem. Nam tempus contractum est, & habitus huius mundi praeterit, 1.Corinth. 7. Ideo nunc hic, nunc isthic tabernacula erigebant, quasi in peregrinatione agentes: non sicut nos facimus, habitantes in aliena terra quasi in patria, & domos extruimus splendidas, & deambulacra: & villas possidemus, & balnea facimus, aliaque plurima. Sed vide quomodo iustus substantiam suam in vernaculis tantùm & pecoribus possidens, & nunquam in eodem loco stans: & aliquando quidem in Bethel figit tabernaculla: interim autem apud quercum Mambre. Interdum in Aegyptum descendit, nunc autem in Geraris tabernaculum figit: & omnia facilè sustinet, & gratitudinem erga suum dominü per omnia manifestè declarat: & post tantas promissiones, quæ ei à Deo factæ erant, videns se in tantis versari difficultatibus, & in diversas tentationes incidere, quasi adamas immotus persistit: piamque suam mentem ostendens; nullis obstaculis fiebat negligentior. Vide enim & nunc dilecte, qualis tentatio eum in Geraris invadit, & admirare fortitudinem & virtutem iusti, quomodo quod omnibus intolerabile, & quod neque auribus suscipere quis vellet, hoc ipse sustinuit: non ægrè ferens, neque exigens à Domino, ut ulcisceretur ea quæ fiebant, sicut plerique homines faciunt, hique innumeris peccatorum sarcinis pressi. Nam cùm in difficultates quasdam inciderint, statim obmurmurant, & curiosius inquirunt, & dicunt: Quare hoc & hoc evenit? quare hoc & hoc permissum est? At iustus ille non sic: unde & amplior ei superna gratia concessa est.
units.tr: 1 Abraham and Sarah are set before the faithful as an example, and especially before Christian married couples (1 Pet. 3). For the virtues of all the righteous have been handed down in the Scriptures, by the grace and disposition of the Holy Spirit, so that, having a continual teaching, we may order our lives in emulation and imitation of the righteous. We ought therefore to know how they conducted themselves and what happened to them. They spent their lives in this land as strangers and sojourners, and rightly so: for the time is short, and the form of this world passes away (1 Cor. 7). So they pitched their tents now here, now there, as men living in a foreign land; not as we do, who dwell in a strange land as if it were our homeland, and build splendid houses, and walks, and possess country estates, and make baths, and many other things. But see how the righteous man, possessing his substance only in tents and flocks, and never standing in one place, sometimes pitches his tents at Bethel, at other times by the oak of Mamre; at times he goes down into Egypt, and now he pitches his tent in Gerar. He bears all things easily and openly declares his gratitude to his Lord in everything. And after such great promises which God had made to him, seeing himself caught in such great difficulties and falling into various temptations, he stood firm like an immovable adamant, showing his pious mind; he was never made more careless by any obstacles. For see now, beloved, what temptation attacked him in Gerar, and admire the courage and virtue of the righteous man, how he endured what is intolerable to all, and what anyone would be unwilling even to hear: he did not bear it grudgingly, nor demand that the Lord avenge what was being done, as most men do, who are weighed down by countless burdens of sins. For when they fall into certain difficulties, they immediately grumble, inquire too curiously, and say, "Why has this happened? Why has this been permitted?" But that righteous man did not do so; and therefore a greater heavenly grace was granted to him.

units.la: Etsi igitur multæ sunt tribulationes iustorum & fideles coniuges afflictionem habent in carne: tamen ex his omnibus liberat eos Dominus, & tandem illis benedicit, ut hic Abrahamo, cui Abimelæch, qui prius vxorem tulerat, postea de suo largitus est munera.
units.tr: Although therefore the tribulations of the righteous are many, and faithful spouses have affliction in the flesh, yet the Lord frees them from all these things, and at last blesses them, as here to Abraham, to whom Abimelech, who had earlier taken away his wife, afterwards gave gifts from his own goods.

units.la: 2 Exponuntur autem hæc ordine in ista sacra historia: principio raptus Sarae, quæ soror erat Abrahami, ut Lothus frater: quia neptis ex fratre Aran, qui eundem cum Abrahamo patrem, videlicet Thare habuit, sed non eandem matrem, vel filia patris Abrahami adoptiva, ut quidam putant. Deinde providentia Dei pro liberanda Sara: accusatio & iudicium Abimelechi regis Palaestinorum: causa accusationis & intentatæ mortis, quâ merentur adulteri: defensio Abimelechi, primo negantis Saram attactam: deinde dicentis, non uxorem, sed sororem ablatam: querela eiusdem & expostulatio ad Abrahamum: purgatio Abrahami, qui propter metu mortis, quæ nondum per mortem Christi erat mortificata, sustinuit suis oculis, ut socia vitæ suæ in regis manus incideret: fructus patientiæ in tentatione, per quam muneribus Abrahamus ornatur ab eo, quem dissimulato uxoris nomine in periculum adduxerat: precatio Abrahami pro Abimelecho, quem Deus (sicut & Pharaonem, Genes. 12.) propter Abrahamum servum suum corripuerat (qui enim peccat in sanctos, in ipsum deum peccat, Zachar. 2. Luc. 10.) & eiusdem exauditio.
units.tr: 2 These things are set out in order in this sacred history: first the abduction of Sarah, who was Abraham's sister, as Lot was his brother, for she was the daughter of Haran, the brother of Abraham, who had the same father, namely Terah, but not the same mother; or, as some think, she was Abraham's adoptive daughter. Then the providence of God for the rescue of Sarah; the accusation and judgment of Abimelech, king of the Philistines; the cause of the accusation and the threatened death, which adulterers deserve; the defence of Abimelech, who first denied that Sarah had been touched, and then said that it was not a wife but a sister who had been taken away; his complaint and remonstrance to Abraham; the vindication of Abraham, who, out of fear of death, which had not yet been put to death through the death of Christ, allowed his wife to fall into the king's hands by his own eyes, having concealed the name of wife and brought her into danger; the fruit of patience in temptation, whereby Abraham is adorned with gifts by him whom he had led into danger by concealing his wife's name; Abraham's prayer for Abimelech, whom God (as also Pharaoh, Gen. 12) had rebuked on account of Abraham his servant (for whoever sins against the saints sins against God himself, Zech. 2; Luke 10), and the granting of that prayer.

units.la: 3 Porro si rex ille in Gerarim ex ignorantia peccans punitur, quid accidet illis, qui volentes & scientes peccant? Orandus ergo Deus,vt nos à peccato conseruet atque custodiat: id quod fit tribus modis, teste Augustino lib.2. Medit. scilicet occasionis subtractione, resistendi data virtute, affectionis sanitate. Item, si Abrahamus pro raptore vxoris suae rogauit: debemus etiam nos hoc opus Abrahami facere, ac orare pro inimicis,Matth.5.
units.tr: 3 Further, if that king who sinned in Gerar out of ignorance was punished, what will happen to those who sin willingly and knowingly? God must therefore be prayed to keep us from sin and guard us, which is done in three ways, according to Augustine in the second book of the Meditations: namely, by removing the occasion, by giving the strength to resist, and by the health of the affections. Likewise, if Abraham prayed for the one who had taken his wife, we too ought to do this work of Abraham and pray for our enemies (Matt. 5).

units.la: Cogitemus etiam hic grauitatem tentationis fidei Abrahami,cui ex Sara promissus erat filius. Nihil enim minus futurum videbatur, quàm vt ex Sara iam ab Abimelecho rapta,Isaacus nasceretur. Sed ille silenter[?] ferebat omnia,sciens quòd se non esset defpecturus dominus, sed acceleratum adhibiturus subsidium.
units.tr: Let us also consider here the severity of the temptation to Abraham's faith, to whom a son had been promised through Sarah. For nothing seemed less likely to happen than that Isaac should be born of Sarah, now already taken by Abimelech. But he bore everything in silence, knowing that the Lord would not forsake him, but would bring a speedy help.

units.la: Admirabilis quoq; Sarae charitas est,quae periculo mortis iustum eripere voluit.Poterat enim ipsa detegendo factum, contumeliam effugere:sed pertulit omnia fortiter,vt viro salutem pararet. Et impletum est illud dictum: Erunt duo in carnem vnam. Ita mutuae salutis curam vicissim agebant, & tanta declarabant concordiam,quasi vnum essent corpus,& vna anima. Audiant haec viri,audiant & mulieres:& istae quidem vt eandem erga suos viros charitatem declaret, & nihil aliud illorum praeferant saluti:viri autem erga vxores habeant benevolentiam, & quasi vnam animam & vnum corpus possiderent, omnia faciant. Hoc enim verum est coniugium, quando tanta inter eos est concordia, quando vinculo charitatis ita sunt concatenati. Sicut enim corpus nunquam à semetipso dissidet, neq; anima aduersus seipsam: ita virum & mulierem non conuenit diffidere. Tunc enim bona infinita sibi coaceruare poterunt. Vbi enim concordia, ibi bonorum confluxus, ibi pax, ibi charitas, ibi spiritualis laetitia: nullum bellum, nulla rixa, nusquam inimicitiae & contentio: sed haec omnia é medio tolluntur per concordiam, bonorum omnium radicem, quae omnia illa simul abolet. Vide deniq; Dei misericordiam, quomodo, quia vidit iusta propter merum mortis, Sarę ablationem fortiter ferre, & regem eam vt sororem iusti abducere: suam postea declarat prouidentiam, iusta quoq; illustriore reddit, & Saram ab iniuria, regem vero à peccato liberat. Hoc enim potest, Iudith 13. Iudae 1. Cætetum haec audiens dilecte, ne condemnes iustum (qui homo fuit, non angelus) ob pusillanimitate, quod mortem timuerit: sed potius admirare conditore vniuersi, qui tantae erga nos est misericordiae, quod mortem iustis illis & sanctis tunc terribilem, eandem nunc ita contemptibilem fecerit Christus, vt quam formidabant illi virtute clari, & tanta erga Deum fiducia freti, nunc derideant & iuuenes, & tenerae virgines. Nihil enim mors est vltra, quàm somnus & peregrinatio, & transmigratio à deterioribus ad meliora. Mors enim Domini immortalitatem nobis donauit. Huic igitur debetur honor & gloria in sempiternum, Amen.
units.tr: Sarah's love is also admirable, for she was willing to rescue the righteous man from the danger of death. For she could have escaped the insult by disclosing the deed; but she bore everything bravely, so that she might secure her husband's safety. And that saying was fulfilled: "The two shall be one flesh." Thus they took turns in caring for each other's safety, and showed such great harmony, as if they were one body and one soul. Let husbands hear this, and let wives hear it too: let the wives show the same love towards their husbands and prefer nothing to their safety; and let husbands have goodwill towards their wives and do everything as if they possessed one soul and one body. For that is true marriage, when there is such great harmony between them, when they are bound together by the chain of love. For just as the body never quarrels with itself, nor the soul against itself, so it is not fitting for husband and wife to be at odds. For then they can heap up for themselves unending goods. Where there is harmony, there is a flowing together of goods, there is peace, there is love, there is spiritual joy; no war, no quarrel, nowhere enmity and strife; but all these things are removed from the midst by harmony, the root of all good things, which abolishes all of them at once. Finally, see the mercy of God: because he saw that the righteous man bore the abduction of Sarah bravely, out of fear of death, and that the king took her away as the righteous man's sister, he afterwards displayed his providence, made the righteous man more illustrious, and freed Sarah from injury and the king from sin. For he can do this (Judith 13; Jude 1). Hearing these things, beloved, do not condemn the righteous man (who was a man, not an angel) for timidity because he feared death; but rather admire the Creator of the universe, who has such mercy towards us that he has made that death, once so terrible to those righteous and holy men, now so contemptible through Christ, that those who were once bold in virtue and relied on such great trust in God, now young men and tender virgins mock. For death is nothing more than sleep and a journey, and a passing over from worse things to better. For the death of the Lord has given us immortality. To him therefore be honour and glory for ever, Amen.

units.la: CONCIO VIII.
units.tr: SERMON VIII.

units.la: Genef. 21.
units.tr: Gen. 21.

units.la: VISITAVIT autem Dominus Saram, quemadmodum dixerat: fecitq; dominus Sara, sicut loquutus fuerat. Nam concepit & peperit Sara ipsi Abraham filium in senectute sua, idq; illo tempore, quod prædixerat ei Deus. Et Abraham vocauit nomen filii sui, qui sibi natus erat, & quem sibi genuerat Sara, Isahac. Circumcidit quoque Abraham Isahac filium suum, cum esset filius octo dierum, quemadmodum præceperat illi Deus. Porrò Abraham fuit filius centum annorum, cum sibi nasceretur Isahac filius suus. Sara verò dixit: risum fecit mihi Deus, ut omnis qui audierit, corrideat mihi. Dixitq;, quis unquam dixit Abraha, lactauit Sara filios? siquidem genvi filium in senectute illius. Creuit itaque puer & ablactatus est, fecitq; Abraham convivium magnum illo die cum ablactaretur Isahac. Et vidit Sara filium Hagar Aegyptia, quem illa genuit ipsi Abraham, esse derisorem. Unde dixit ad Abraham: eijce[?] ejce[?] ancillam istam & filium eius: non enim erit heres filius istius ancillae cum filio meo, nempe cum Isahac. Et valde displicuit verbum istud in oculis Abraham, super causa filii sui. Et dixit Deus ad Abraham: Non displiceat in oculis tuis super puero, & super ancilla tua: omnia quae dixerit tibi Sara, audi vocem eius, quia in Isahac vocabitur tibi semen. Quin & filium ancillae ponam in gentē, quia semen tuum est. Surrexit itaque Abraham diluculo, & tulit panem & lagenulam aquae, deditq; Agar, imponens humero eius unā cum puero, & emisit eam: quae abiens erravit in deserto Beer Sæba. Consumptaq; quoque jam aqua in lagenula, & proiecit puerum sub unum ex virgultis. Et abiens sedit e regione, elongans scilicet se quantum est iactus arcus: dixit enim, non Videbo morte pueri, & sedens ex adverso, levavit vocem suam & fleuit. Audivit autem Deus vocem pueri, vocavitq; angelus Dei Hagar de cælo, & dixit ad eam: quid est tibi Hagar? noli timere, quia exaudivit Deus vocem pueri ex eo(loco)in quo est: Surge, tolle puerum, & apprehende eum manu tua, quoniam in gentem magnam ponā eum. Et aperuit Deus oculos eius, viditque fontem aquarum: & abiens implevit lagenulam aqua, & dedit puero bibere. Fuit autem Deus cum puero, & crevit, mansitq; in solitudine, & factus est sagittarius. Habitauit autem in deserto Pharan: & accepit illi mater sua uxorem de terra Ægypti.
units.tr: The Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did to Sarah as he had spoken. For Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the time of which God had told him. And Abraham called the name of his son, who was born to him and whom Sarah bore him, Isaac. Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him. Now Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. And Sarah said, God has made me laugh, so that everyone who hears will laugh with me. She said, Who would ever have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age. The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned. And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking. Therefore she said to Abraham: Cast out this maidservant and her son; for the son of this maidservant shall not be heir with my son, that is, with Isaac. The matter was very grievous in Abraham's eyes, on account of his son. But God said to Abraham: Do not let it displease you concerning the boy and your maidservant; whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Isaac shall your seed be called. I will also make the son of the maidservant into a nation, because he is your seed. So Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, putting them on her shoulder along with the boy, and sent her away. She departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. When the water in the skin was used up, she cast the boy under one of the shrubs, and went and sat opposite him, at about the distance of a bowshot, for she said, Let me not see the death of the boy; and sitting over against him, she lifted up her voice and wept. God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her: What troubles you, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Arise, lift up the boy and take him by the hand, for I will make him a great nation. Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy to drink. God was with the boy, and he grew, and lived in the wilderness, and became an archer. He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took him a wife from the land of Egypt.

units.la: I In hac historia de genito Isaaco, & de eius ancilla eiusque filio, habemus multa notatu digna. Ac primum quidem consideranda nobis proponitur Dei bonitas, veritas, & omnipotentia. Visitauit enim Saram sterilem, atque eius recordatus est, quemadmodum dixit & promisit Genes. 17. & 18. In Abrahamo & in Sara discimus fidem, obedientiam, spem, & patientiam. Abrahamus enim recte Apostolo Romanorum 4. praeter spem sub spe credidit, se fore patrem multarum gentium: iuxta id quod dictum est: Sic erit semen tuum. Ac non infirmatus fide, haud confiderauit suum ipsius corpus iam emortuum, quum centum fere natus esset annos, nec ea[?] mortuam vuluā Sarae: verum ad promissionem Dei non haesitabat ob incredulitatem, sed robustus factus est fide, tribuens gloriam Deo: certa persuasione concepta, quod is, qui promiserat, idem potens esset & praestare. Quapropter etiam imputatum est illi ad iustitiam. Per fidem & ipsa Sara, vt Hebræor. ii. legimus, vim ad concipiendum ac retinendum semen accepit, ac praeter aetatis rationem peperit, quod fidelem iudicaret eum, qui promiserat. Igitur dilecti, & nos eandem, quam fideles illi patientiam habeamus, & nunquam desides fimus: sed spe bona recreemur, scientes quod neque rerum difficultas, neque aliud quid humanum obstaculum nobis esse poterit, si quando Dei gratia suam declarare voluerit liberalitatem. Quoties enim ille annuit, omnia sibi cedunt & obtepe rat [?], & difficilia facilia, & impossibilia possibilia sunt: tantum firma in ipso fidem conferuemus, & ad magnitudinem potentiae suae sperantes, humanis omnib. superiores fiamus.
units.tr: I. In this history of the birth of Isaac, and of his maidservant and her son, we have many things worth noting. First, we are shown the goodness, truthfulness and omnipotence of God. For he visited barren Sarah and remembered her, just as he had said and promised in Genesis 17 and 18. In Abraham and Sarah we learn faith, obedience, hope and patience. For Abraham, as the Apostle says in Romans 4, against hope believed in hope, that he would become the father of many nations, according to what was said: So shall your seed be. And not weakened in faith, he did not consider his own body, now as good as dead, since he was almost a hundred years old, nor the dead womb of Sarah; but he did not hesitate at God's promise through unbelief, but was made strong in faith, giving glory to God, being fully persuaded that he who had promised was also able to perform it. Therefore it was also counted to him for righteousness. Through faith Sarah herself, as we read in Heb. 11, received power to conceive and to retain seed, and bore a child beyond the course of her age, because she judged him faithful who had promised. Therefore, beloved, let us also have the same patience as those faithful ones, and never be idle; but let us be refreshed by good hope, knowing that neither the difficulty of things nor any other human obstacle can stand in our way, whenever the grace of God wishes to show its generosity. For whenever he consents, all things yield to him: difficult things become easy, and impossible things possible. Only let us keep firm faith in him, and hoping in the greatness of his power, let us rise above all human things.

units.la: Obseruandum hoc loco etiam est, liberos esse Dei donum. Concepit enim & peperit Sara vi promissionis diuinae: quod & ipsa postea fatetur, vbi ait, Risum fecit mihi Dominus.i. Deus me affecit gaudio, & quicunque audierit, corridebit mihi .i. congratulabitur mihi, & gaudebit de Dei bonitate. Et maximè hoc dicitur, quia de Isaac nata est beata virgo, quae per filium suum gaudium attulit vniuerso mundo, Luc.2. qui filius initium signorum suorum fecit in Cana Galilęæ, vbi aquam vertit in bonum ac generosum vinum, Ioan. 2. vinum autem laetificat cor hominis, Pfal.104. Porrò Isaac risum, seu gaudium sonat. Hunc Abrahamus non genuit, nisi iam emortuo corpore, tum ipsius, tum vxoris, cui iam desierant muliebria. Hoc arcanum gaudium mentis sibi bené conscię, non nascitur in nobis, nisi per spiritum mortificatis carnis affectibus.
units.tr: It must also be observed here that children are a gift of God. For Sarah conceived and bore by the power of the divine promise; she herself confesses this afterwards, when she says, The Lord has made me laugh, that is, God has filled me with joy, and whoever hears will laugh with me, that is, will rejoice with me and be glad at God's goodness. And this is said especially because the blessed Virgin was born of Isaac's line, who through her Son brought joy to the whole world, Luke 2. This Son made the beginning of his signs at Cana of Galilee, where he turned water into good and noble wine, John 2. And wine gladdens the heart of man, Ps. 104. Moreover, Isaac means laughter or joy. Abraham begot him only when the bodies of both himself and his wife were already dead, since she had already ceased to have the course of women. This hidden joy of a mind well conscious of itself is not born in us unless the desires of the flesh are mortified by the Spirit.

units.la: Item, Saram matrem ipsam lactasse filium suum: id quod nonnullæ delicatæ ac molles fœminæ non faciunt: contra quas Erasmus multa lib. 2. de Rat. conc. pag. 145. & lib. 4. pag. 440. Sed & propter hoc lactis fontes concessi sunt Sarę, ut partum magis credibilem faciant, & ne quis suppositicium esse putet puerum.
units.tr: Likewise, that Sarah herself nursed her son, which some delicate and soft women do not do: against them Erasmus says much in book 2 of De ratione concionandi, page 145, and book 4, page 440. But also on account of this, the springs of milk were granted to Sarah, so that the birth might be more credible, and lest anyone think the boy was a substitute child.

units.la: Locus hic admonet etiam à sanctis convivia agitata esse, idque cum gratiarum actione, & timore Dei. Ablactato enim Isaaco celebratur festivum & hilare convivium. Quanto hilarius convivium paratur cœlesti familiæ Abrahami in regno Dei ablactato Messia, hoc est, crucis eius cursu peracto, de quo ipse apud Euangelistam: Dico vobis, non bibam posthac ex hoc fructu vitis usque in diem illum, cum bibam vobiscum novum in regno patris mei.
units.tr: This place also reminds us that feasts were held by the saints, and that with thanksgiving and the fear of God. For when Isaac was weaned, a festive and cheerful banquet was celebrated. How much more cheerful a banquet is prepared for the heavenly family of Abraham in the kingdom of God, when the Messiah is weaned, that is, when the course of his cross is finished; of this he himself says to the Evangelist: I tell you, I will not drink again of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.

units.la: 2 Habent autem omnes coniuges exemplum in Abrahamo & Sara hic, quod imitentur. Sancta enim illa mulier noluit ancillam superbam, & arrogantem eius prolem eijcere, marito non consulto & appellato. Rursum Abrahamus rectè monentem uxorem non spreuit, quemadmodum Pontius Pilatus suam, Matthæi 27. Verbum enim Dei, & fides qua illi habuit, omnes in vetere homine affectus, quos habuit erga filium Ismaele, vicit. Quæ victoria nobis ad imitandum proponitur. Ubi enim Dominus quid præcipit, facessant omnes affectiones: quia naturæ Dominus est, qui præcipit. Itaque non fuit inhumanitatis, quòd Abrahamus sic dimisit ancillam, sed obedientiæ diuinæ, in qua verū humanitatis & clementiæ ius cernitur.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, all spouses have in Abraham and Sarah here an example to imitate. For that holy woman was unwilling to cast out the proud maidservant and her arrogant offspring without consulting and appealing to her husband. Again, Abraham did not despise his wife when she gave him good advice, as Pontius Pilate despised his, Matthew 27. For the Word of God and the faith with which he held it conquered all the affections of the old man that he had for his son Ishmael. This victory is set before us for imitation. For where the Lord commands something, all affections must cease, because it is the Lord of nature who commands. Therefore it was not inhumanity that Abraham dismissed the maidservant in this way, but obedience to the divine command, in which the true right of humanity and mercy is seen.

units.la: Cæterum causa eiectionis ancillæ & filij eius, exprimitur his verbis: Cumque vidisset Sara filium Agar Aegyptiæ ludentem, vel, derisorem esse, ut Chaldæus paraphrastes exponit. Quid autem risərit Ismael, vel quid aut quem irriserit, non exprimitur in textu. Munsterus dicit: Cùm esset magnum conuiuium, & omnes congratularentur ipsi Abraham, quòd in senectute Dominus illi dedisset filium, filius ancillæ deridebat & subsannabat illos. Quod Sara aduertens, marito indicauit. Ita sæpe videmus lætitiæ comitem esse tristitiam.
units.tr: Moreover, the cause of the casting out of the maidservant and her son is expressed in these words: When Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian playing, or, being a mocker, as the Chaldee paraphrast explains. But what Ishmael mocked, or what or whom he mocked, is not stated in the text. Munster says: When there was a great feast, and all were congratulating Abraham that the Lord had given him a son in his old age, the son of the maidservant mocked and scoffed at them. Sarah, noticing this, told her husband. So we often see that sadness is the companion of joy.

units.la: Hebræorum quidam referunt, Saram animaduertisse Ismaelem proclivem fuisse ad idololatriam, ad homicidia, & ad scortationē, quòd colligunt ex vi verbi מצחק[?] quòd in textu Hebraico ponitur, eo quòd in quibusdam Scripturæ locis usurpatur, ubi de istis flagitijs sermo est, ut Exodi 32. 2.Regū 2 Genesis 26. Septuaginta interpretes & author vulgatæ æditionis Latinæ, ita transtulerunt hunc locum, quasi Sara viderit Ismaelem ludentum cum Isaaco filio suo. Addiderunt illud de suo, Cum Isaaco filio suo, ad abfoluendam sententiam, quæ aliàs concisa & imperfecta videbatur. Et id quidem non male. omnino enim ex textu apparet, altercationem inter Ismaelem & Isaacum subnatam suisse (quod & Hebraei sentiunt) de hæreditate, quis nam ipsorum potior hæres Abrahami futurus esset: ibique Ismaelem confisum[?] prærogativa primogenituræ, præfe[?] Isaacum contempsisse. Quæ sententia facile stabilitur ex verbis Sarae, dicentis ad Abrahamum: Eijce ancillam istam & filium eius: non enim erit hæres filius istius cum filio meo Isaaco. Atqui hæc erat persecutio, qua Ismael persequebatur Isaacum, de qua Apostolus scribit ad Galatas capite quarto. Unde & Augustin. Tractat. 11.in Ioan. Illa lusio, illusio erat. Illa lusio deceptionem significabat. Persecutionem illa vocat Apostolus, &c. Duplex igitur genus filiorum adumbratur: alterum eorum qui legem perficere tentant, naturæ facultate, non spiritu promissionis fidei Iesu Christi freti. Tales sunt, qui sua iustitia, sua sanctimonia inflati, deridet omnes, qui hoc instituto non sunt: & quia corde impuro sunt, legi divinæ nequaquam satisfacientes, quæ cor mundum, amorem nimirum, quo Deum supra omnia, & alterum ut nos diligamus, requirit, sub lege sunt, id est, sub damnatione legis servi, & cum Ismaele ex Hagare ancilla peccati & mortis mancipia. Alterum autem genus eorum habetur, qui suo præsidio & omni humana ope diffisi, intelligunt se per vim naturæ præstare legem non posse, quòd sub peccatum ad ius mortis venundatos se sciunt, atque ita uno Christo niituntur per fidem, qui ipsorum iustitia, salus & redemptio fit:hi à iure, id est, demnatione legis liberi cum sint, & sub gratia per Christi fidem continentur, liberæ cum Isaaco filij reputantur, & hæredes scripti in domo manet, Ismaele superbo & derisore expulso.
units.tr: Some of the Hebrews report that Sarah noticed Ismael was prone to idolatry, to murder and to fornication. They gather this from the force of the Hebrew word מצחק [mtsachaq], since it is used in certain passages of Scripture where such crimes are the subject, as in Exodus 32, 2 Samuel 2 and Genesis 26. The Septuagint and the author of the Vulgate Latin edition translated the passage as if Sarah had seen Ismael playing with her son Isaac. They added of their own, "with her son Isaac," to complete the sentence, which otherwise seemed broken off and incomplete. And indeed this is not wrong. For it clearly appears from the text that a quarrel arose between Ismael and Isaac (as the Hebrews also think) about the inheritance, namely which of them would be the more important heir of Abraham. In this, Ismael, relying on the privilege of the firstborn, despised Isaac. This view is easily confirmed from the words of Sarah, who says to Abraham: "Cast out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac." Yet this was the persecution by which Ismael pursued Isaac, of which the Apostle writes to the Galatians in chapter four. Whence also Augustine, Tractate 11 on John: "That play was a mockery; that mockery signified deception." The Apostle calls it persecution, etc. Therefore a twofold kind of children is foreshadowed: one of those who try to fulfil the law, relying on the power of nature and not on the Spirit of the promise of faith in Jesus Christ. Such are those who, puffed up with their own righteousness and their own holiness, mock all who are not in this way of life; and because they have an impure heart, by no means satisfying the divine law, which requires a pure heart, that is, love by which God is loved above all things and by which we love one another, they are under the law, that is, under the condemnation of the law, slaves with Ismael, born of the handmaid Hagar, the bondservants of sin and death. The other kind, however, is of those who, distrusting their own protection and every human aid, understand that they cannot fulfil the law by the power of nature, because they know they have been sold under sin into the right of death; and so they rest on Christ alone through faith, who becomes their righteousness, salvation and redemption. These, since they are free from the right, that is, the condemnation of the law, and are held under grace through faith in Christ, are reckoned free like Isaac, the children, and are written as heirs who remain in the house, with the proud and mocking Ismael cast out.

units.la: ¶ Porrò quid amandatæ Agari & filio eius in deserto acciderit, iam sequenter narratur.
units.tr: Next, what happened to Hagar, who had been sent away, and to her son in the desert, is now related in what follows.

units.la: Vbi obseruanda hæc veniunt:
units.tr: Here the following points are to be observed:

units.la: Primo, Deum ubique intueri necessitates afflictorum, & tum maxime adesse, quum omne humanum præsidium deest.
units.tr: First, God looks everywhere upon the needs of the afflicted, and is most present especially when every human help is lacking.

units.la: Secundo, pietatem sic vtilem esse, vt ob eam etiam liberis piorum benefiat, vt Ismaeli propter Abrahamum.
units.tr: Second, piety is so useful that it benefits even the children of the pious for its sake, as Ismael did for Abraham's sake.

units.la: Tertio ignorare nos etiam præsentissima, si ea Deus nobis negare voluerit, & oculos non aperire.
units.tr: Third, we do not know even the most present things if God is willing to deny them to us and does not open our eyes.

units.la: Quarto, liberos in iure parentum esse: & pares cum paribus debere coniungi. Dedit enim Agar filio suo uxorem, de sua gente & stirpe: neque duxit Ismael uxorem inscia aut nolente matre. Parentes enim honorandi sunt iuxta Dei præceptum, cui iure ac merito debetur fidelis obedientia in omnibus.
units.tr: Fourth, children are under the right of their parents, and ought to be joined with equals to equals. For Hagar gave her son a wife of her own people and stock, and Ismael did not take a wife without his mother's knowledge or against her will. For parents are to be honoured according to the precept of God, to whom faithful obedience in all things is due by right and merit.

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.

units.la: CONCIO IX. Genes. 24.
units.tr: SERMON IX. Genesis 24.

units.la: ORrò Abraham senuit, venitq; in dies: & Dominus benedixit Abraham in cunctis. Et dixit Abraham ad seruum suum, seniorem domus suæ: qui præerat omnibus, quæ illius erant: Pone (inquiens) manum tuam subter fœmur meum. Et adiurabo te per Dominum Deum cœli et Deum terræ, ut non accipias uxorem filio meo de filiabus Chanaan, in quorum medio ego habito. Sed ad terram meam & ad patriam meam ibis, & accipies uxorem filio meo Isaac. Dixit vero seruus ille ad eum: Fortasse renuet mulier illa venire post me ad terram istam, & nunquid reducendo reducere debeo filium tuum ad terram unde tu egressus es? Cui respondit Abraham: Caue ne forte reducas filium meum illuc. Dominus Deus cœli, qui tulit me de domo patris mei, & de terra natiuitatis meæ, & qui locutus est ad me, quique iurauit mihi, dicens, Semini tuo dabo terram istam, ipse mittet angelum suum ante te, & accipies, pies inde uxorem filio meo. Quod si noluerit mulier sequi te: innocens eris a iuramento isto meo: tantum filium meum ne reducas illuc. Posuit itaq; seruus manum suam sub fœmore Abraham domini sui, & iurauit illi super hac re. Et accipiens seruus decem camelos ex camelis domini sui, abiit, eratq; omne bonum domini sui in manu sua: & surgens abiit in Mesopotamiam, ad civitatem Nahor. Porro camelos fecit accumbere extra civitatem iuxta fontem aquæ, tempore vespertino, eo tempore, quo egrediuntur (mulieres aquam) haustura. Dixitq;: Domine Deus domini mei Abraham, obsecro fac occurrere mihi hodie, & fac miseri-cordiam cum domino meo Abraham. Ecce ego sto iuxta fontem aquæ, & filiæ hominum civitatis egrediuntur, ut hauriant aquam. Erit itaque, ut puella, ad quam dixero, inclina quaeso hydriam tuam ut bibam: illaq; dixerit, bibe, quin & camelis tuis potum dabo, ea sit quam parasti seruo tuo Isaac: & in hoc sciam quod feceris miseri-cordiam cum domino meo. Factumq; est, priusquam ipse desiit loqui, ecce Rebecca egrediebatur, quæ nata erat Betueli filio Milcha uxoris Nahor fratris Abraham: eratq; hydria sua in humero suo. Erat autem puella illa valde pulchra aspectu, eratq; virgo, quippe quam nullus vir cognouerat: & descendebat ad fontem, impleuitq; hydriam suam & ascendit. Et currens seruus in occursum eius, dixit: Pota me quaso paux-illo aquae de hydria tua. Qua ait: bibe domine: festinansq; deposuit hydriam suam super manum suam[?], & dedit illi bibere. Et ubi desiit potare illum, dixit: gamelis quoq; tuis hauriam, donec cessauerint bibere. Et festinans effudit hydriam suam in canale, currensq; iterum ad puteum, ut hauriret, hausit pro omnibus gamelis illius. Porro vir ille stupefactus est in ea, tacens quidem, ut cognosceret, nū Dominus prosperum fecisset iter suum, an non. Factumq; est, ut cessauerunt gameli bibere, tulit vir ille inaurem aureā, cuius pondus erat dimidium sicli, & duas armillas super manus illius, quarum pondus erat decem aureorum. Dixitq;, cuius filia es? indica quaso mihi: est ne in domo patris tui locus nobis ad pernoctandum? Respondit ei: Filia sum Betuelis fiIis filij Milcha, quæ illum genuit ipsi Nahor. Dixitq; ad eum: Etiam palea & pabulum multum est nobiscum, quin & locus ad pernoctandum. Inclinauit verticem vir ille, & adorauit Dominum. Dixitq;: Benedictus Dominus Deus domini mei Abraham, qui non intermisit misericordiam suam & veritatem suam à domino meo: ego existens in itinere, deduxit me Dominus vsque ad domum fratrum domini mei. Et currens puella, nunciauit domui matris suæ iuxta hæc verba.
units.tr: Abraham was now old and advanced in years, and the Lord blessed Abraham in all things. And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that was his: "Put your hand under my thigh. And I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of Canaan, among whom I dwell. But you shall go to my land and to my country, and take a wife for my son Isaac." But the servant said to him, "Perhaps the woman will not be willing to come after me to this land. Must I then lead your son back to the land from which you came?" Abraham answered him, "Take care that you do not lead my son back there. The Lord God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land,' he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there. But if the woman will not follow you, you will be free from this oath of mine. Only do not lead my son back there." So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord, and swore to him concerning this matter. Then the servant took ten camels from his lord's camels and departed, carrying all the good things of his lord in his hand, and he rose and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor. And he made the camels kneel outside the city by a well of water, at evening time, the time when the women go out to draw water. And he said: "O Lord, God of my master Abraham, I beg you, grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham. Behold, I stand by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water. So let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please lower your pitcher that I may drink,' and who answers, 'Drink, and I will give your camels drink also,' let her be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac; and by this I shall know that you have shown kindness to my master." And it happened, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebecca came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham; and her pitcher was on her shoulder. The young woman was very beautiful in appearance, and she was a virgin, whom no man had known. She went down to the well, filled her pitcher, and came up. And the servant ran to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water to drink from your pitcher." She said, "Drink, my lord"; and she quickly lowered her pitcher onto her hand and gave him a drink. And when she had finished giving him drink, she said, "I will draw for your camels also, until they have finished drinking." And she quickly emptied her pitcher into the trough, ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels. The man was astonished at her, keeping silent, so that he might know whether the Lord had made his journey prosperous or not. And when the camels had finished drinking, the man took a golden ring, whose weight was half a shekel, and two bracelets for her hands, whose weight was ten gold pieces. And he said, "Whose daughter are you? Tell me, please. Is there room in your father's house for us to lodge for the night?" She answered him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, who bore him to Nahor." And she said to him, "We have plenty of straw and fodder with us, and also a place to spend the night." Then the man bowed his head and worshipped the Lord. And he said, "Blessed be the Lord, God of my master Abraham, who has not withdrawn his mercy and his truth from my master; while I was on the journey, the Lord led me to the house of my master's kinsfolk." And the young woman ran and told her mother's household all these words.

units.la: I In hac historia veniunt considerandæ omnes circumstantiæ rerum. Quod enim ipsum factum attinet, contractum est matrimonium inter duos: quòd personas, isteq; sunt Isaac filius Abrahami, & Rebecca filia Betuelis: hæc Christi ecclesiam, ille Christum ipsum præfiguravit: quòd locum, ille in Chanaan, hæc in Mesopotamia habitauit: quòd tempus, Isaacus excesserat iam triginta septem annos, quæ ætas, iudicio etiam eorum, qui qua ætate matrimonia contrahi debeant, docent[?]. apta erat coniugio: quòd auxilia, Deus fuit præparator, angelus eius paranymphus, seruus Abrahami minister: quòd causam, ea fuit propagatio sobolis: quòd formam & modum, is à Mose conscribitur multis verbis.
units.tr: 1. In this history all the circumstances of the matter must be considered. As to the deed itself, a marriage was contracted between two persons: Isaac, son of Abraham, and Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel; the one prefigured Christ, the other the Church of Christ. As to the place: the one dwelt in Canaan, the other in Mesopotamia. As to the time: Isaac had already passed thirty-seven years, an age which, even in the judgement of those who teach at what age marriages ought to be contracted, was suitable for wedlock. As to the helps: God was the one who prepared the way, his angel was the go-between, and Abraham's servant was the minister. As to the cause: it was the propagation of offspring. As to the form and manner: Moses records these at length.

units.la: 2 In descriptione Abrami,& colloquij ipsius cum seruo suo Eleezer, primo confideremus sene-stute[?] & benedictione, quam iuxta veracis Dei promissionem, cui credidit,consecutus est. Dixerat enim Deus: Tu autem abis ad patres tuos in pace,sepultus in senestute bona. Item, Benedicam tibi, erisque benedictus. Deinde curam eius in procurāda uxore filio Isaaco: cui noluit dari in uxorem Chananæam, prophanam, & ad seruitutem in Chamo damnatam: quo facto legi Deuteron.7.praeitum est,& exemplum propositum, in contrahendis matrimonijs delectum esse habendum (quem cum supra cap. 6.Gen.filij Dei negligerent, nubentes in familiam Cainam,diluuio puniti sunt) neque formam, nec generis nobilitatem, nec opes spectandas,sed Dei voluntatem: nec non parentibus in id diligenter incumbendum, ut sui liberi matrimonio iungantur honestorum atque piorum hominum: & rursus liberis praeter voluntatem parentum matrimonia contrahenda non esse. Ut enim in paradiso Euam ipse Deus ad Adamum adduxit: sic vult deinceps parentum consensu ac voluntate desponsationes fieri,ut dicitur Exod.20. Honora patrem, &c. & 1. Corint. 7. Qui elocat,rectè facit. Et Ambrosius hanc Rebeccę historiam enarrans, postulat consensum parentum, & citat ex Andromache Euripidis versiculos:
units.tr: 2. In the account of Abraham and his conversation with his servant Eliezer, we should first consider his old age and the blessing which, according to the promise of the true God, in whom he believed, he obtained. For God had said: "But you shall go to your fathers in peace, buried in a good old age." Likewise: "I will bless you, and you shall be a blessing." Next, consider his care in providing a wife for his son Isaac: he did not wish a Canaanite wife to be given him, a profane woman, condemned to servitude in Ham. In doing this, the law of Deuteronomy 7 was followed and an example set, that in contracting marriages one must choose (as those who, when the sons of God neglected this in Genesis 6, took wives from the family of Cain, were punished by the flood). Neither beauty, nor nobility of birth, nor wealth is to be looked at, but the will of God. Parents must also diligently take care that their children are joined in marriage to honourable and godly people; and, on the other hand, children must not contract marriages against the will of their parents. For just as God himself brought Eve to Adam in paradise, so he wills that betrothals now be made with the consent and will of the parents, as is said in Exodus 20, "Honour your father," etc., and in 1 Corinthians 7, "He who gives her in marriage does well." Ambrose, too, expounding this history of Rebecca, requires the consent of parents, and cites some lines from Euripides' Andromache:

units.la: ψυμφευμάτων μὲν τῶν ἐμῶν πατὴρ ἐμὸς [?] μεσιμνῶν ἐξῆλθ' κ' οὐκ ἐμὸν σκοπεῖν τόδε[?]. hoc est:
units.tr: [ψυμφευμάτων μὲν τῶν ἐμῶν πατὴρ ἐμὸς [?] μεσιμνῶν ἐξῆλθ' κ' οὐκ ἐμὸν σκοπεῖν τόδε[?]] That is: "Concerning my marriages, my father will take care; it is not for me to decide this."

units.la: Sponsalium meorum pater meus Curá habebit, & non est meum statuere hoc.
units.tr: My father will have care of my betrothals, and it is not mine to decide this.

units.la: Et textus in Iure ciuili inqt in Institut. Tit. de Nuptijs: Si filij familiarum sunt, consensum habeant parentum, quorum in potestate sunt. Nam hoc fieri debere, & ciuilis & naturalis ratio suadet, in tantum ut iussus parentum praecedere debeat.
units.tr: And the text of the civil law says in the Institutes, title On Marriages: "If children are under the authority of a father, they should have the consent of the parents in whose power they are. For that this ought to be done, both civil and natural reason persuade, to such an extent that the command of the parents ought to come first."

units.la: Tertiò morem fuisse olim feruis iurantib. (iurare enim non semper malum est, sed peierare) manum sub fœmore ponere, quo ritu se in potestate dominorum esse declarabant. Hoc etiam hodie in quibusdam Orientis partibus utuntur. Ex fœmore item liberi prodeunt, qui iure generationis sub potestate ac imperio parentum fatentur se teneri. Nostri sanctè tradunt, fœmur iurijurando sacratum propter Christum, cui nascendo ex fœmore Abrahami, omnia subijcieda essent, ut Christus ipse de se fatetur, Mihi data est omnis potestas in coelo & in terra. Itaq; propter hunc iussum seruum ponere manum sub (non super) fœmur domini fui Abrahami, quòd Christus esset in lumbis eius ex suturo matrimonio Isaaci & Rebeccæ nascendus. Sic enarrat Hieronymus lib.1.contra Iouinianum: Adiurat seruum in fœmore, hoc est, in Christo, qui de eius femine erat nasciturus.
units.tr: Thirdly, it was once the custom for servants swearing an oath (for to swear is not always evil, but to perjure oneself is) to place their hand under the thigh, and by this rite they declared that they were in the power of their masters. Even today they use this in some parts of the East. Likewise, children who are born from the thigh acknowledge that by the right of generation they are bound under the power and authority of their parents. Our writers rightly teach that the thigh was consecrated by the oath because of Christ, to whom all things were to be made subject by his birth from the thigh of Abraham, as Christ himself confesses of himself: "All power is given to me in heaven and on earth." Therefore, on account of this, the servant was commanded to put his hand under (not over) the thigh of Abraham his lord, because Christ was to be born in his loins from the future marriage of Isaac and Rebecca. So Jerome expounds it in book 1 against Jovinian: "He makes the servant swear on the thigh, that is, on Christ, who was to be born from his seed."

units.la: Quartò consideranda fides Abrahami erga Dei providentiam de paranda uxore. Domus enim (inquit Salomon) & divitiae dantur à parentibus: à domino aut uxor prudes.
units.tr: Fourthly, we should consider Abraham's faith in God's providence concerning the procuring of a wife. For "house and riches are given by parents, but a prudent wife is from the Lord," as Solomon says.

units.la: Quintò ipsa divina providentia per ministerium angelorum in coniugijs sanciendis apparens, Tob 7.
units.tr: Fifthly, divine providence itself, appearing through the ministry of angels in the solemnising of marriages: Tobit 7.

units.la: Sextò fides servi, obedientia, pietas & oratio. Estque hoc consolatione plen[?]simum, quòd pius Abraham ac servus eius auspicem, ꝑ[?] fidemq; nuptiarum constituunt Deum, o[?] antque ut filio Isaac [?]enè prospicere dignetur, atq; fortunare matrimonii. quod tanti fecerunt, & in cons. estu Dei tam honorabile reputarunt, ut crediderint missum iri coelitùs angelum, ad omnia prosperanda co nubij futuri negocia. Quia ergo cura singulari Dei, piorum matrimonia angelorum ministerio (ut contrà impiorum scortationes & adulteria dæmonum consilio ac ope) geruntur: (Tob.6.7.8.) idcirco debent matrimonia piè & sanctè sanciri, atque sancita geri & haberi.
units.tr: Sixthly, the faith, obedience, piety and prayer of the servant. And this is most full of comfort: that pious Abraham and his servant, taking God as the author and guarantor of the marriage, asked that He would deign to look upon his son Isaac and bless the marriage. They held this in such esteem, and judged it so honourable in the sight of God, that they believed an angel would be sent from heaven to prosper all the affairs of the coming wedding. Therefore, since the marriages of the godly are conducted by God's singular care through the ministry of angels (as the fornications and adulteries of the wicked are conducted by the counsel and help of demons): (Tobit 6, 7, 8) for this reason marriages ought to be solemnised piously and holily, and, once solemnised, to be conducted and held so.

units.la: In colloquio servi & Rebeccæ consideraremus non solum pulchritudinem & virginitatem spiritualis Rebeccæ, id est, Ecclesiæ sanctæ: sed etiam charitatem & hospitalitatem, ex qua etiam discipuli Christi cognoscuntur, Ioan.13. item munera sponsalia, quibus nova sponsa[?] ornata fuit. Protulit enim servus Abrahami ornamenta aurium & mannum: quæ ornamenta usurpata à sanctis olim, ornatum commendant, luxum ad ostentationem
units.tr: In the conversation of the servant and Rebekah we should consider not only the beauty and virginity of the spiritual Rebekah, that is, the holy Church, but also her charity and hospitality, by which the disciples of Christ are also known (John 13); likewise the bridal gifts with which the new bride was adorned. For the servant of Abraham brought out ornaments for the ears and hands: ornaments which, once used by the saints, commend adornment, while they condemn luxury and finery prepared for display.

units.la: tationem ta[?]onem paratum damnant. Ut autem seruus ille Rebeccæ inaures aureas, & armillas pondo siclorum decem dedit: sic Apostoli, dispensatores donorum Dei, fidem, quæ ex auditu verbi Dei est, & charita-tem, quæ consistit in seruandis decem præceptis Dei, annunciant. Hanc fidem, quæ fit per charitatem efficax, adaugeat nobis Dominus noster Iesus Christus, Amen.
units.tr: But just as that servant gave Rebekah golden earrings and bracelets weighing ten shekels, so the Apostles, the dispensers of God's gifts, proclaim the faith which comes from hearing the Word of God, and the charity which consists in keeping the ten commandments of God. May our Lord Jesus Christ increase in us this faith, which works through charity. Amen.

units.la: CONCIO X.
units.tr: SERMON X.

units.la: Genes. 24.
units.tr: Genesis 24.

units.la: ABEBAT autem Rebecca fratrem nomine Laban: & is cucurrit ad virum foras, nepe ad fontem. Et factum est, cum vidisset inaurem, & armillas in manibus sororis suæ, & cum audisset verba Rebeccæ sororis suæ dicentis: Sic locutus est ad me vir ille: venit ad virum: & ecce is stabat apud fontem iuxta gamelos. Et dixit: Veni benedicte Domini, cur stas foris? & ego quidem præparaui domum & locum pro gamelis. Intrauit itaque vir ille domum, & soluit gamelos. & dedit (Laban) paleam & pabulum gamelis, atque aquam, ut lauarent pedes suos, & pedes virorum qui cum illo erant. Apposuit quoque corāeo ut comederet: at ille ait: non comedam donec expressero verba mea: qui dixit: loquere. Et ait: Serus sum Abraham. Et quidem Deus benedixit domino meo valde, & magnificatus est, dedit ꝗ illi oues & boues, argentum & aurum, seruos & ancillas, gamelos quoq; & asinos. Sed & Sara vxor domi ni mei peperit filium domino meo, postquam ipsa consenuit: & dedit illi omnia quæ habet. Adiurauitq; me dominus meus dicens: Non accipies vxorem filio meo de filiabus Chananai, in cuius terra ego habito. Sed ad domum patris mei perges, & ad cognationem meam, & accipies vxorem filio meo. Dixitq; ad dominū meum: Fortassis non ibit mulier post me. Et ille respondit mihi: Dominus, in cuius conspectu ambulo, mittet angelum suum tecum, & prosperum faciet iter tuum, ac cipiesq; vxorem filio meo de cognatione mea, & de domo patris mei. Tunc innocens eris à maledictione mea, cùm veneris ad cognationem meam: & si non dederint tibi, eris innocens à maledictione mea. Ego itaque veni hodie ad fontem, & dixi: Domine deus domini mei Abraham, si tu nunc prosperum facis iter meum, in quo ego ambulo. Ecce ego sto iuxta fontem aquae: & erit, ut puella, quae egreditur ad hauriendam aquam, dixeroq; ad eam, da mihi quaso pauxillum aquae de hydria tua ut bibam: Et illa dixerit mihi, & tu bibe, & gamelis tuis hauriam: illa sit mulier, quam praeparauit Dominus filio domini mei. Et ego antequam consummassem loqui in corde meo, ecce Rebecca egrediebatur, & hydria eius in humero eius, descenditq; ad fontem, & hausit aquam, & dixi ad eam: Da mihi quaso bibere. Illa vero festinans depo-suit hydriam suam a se, & dixit: bibe, quin & gamelis tuis potum dabo: & ego bibi: & gamelis quoque ipsa potum tribuit. Interrogans autem eam dixi: cuius filia es tu? quae respondit, filia Betuelis filij Nahor, quam illi peperit Milcha: et posui inaurem super faciem eius, & armillas super manus eius. Incuruatoq; vertice adoraui Dominum, & benedixit Domino Deo domini mei Abraham, qui deduxit me per iter rectum, ut sumerem filiam fratris domini mei filio eius. Et nunc si consentitis facere pietatem & veritatem cum domino meo, indicate: si nolueritis, annunciate mihi, ut vertam me ad dextram vel sinistram. Et respondit Laban atq; Betuel dicentes: à Domino egressum est verbum istud, & idcirco non poterimus loqui ad te vel malum vel bonum. En Rebecca coram te est, accipe & vade, ut sit in uxorem filio domini tui, sicut locutus est Deus. Factum autem est, cum audisset servus Abraham verba illorum, adorauit pronus in terra Dominum. Et protulit servus ille vasa argentea, & vasa aurea, atque vestimenta, & dedit Rebecca: munera quoque obtulit fratri eius atque matri. Et comederunt atque biberunt ipse & viri qui cum ipso erant, & pernoctauerunt: surgentesque mane, dixit ille: dimitte me ad dominum meum. Respondit frater eius atque mater: maneat puella nobiscum per dies saltem decem, & postea ibit. Qui ait illis: Nolite impedire me: en Dominus prosperā fecit viam meam, dimittite igitur me, ut vadam ad dominum meum. Et illi dixerunt: vocabimus puellam, & interrogabimus os eius. Vocauerunt igitur Rebeccam & dixerunt ad eam: vis ire cū viro illo? & respondit, ibo. Dimiserunt itaq atq;[?] Rebeccam sororem suam atq; nutricem eius, & seruum Abraham atq; viros eius. Et benedixerunt Rebeccæ, dixerunt q; ad eã: soror nostra tu es, sis in mille millia, & possideat semen tuum portam inimicorum suorum. Surrexit itaque Rebecca & puella eius, & conscendentes gamelos secutæ sunt virum: & tulit seruus ille Rebeccam, atq; abijt. Et Isahac veniebat ab itinere putei (cuius nomen erat, Viuentis videntis me) habitabat siquidē in terra australi. Et egressus est Isaac ad orandum in campo tempore vespertino: & leuans oculos suos, vidit gamelos venientes. Rebecca quoq; leuauit oculos suos, & viso Isahac lapsa est de gamelo. Et dixit ad seruum: quis est vir ille qui ambulat in campo in occursum nostrum? respondit seruus: ipse est dominus meus. tulit igitur peplū, et operuit se. Et narrauit seruus ipsi Isahac omnes res quas gesserat. Introduxitq; eã Isahac in tabernaculū Sarae matris suae, & accepit Rebeccam, factaq; est ei in uxorē: et dilexit eam, consolationemq; accepit Isahac post matrem suam.
units.tr: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban: and he ran out to the man, namely to the well. And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well. And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels. So the man came into the house, and unloaded the camels. And Laban gave straw and provender to the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who were with him. Meat was set before him to eat; but he said, I will not eat until I have told my errand. He said, Speak on. And he said, I am Abraham's servant. The LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great: he has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, camels and asses. And Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master when she was old, and he has given him all that he has. And my master made me swear, saying: You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell; but you shall go to my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son. And I said to my master, Perhaps the woman will not follow me. And he answered me: The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you and prosper your way, and you shall take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father's house. Then you will be innocent of my curse, when you come to my kindred; and if they do not give her to you, you will be innocent of my curse. So I came today to the well, and said: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if now you prosper the way in which I walk, behold, I stand by the spring of water; and let it be that the maiden who comes out to draw water, and to whom I say, Give me, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher to drink, and she says to me, Drink, and I will draw for your camels also, let her be the woman whom the LORD has prepared for my master's son. And before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder, and went down to the well, and drew water; and I said to her, Give me, I pray, something to drink. And she quickly lowered her pitcher from her shoulder and said, Drink, and I will give your camels drink also; so I drank, and she also gave the camels drink. And I asked her, Whose daughter are you? She answered, The daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him. Then I put the earring on her face, and the bracelets on her hands. And I bowed my head and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, who had led me by the right way to take my master's brother's daughter for his son. Now then, if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me; and if you will not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left. Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said: The thing proceeds from the LORD; we cannot speak to you either bad or good. Behold, Rebekah is before you; take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken. And when Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed down to the earth before the LORD. And the servant brought out silver vessels and gold vessels and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; he also gave gifts to her brother and her mother. And he and the men who were with him ate and drank, and stayed the night; and when they rose in the morning, he said, Send me away to my master. Her brother and her mother answered, Let the girl stay with us at least ten days; after that she shall go. But he said to them, Do not hinder me, for the LORD has prospered my way; send me away, that I may go to my master. And they said, We will call the girl and ask her. So they called Rebekah and said to her, Will you go with this man? And she said, I will go. So they sent away Rebekah their sister, with her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men. And they blessed Rebekah and said to her: You are our sister; may you become thousands of thousands, and may your seed possess the gate of their enemies. So Rebekah arose with her maidservants, and mounting the camels they followed the man; and the servant took Rebekah and went away. Now Isaac was coming from the way of the well (whose name was, The living one who sees me), for he dwelt in the southern land. And Isaac went out to pray in the field at evening; and lifting up his eyes, he saw the camels coming. Rebekah also lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac she slipped down from the camel. And she said to the servant, Who is that man walking in the field to meet us? The servant answered, He is my master. So she took a veil and covered herself. And the servant told Isaac all the things he had done. And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her, and Isaac was comforted after his mother.

units.la: Quemadmodū in Laban hospitalitatis, sic in seruo Abrahami diligētis fidei exemplum habemus. Noluit enim edere, donec heri fui negocium exequutus esset. Repetit autem res gestas inter ipsum & herum suum (quem benedixerat Dominus) item inter se & deum, nec non inter se & puellam Rebeccam, &c. quae omnia ita narrat, ut ostendat rem non humana iudustria, sed prouidentia, voluntate & consilio Dei geri: cui parentes Rebeccæ repugnare noluerunt.
units.tr: As in Laban we have an example of hospitality, so in Abraham's servant we have an example of diligent faith. For he would not eat until he had carried out his business. He recounts the deeds done between himself and his master (whom the Lord had blessed), likewise between himself and God, and also between himself and the girl Rebekah, and so on; all of which he narrates so as to show that the matter was carried out not by human industry but by the providence, will and counsel of God, to which Rebekah's parents were unwilling to object.

units.la: 2 Ex his quatuor discere debemus, quae ad feliciter contrahenda coniugia pertinet.
units.tr: 2 From these four points we ought to learn what pertains to contracting marriages happily.

units.la: Primum non inter pocula (ut hodie non raro fieri solet) sed ante captum cibum & hauftum vinum, de rebus matrimonialibus agi debere. Deinde, primo cognatos & parentes, in quorum potestate sunt liberi, appellandos esse. Tum enim rata sunt matrimonia, si accesserit maiorum consensio. Tertio, sententiae ac voluntati Dei, temere non esse reluctandum, & eos non dirimendos, quos copula coniugali Deus coniunxerit. Nam etsi in parentum potestate posita sunt liberorum matrimonia: tamen illi scire debet, se in Dei iure esse, cui tanquam summo magistratui in curandis matrimonijs pareant. Quarto,non licere ut liberi in matrimonia elocentur, vel inscientes, vel inviti. Ut enim certa est haec sententia ex masculi & foeminae in unam carnem creatione, Quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet: ita verum est, coniunctos non fore, quos Deus amore coniugali non coniunxerit. Unde hoc loco non prius defpondetur Ifaaco Rebecca, quàm cognoscatur de voluntate eius. Sic 1. Reg. 25. Dauid & Abigail in nuptias confentiunt. Idem in hiftoria Tobiæ exponitur.
units.tr: First, that matters of marriage should be discussed not over the cups (as is often done nowadays) but before food is taken and wine drunk. Second, that first the kinsfolk and parents, in whose power the children are, should be addressed; for marriages are then valid when the consent of the elders is added. Third, that one should not rashly resist the judgment and will of God, nor separate those whom the marital bond God has joined together. For although the marriages of children lie in the power of parents, yet the parent ought to know that he is under the right of God, to whom, as supreme magistrate in arranging marriages, he should submit. Fourth, that children may not be given in marriage either without their knowledge or against their will. For just as this teaching is certain from the creation of male and female into one flesh, "What God has joined together, let no man put asunder," so it is true that those will not be united whom God has not joined in conjugal love. Hence in this place Rebekah is not betrothed to Isaac before her will is learned. So in 1. Reg. 25, David and Abigail consent to the nuptials. The same is set out in the history of Tobias.

units.la: Porrò in fponfa & fponfo exemplum habent omnes coniuges. Rebecca enim relinquit domum, parentes, fratres, propinquos, vt viuat cum fponfo fuo. Hæc eft vis vocationis diuinæ, & legis coniugalis ab initio editæ: Quamobrem relinquet homo patrem & matrem, & adhærebit vxori fuæ. Sicut autem Rebecca ex Mofopotamia ad Ifaacum venit in Chanaan: fic ante illum Sara fequuta eft Abraham egredientem ex Vhr Chaldæorum: & cum eo profecta eft in Geraras, Gen. 12. 20. & poft illum Lia & Rachel Iacobum profugū fponte fequutæ funt, Gen. 31.[?] Et Sephora abijt cum Mofe in Aegyptum, Exod. 4. Et cum Tobia fugiente vxor etiam abijt, Tob. 1.[?] Eft enim vxoris fequi maritum.
units.tr: Moreover, all married couples have an example in the bride and bridegroom. Rebecca left her home, her parents, her brothers and her relatives, so that she might live with her husband. This is the force of the divine calling and of the marriage law laid down from the beginning: "Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and cleave to his wife." Just as Rebecca came from Mesopotamia to Isaac in Canaan, so before him Sarah followed Abraham when he went out from Ur of the Chaldeans, and went with him into Gerar (Gen. 12. 20.). After him Leah and Rachel willingly followed Jacob when he fled (Gen. 31.). Zipporah went with Moses into Egypt (Exod. 4.), and when Tobias fled, his wife also went with him (Tob. 1.). For it belongs to a wife to follow her husband.

units.la: Tefcha Dionyfij foror nupta Polyxeno, pofteaquam maritus metu tyranni profugerat, & rex fororem accufaret, quòd confcia fugæ mariti non indicaffet, Adeone, inquit, Dionyfi me evilem abieftiq; animi fœminam iudicas, vt fi fenfiffem illum moliri fugam, non me illi nauigationis & omnium fortunarum comitem additura fuerim? Item Rebecca vifo Ifaaco, defcendit de gamelo, reuerentiæ & honoris gratia, & operuit fe velamine, quod verecundiæ ac pudoris in noua fponfa, & futuræ erga maritum obedientiæ significationem habuit. Notum est enim quod Apostolus 1. Corinth.11. de muliebri velamine meminit.
units.tr: Tesca, the sister of Dionysius, was married to Polyxenus. After her husband had fled for fear of the tyrant, the king accused her of not reporting her husband's flight although she knew of it. "Do you judge me," she said, "to be so base and spiritless a woman that, if I had known he was planning to flee, I would not have added myself as his companion in the voyage and in all his fortunes?" Likewise Rebecca, when she saw Isaac, got down from the camel out of reverence and honour, and covered herself with a veil, which signified the modesty and shame of a new bride and her future obedience to her husband. For it is well known that the Apostle, in 1 Corinthians 11, speaks of the woman's veil.

units.la: Ifaacus autem sub vesperam meditandi, & orandi gratia deambulans secus puteum, vidit suam sponsam. Verisimile est eum precatum esse, primùm, ut contingeret illa, quae sibi a Deo promissa esset: deinde, ut suum matrimonium sibi commodum & Deo gloriosum redderetur: demùm, ut liberis in aedificationem familiae & in ecclesiae corporis Mef-fiae extructionem augeretur ad implendum promissum illud: Et ex illa dabo tibi filium, cui benedicturus sum, erisque in nationes, & reges populorum orientur ex eo.
units.tr: Isaac, however, toward evening was walking beside the well for the sake of meditation and prayer, and he saw his bride. It is likely that he prayed, first, that she might be the one promised to him by God; then, that his marriage might be made useful to himself and glorious to God; and finally, that by children it might be increased for the building up of his household and for the building of the body of the Church of the Messiah, in fulfilment of that promise: "And from her I will give you a son, whom I will bless, and he shall be a father of nations, and kings of peoples shall come from him."

units.la: Item Ifaacus, ut historia testatur, uxorem suam dilexit, consolationemq; accepit post matrem suam, cuius obitum pro pietate sua tres annos luxerat .i. temperauit dolorem, quem acceperat de morte matris suae. Debent igitur omnes mariti suas uxores diligere, quemadmodum & Christus Ecclesiam, Eph. 5. idque amore gratuito, recto, discreto, vehementi, fructuoso, perseveranti.
units.tr: Likewise Isaac, as the history testifies, loved his wife, and he found comfort after his mother, whose death he had mourned for three years out of devotion, that is, he moderated the grief he had felt at his mother's death. Therefore all husbands ought to love their wives, just as Christ also loved the Church (Eph. 5.), and to love them with a love that is free, upright, discreet, ardent, fruitful and enduring.

units.la: 4 Vidisti, inquit D. Chryfoftomus, quomodo folebant olim filijs suis uxores ducere? Quomodo magis[?] animae generositatem, quàm opum abundantiam inquirebant? nusquam instrumenta, nusquam pacta & alia ridicula, quae nunc apud nos fiunt, & verba illa quae in literis continentur: Si absque liberis, inquit, moritur, si hoc & hoc contingat. verùm apud illos nihil tale, sed maximæ & se curisimæ literæ erant virginis mores: nusquam cymbala & choreæ. Er iterum, hic considera oro, inquit, quomodo nusquam superflua illa & inutilia, nusquam diabolica pompa, nusquam cymbala, & titiæ[?], & choreæ, & satanica illa conuiuia, & fcommata omni obfcoenitate plena: sed omnis honestas, omnis sapientia, omnis mititas.
