Hence it is that Abraham and Isaac asked their wives to say that they were their sisters, lest they themselves be killed on account of them (Gen. 12, 20, 26).

units.la: Tertiò credidit & apud fe cogitauit, fi dormires cum vxore domini, peccares etiam in Deum,qui te tot beneficiis ornauit, & iustus vindex est scelerum,quem nemo sua crimina celauerit,cuius oculi cuncta vident. Qui enim adulter est, variis & multis modis in ipfum Dominum Deum suum peccat,Genef.20. Contemnit enim verbum Dei,tranfgreditur legem Dei, Exqd. 20. Deut. 5. facit nomen Dei blasphemari ab inimicis eius, 2. Reg. 12. Amos 2. Rom. 2. prophanat templū Dei,ex membro Christi Domini membrum scorti facit, in ius redemptoris fui Christi peccat,1.Cor.6.ordinem non Benedicti,non Augustini, sed Dei, id est,fontem & radicem generis nostri, matrimonium scilicet contaminat: pallium matris Domini inquinat, sub quo occultat est cœlestis partus: delectatio nem vilium & turpium membrorum, delitiis, quæ in Deo sunt, præponit: angelos Dei tristitia afficit: hostes Dei, id est, dæmones ex hilarat, quia vident in adulterio hominis & animam, & corpus maculari.
units.tr: Third, he believed and reflected within himself that if you lay with your master's wife you would also sin against God, who has adorned you with so many benefits, and who is a just avenger of crimes, whom no one can hide his sins from, whose eyes see all things. For he who is an adulterer sins against the Lord his God in various and many ways (Gen. 20). For he despises the word of God, transgresses the law of God (Exod. 20; Deut. 5), causes the name of God to be blasphemed by his enemies (2 Sam. 12; Amos 2; Rom. 2), profanes the temple of God, makes a member of Christ the member of a harlot, sins against the right of his Redeemer Christ (1 Cor. 6), and defiles not the order of St Benedict or of St Augustine but the order of God, that is, the fountain and root of our kind, namely marriage; he soils the mantle of the mother of the Lord, under which the heavenly offspring was hidden; he prefers the delight of vile and shameful members to the delights that are in God; he saddens the angels of God; and he gladdens God's enemies, that is, the demons, because they see both soul and body of a man being stained in adultery.

units.la: Quarto Iofeph non ebrietati, sed fobrietati studuit. Nunquam enim ebrium putabo castum, inquit Hieronymus. Item alius:
units.tr: Fourth, Joseph devoted himself to sobriety, not drunkenness. For I will never think a drunkard chaste, says Jerome. Likewise another writer:

units.la: Et Venus in vinis, ignū in igne furit.
units.tr: And Venus rages in wine, as fire rages in fire.

units.la: Iofeph igitur non cognouit cum domino suo quicquam nisi panem, quem ipse comedebat, hoc est, sicut Rabi Abraham Sephardi exponit, Iofeph nihil ex cibis domini fui cognouit, præter panem siccum quo vescebatur, & tamen habuit vultum elegantem: sicut & Daniel abstinens à regis cibis, vescebatur leguminibus, & interim erat corpulentior & pulchrior iliis, qui regijs nutriebantur cibis. Vel, sicut alius ex doctioribus Hebræorum explicat: omnia curabat præter cibum domini fui, quod alijs cibis vteretur Iofeph, alijs dominus eius. panis enim pro omni ciborum genere, apud Hebræos frequenter capitur.
units.tr: Joseph therefore knew nothing with his master except the bread which he himself ate; that is, as Rabbi Abraham Sephardi explains it, Joseph knew nothing of his master's food except the dry bread on which he fed, and yet he had a handsome face. So also Daniel, abstaining from the king's food, fed on pulse, and meanwhile was fatter and better looking than those who were nourished on the royal food. Or, as another of the more learned Hebrews explains it: Joseph took care of everything except his master's food, since Joseph used other foods and his master used others. For among the Hebrews "bread" is often taken to stand for every kind of food.

units.la: Quinto, non solum verbis adulteræ obedire recusauit, sed etiam eius cosuetudinem declinauit: tantum abfuit, vt oculos suos in ipsam conuerterit. In [?] continentiæ enim præparatione aureum illud os, Ioannes Chrysostomus dicit, victoriam concedi, non ex virginum (aut mulierum) consuetudine, sed secessu. Cum aliis vitiis, inquit D. Ambrosius, potest expectari conflictus: exhortationem autem fugite, ne approximetis, quia non potest aliter melius vinci.
units.tr: Fifth, he not only refused to obey the adulterous woman's words, but also avoided her company; so far was he from turning his eyes upon her. For in preparing for continence, that golden-mouthed John Chrysostom says, victory is won not by the company of virgins (or of women), but by withdrawal. Against other vices, says St Ambrose, a struggle may be awaited; but flee the occasion, lest you come near, because it cannot otherwise be overcome more easily.

units.la: Sexto, Ioseph fugit ocium, & officium ac opus suum diligenter fecit. Poeta enim inquit: Ocia si tollas, perire Cupidinis arcus.
units.tr: Sixth, Joseph shunned idleness, and carried out his duty and work diligently. For the poet says: If you take away idleness, the bow of Cupid perishes.

units.la: Item: Quaeritur Ægistus quare sit factus adulter? In promptu causa est, desidiosus erat.
units.tr: Likewise: Why did Aegisthus become an adulterer? The cause is at hand: he was idle.

units.la: Postremo, Ioseph absque dubio serio invocavit Dominum pro dono continentiae & castitatis, quod ipse solus dat, Sapien.8.Iacob.1.Sirac.23. & pro Spiritu sancto, qui ipsi adfuit in his tentationibus, & consolatus est eum etiam in carcere & in omni afflictione. Hic Deus consolationis adsit nobis omnibus in universis nostris tentationibus & tribulationibus, per Christum Iesum Dominum nostrum, Amen.
units.tr: Lastly, Joseph without doubt earnestly called upon the Lord for the gift of continence and chastity, which he alone gives (Wisdom 8; James 1; Ecclesiasticus 23), and for the Holy Spirit, who was present with him in these temptations and comforted him even in prison and in every affliction. May the God of all comfort be with us all in all our temptations and tribulations, through Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XVI
units.tr: CONCIO XVI

units.la: Exod. 2.
units.tr: Exod. 2.

units.la: Taudiens Pharao sermonem istum, quaerebat occidere Mosen: & fugiens Moses à facie Pharaonis, mansit in terra Midian, seditq; iuxta puteum. Erant autem sacerdotis Midian septem filiae, quae venerunt & hauserunt, impleveruntq; canales, ut potarent oves patris sui. Et venerunt pastores atque repulerunt eas: & consurgens Moses, auxiliatus est eis, potauitq; oves illarum. Quae venientes ad Rehuel patrem suum, dixit ille: Quare hodie tam festinanter redijstis? Responderunt: Vir Aegyptius liberavit nos de manu pastorum, nam hauriendo hausit nobis, atque potum praebuit ovibus. Qui dixit ad filias suas, & ubi est ille? quare sic dereliquistis virum illum? vocate eum, ut comedat panem. Et conscensit Moses habitare cum viro illo: dedit{que} ille Ziporam filiam suam Mosi. Quae cum peperisset filium, vocavit ille nomen eius Gerson. dixit enim: peregrinus fui in terra aliena.
units.tr: When Pharaoh heard this word, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, who came and drew water and filled the troughs, that they might water the flock of their father. And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses rose up, helped them, and watered their flock. When they came to Reuel their father, he said: "Why have you come back so quickly today?" They answered: "An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds; he drew water for us and gave the flock to drink." He said to his daughters: "And where is he? Why have you left the man behind? Call him, that he may eat bread." And Moses agreed to dwell with that man, and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses. When she had borne a son, he named him Gershom, for he said: "I have been a stranger in a foreign land."

units.la: Trium personarum potissimè fit mentio in his verbis: nimirum Mosis, Rehuelis, Ziporae: hoc est, generi, soceri, uxoris.
units.tr: In these words three persons are especially mentioned, namely Moses, Reuel, and Zipporah: that is, the son-in-law, the father-in-law, and the wife.

units.la: 1 Fuga Mosis (quem Pharao quaerebat occidere, ex tyrannide, quae sibi metuens fortes viros nequaquam tolerat) non turpiter sibi metuentis erat: sed prudenter sibi & gentis suae saluti consulentis, expectantisque occasionem[?] confirmandi ad Israelitas liberados, muneris. Sic Iacob fugit Esaum, Dauid Saulum, Paulus ex Damasco aduersarios suos, Christus ipse Iudaeos. Non enim tentandus est Deus, sed in tempore potentium tyrannorum furor declinandus, iuxta illud Matt.10. Cum persecuti vos fuerint in ciuitate hac, sugite in aliam.
units.tr: 1 Moses' flight (from Pharaoh, who sought to kill him, out of the tyranny that cannot tolerate brave men who fear for their own position) was not a shameful fleeing from one who feared; rather it was the prudent act of one who consulted his own safety and that of his people, and who waited for an opportunity of the task of freeing the Israelites. So Jacob fled from Esau, David from Saul, Paul from his adversaries at Damascus, and Christ himself from the Jews. For God is not to be tempted, but the fury of powerful tyrants is to be avoided in its time, according to that saying of Matthew 10: "When they persecute you in this city, flee into another."

units.la: Neque hoc praetereundum est, quod Moses, qui populum liberaturus erat, fugere cogitur, ut in omnibus diuinam prouidentiam discamus agnoscere. Nam quid magis alienum[?] quid magis impossibile humanae rationi videri potuit, quàm hominem fugitiuum captiui populi liberatorem fore[?] At hunc ducem & imperatorem Deus populo suo facit, ut omnem humanam sapientiam pudefaciat.
units.tr: Nor should this be passed over: that Moses, who was about to free the people, is forced to flee, so that in all things we may learn to recognize divine providence. For what could seem more alien or more impossible to human reason than that a fugitive should become the liberator of a captive people? Yet God makes this man the leader and commander of his people, so that he may put all human wisdom to shame.

units.la: Moses suam futuram coniugem inuenit apud puteum. Sic Rebecca, sic Rahel inuentae sunt ad puteum: ita Christus Samaritanā apud fontem reperit. Sanctorum enim nuptiae, quae sunt coniunctio animae cum verbo Dei, aliter fieri non possunt, nisi per instructionem diuinorum librorum, qui figuraliter putei appellantur: de quibus Ioan. 5. Scrutamini scripturas, &c. Sed & ecclesia Christo in lauacro aquae coniungitur.
units.tr: Moses found his future wife at the well. So Rebekah and Rachel were found at a well; so Christ found the Samaritan woman at the fountain. For the marriages of the saints, which are the joining of the soul with the Word of God, cannot take place otherwise than through the instruction of the divine books, which are figuratively called wells: concerning which John 5: "Search the Scriptures," etc. But also the Church is joined to Christ in the washing of water.

units.la: Moses à puellis (infirmiores enim semper in mundo opprimuntur) violentiam (quam odio habuit) depellit, in quo eius magnanimitas & virtus notatur. Sic etiam supra depellendo oppressionem à fratribus, futuri malorum vindicis specimen dedit.
units.tr: Moses, when the girls (for the weaker are always oppressed in the world) were subjected to violence, drove it off, which he hated; in this his magnanimity and virtue are noted. So too, earlier, by driving off the oppression by his brothers, he gave a sample of the future avenger of evils.

units.la: Moses consensit & coepit habitare cum facerdote in Midian: cuius filiam non antè accepit, quàm pater dederit. Hæc peperit ei filium (in hunc enim præcipuè finem ineundum est matrimonium) & vocauit eum Gerfom. Deus enim suos nec in exilio deserit. Sunt autem huiusmodi apud Hebræos nomina ab euentu munerū Dei imposita, quibus pij sese ad gratitudinem & laudem Dei excitare voluerint: vt quandocunque liberos aspicerent aut nominarent, diuinorum beneficiorū memoria refricaretur illis. Absurdum ergo est (vt inquit Zuinglius) quod Christiani liberis suis non solum peregrina nomina, sed gentilia etiam asciscunt, quorū significationes non intelligunt. Græci cum vetere interprete addunt de altero filio, quē Zipora peperit Mosi, & vocauit Eliezer, ab auxilio Dei. Aduenæ enim sunt sancti super terrā: sed Dei adiutorio nunquā carent.
units.tr: Moses agreed and began to dwell with the priest in Midian; he did not take the daughter before the father gave her. She bore him a son (for marriage is entered into chiefly for this end), and he called him Gershom. For God does not forsake his own even in exile. Now names of this kind among the Hebrews were imposed from the outcome of God's gifts, by which the pious wished to stir themselves to gratitude and praise of God: so that whenever they looked upon or named their children, the memory of the divine benefits would be refreshed in them. It is absurd, therefore (as Zwingli says), that Christians give their children not only foreign names but even heathen ones, whose meanings they do not understand. The Greeks, with the old translator, add concerning the other son whom Zipporah bore to Moses, whom she called Eliezer, from the help of God. For the sojourners upon the earth are holy, but they never lack God's help.

units.la: 2 Rehuel pater filiarum Iithro soceri Mofis vocatur, cùm alius earum fuerit, vt quidā putant: sed fieri potest, vt socer Mosis ambobus nominibus appellatus fuerit, Exod. 18. Is fuit sacerdos (iuxta alios, princeps) Madianitarum. Nam & apud gentes numinis religio fuit, cognitioque Dei, licet non tam clara. vocantur autem magistratus & principes [?]כהנים sacerdotes etiā in scripturis, eo quòd olim vtrunque officium, & sacerdotale & politicum politicum penes illos erat, etiam apud ethnicos: & quod magistratus inprimis cultum Dei,& quae ad gloriam illius faciunt, promouere debet. Ob hoc enim maxime minister Dei vocatur,Rom. 13. Hic septem habuit filias. Lex enim antiqua & gentibus & Hebraeis est,sacerdotibus licere uxores habere. Nam honorabile est inter omnes coniugiū, Heb.13. Etsi antichristus instinctu Satanæ diuersum sentit, 1. Timoth.4.
units.tr: 2 Reuel is called the father of the daughters, and the father-in-law of Moses is called Jethro, although, as some think, there was another of them; but it may be that Moses' father-in-law was called by both names, Exod. 18. He was the priest (according to others, the prince) of the Midianites. For even among the nations there was a religion of the divine power and a knowledge of God, though not so clear. Moreover, magistrates and princes are called priests [כהנים] even in the Scriptures, because formerly both offices, the priestly and the political, were held by them, even among the heathen; and because the magistrate above all must promote the worship of God and whatever serves his glory. For this reason especially he is called the minister of God, Rom. 13. He had seven daughters. For the ancient law, both for the Gentiles and the Hebrews, allows priests to have wives. For marriage is honourable among all, Heb. 13. Although the Antichrist, by the instigation of Satan, thinks otherwise, 1 Tim. 4.

units.la: Hic causam quaesiuit a filiabus, cur solito citius domum venirent: Ergo multo magis quaerendum quando tardius veniunt.
units.tr: Here he asked his daughters why they came home sooner than usual. Therefore much more should we inquire when they come home later.

units.la: Hic gratus fuit erga beneficum. Sacerdotes enim & suam familiam decet hospitalitas & beneficentia, & ut nullius operam gratis accipiant, sed liberales sint & benefici,etiam ignotis: maxime autem peregrinis, & his praecipuè, quos impigros ac ad labores honestos, alacres conspicimus, non passim ociosè circumuagantibus.
units.tr: Here he was grateful toward his benefactor. For hospitality and beneficence befit priests and their household, and that they accept the labour of no one for nothing, but be generous and kind, even to strangers; especially to foreigners, and above all to those whom we see to be diligent, eager for honest labours, and not idly wandering about everywhere.

units.la: Hic denique pio & prudenti dedit filiam suam, iuxta consilium Sapientis, Sirac.7.
units.tr: Finally, here he gave his daughter to a pious and prudent man, in accordance with the counsel of the Wise Man, Sirach 7.

units.la: 3 Zipora fuit una ex filiabus sacerdotis in Midian regione versus Arabiam spectante: quae non degebant in otio. & saepe a pastoribus depulsæ, non tamen cessarunt ab officio, adaquandi greges patris sui. Cur ergo viri foeminis ignauiores sumus? cur cessamus? putamus ne sic iustitiam ac veritatem coli ac instaurari posse, ut nemo reclamet, nemo resistat pessimis conatibus? Eædem filiæ interrogatæ à patre veritatē dixerunt: nec aufuetæ erant domum ducere (vt hodie nonnullę solent, inuitis & infciis parentibus) viros ignotos & alienos: neqʒ id eas decebat. Ipsæ denique non nupserūt, priusquam pater illas elocauit nuptum. Vt & nos patris nostri cœlestis voluntatem in omnibus faciamus, adiuuet nos Dominus noster & saluator Iesus Christus, Amen.
units.tr: 3 Zipporah was one of the daughters of the priest in the region of Midian facing toward Arabia; they did not live in idleness, and though often driven away by the shepherds, they did not cease from their task of watering their father's flocks. Why then are we men more idle than women? Why do we give up? Do we think that justice and truth can be cultivated and restored in such a way that no one protests and no one resists the worst attempts? These same daughters, when asked by their father, told the truth: nor were they accustomed to bring home (as some women do today, against the will and without the knowledge of their parents) men who were unknown and strangers; nor would that have become them. Finally, they did not marry before their father gave them in marriage. So that we too may do the will of our heavenly Father in all things, may our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ help us, Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XVII. Deuter. 22.
units.tr: SERMON XVII. Deut. 22.

units.la: I quispiam duxerit vxorem, accesseritqꝫ ad eam, & odio cœperit eam habere. Et imposuerit ei data opera verba (mala) protuleritqꝫ contra eam nomen malum, vt si dicat: Cum duxissem mulierem illam, & ingressus essem ad eam, non inueni in ea signa virginitatis. Tollent pater puellæ atque mater eius, & proserent signa virginitatis puellæ ad seniores ciuitatis, qui sunt in porta. Dicetqꝫ pater puellæ ad seniores: Hanc filiam meam dedi viro illi in vxorem, cœpitqꝫ eam odio habere. Et ecce ipse imponit (ei) sigmenta verborum, dicens: non inueni in filia tua virginitatem: hæc vero sunt si-gna gna virginitatis filiæ meæ:& expandent vestimentum coram senioribus civitatis. Tollentq; seniores civitatis illius virum illum,& plagis castigabunt eum: condenabuntque eum centum siclis, quos dabunt patri puellæ, eo quod produxit nomen malum contra virginem Israel,habebitq; eam in uxorem,nec poterit dimittere eam cunctis diebus suis. Quod si verum est verbum illud, Et non inventa fuerint signa virginitatis in puella: ducent puellam ad ostium domus patris sui, obruentq; eam viri civitatis illius lapidibus, ut moriatur:quia fecit nefas in Israel,fornicando in domo patris sui,removebisq; malum de medio tui.
units.tr: If any man takes a wife, goes in to her, and then begins to hate her, and he invents charges against her and brings up an evil name against her, saying, "I took this woman, and when I went in to her I did not find in her the signs of virginity," then the father of the girl and her mother shall take and bring forth the signs of the girl's virginity to the elders of the city who sit in the gate. And the girl's father shall say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has begun to hate her. And see, he now brings charges against her, saying, 'I did not find virginity in your daughter'; but these are the signs of my daughter's virginity." And they shall spread out the cloth before the elders of the city. Then the elders of that city shall take the man and beat him, and they shall fine him one hundred shekels of silver, which they shall give to the girl's father, because he has brought an evil name upon a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife, and he may not put her away as long as he lives. But if the charge is true, and the signs of virginity are not found in the girl, then they shall bring the girl out to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has done a shameful thing in Israel by playing the harlot in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

units.la: Hæc lex de uxore non inventa virgine à marito,& ab ipso vel verè, vel odio diffa-mata, depingit nobis malitiam quorundam virorum, & nonnullarum mulierum: ostendit quæ quantum crimen sit calumnia, & quanta stultitia & iniquitas fornicatio. Potissimè autem videtur hæc lex data adversus eos,qui post primum aut aliquot congressus cupiebant ab uxoribus divertere, quòd suam libidinem explesent.
units.tr: This law concerning a wife who is not found to be a virgin by her husband, and whom he defames either truthfully or out of hatred, portrays for us the malice of certain men and of some women. It shows how great a crime slander is, and how great the folly and wickedness of fornication. This law seems to have been given especially against those who, after the first or a few embraces, wanted to put away their wives so that they might indulge their lust.

units.la: 1 Malitia virorum in eo cernitur,quòd odio habent suam carnem, quod odium plerunque ex insano amore, qui præcesserit, oritur: vt in Ammon filio Dauidis cernere licet, 2. Reg. 13. porrò excidio, id est, interno homicidio, quod cordis est, nascitur calumnia, quæ fit ore: tandem ut[?] Dominus prohibeat, vt accidit in negotio Sufannæ, homicidium externum. Talis calumniator non fuit Ioseph Mariæ maritus, Matth. 1.
units.tr: The malice of men is seen in this: they hate their own flesh, and that hatred usually arises from the wild love that came before it, as can be seen in Ammon, son of David (2 Sam. 13). Then from this inner ruin, which is an inward murder of the heart, comes slander, which is uttered by the mouth; and finally, which the Lord forbid, as happened in the affair of Susanna, an outward murder. Joseph, the husband of Mary, was not such a slanderer (Matt. 1).

units.la: Ex poena calumniatoris intelligitur, quàm graue peccatum sit calumnia. Hæc enim fuit tripartita. Vna, verberatio, constans 39. plagis, Deut. 25. altera pecuniaria: mulctabatur enim 100. siclis argenti, id est, 25. aureis, dandis patri puellæ: quia liberorum dedecus in parentes recidit, quibus liberi honesti honori sunt, inhonesti dedecori. Tandem eam uxorem retinere cogebatur, quam exosus fuerat & diffamauerat: quod erat valde acerbum. Sed iusta poena fuit: quia istiusmodi diffamator & detractor peccat in præceptum, Falsum testimonium ne dici o.[?] Unde Salomon Prouerb. 19. Testis falsus non erit impunitus: & qui mendacia loquitur, non effugiet. Nam falsidicus testis præsentiam Dei contemnit: iudicem mentiendo fallit: in nocentem falso testimonio lædit: imò diabolo filium se esse ostendit.
units.tr: The punishment of the slanderer shows how grave a sin slander is. The punishment was threefold. First, a beating of thirty-nine stripes (Deut. 25). Second, a fine: he was made to pay one hundred shekels of silver, that is, twenty-five gold pieces, to be given to the girl's father, because the disgrace of children falls back upon their parents, to whom children are an honour when they are honourable and a disgrace when they are dishonourable. Third, he was compelled to keep as his wife the woman he had hated and defamed, which was very bitter. Yet the punishment was just, because such a defamer and detractor sins against the commandment, "You shall not bear false witness." Hence Solomon says (Prov. 19): "A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who tells lies will not escape." For the false witness despises the presence of God, deceives the judge by lying, harms the innocent by his false testimony, and indeed shows himself to be a son of the devil.

units.la: 2 Prauitas mulierum seu puellarum quarundam in eo consistit, quod vel post, vel ante sponsalia occultè & sponte fornicantur, & futuros maritos fallunt, domosque parentum suorum dehonestant.
units.tr: The wickedness of certain women or girls consists in this: either after or before betrothal they secretly and willingly fornicate, deceive their future husbands, and dishonour the houses of their parents.

units.la: Supplicium meretricum satis declarat, quanquantum nefas sit scortari, praesertim in populo Dei: in quo ne nominari quidem, nedum grassari deberet tantum peccatum, Ephes. 5. Deut. 23. Vxor enim non inuenta virgo, pro qua fe marito venditauit, lapidibus obruitur. Ad fores autem paternae domus ducenda esse meretricem lex iubet, & ibi necandam: ut tam graui supplico admoniti parentes liberos suos maiore cura, ne talem fer re cogantur confusionem, ad honestatem educare studerent, vt Sapiens monet Eccl. 7. 26.42. & hoc exemplo commotae caeterae pudicitiam suam diligentius tuerentur. Caeterum de eiusmodi casu nuptiali Iuo Epift. 69. ad Rudol. Remenfem archiep. sic scribit, quemadmodum refertur in Eccles. cent. II. cap. 4. Quæsiuit à me vestra prudentia, utrum mulier, quae post completa sacramenta & officia nuptiarum, infra duos aut tres menses peperisse cognoscitur, debeat ꝓpter foedera nuptiarum in coniugio manere, aut propter patratum ante nuptias flagitiu matrimonij dignitatem amittere, cum lex Moysi iubeat huiusmodi lapidari. Super qua re non memini me invenisse Canonicâ sententiam. Dico tamen sine ꝑjudicio sententiae melioris: quia si ante celebrationem sacramenti coniugalis cognita fuisset turpitudo mulieris, secundum severitatem legu, non effet honestanda matrimonio: sed asperis obiurgationibus, tanquam lapidum jactib. severa esset adhibenda correctio. Verùm postquam simpliciter praecedente consensu contracta sunt foedera nuptiarum, postquam matrimoniales tabulae datae sunt, & caetera coniugij sacramenta completa sunt, vir & mulier vnum corpus per coniunctionem carnis facti sunt: non intelligo posse dissolui coniugium, nisi diuortij causa intercurrat adulterium: quamuis ex adulterio, docente Euangelio, possit marito mulier reconciliari: quanto magis simplici fornicatione, quae patrata est, quando nondum alligata est lege matrimoniali, &c. Huius sententiae videtur subscribere Lombardus lib.4.dist.30. vbi ait, Error fortunæ coniugij onfenfum non excludit: nec error qualitatis, vt si quis ducat vxorem in retricem[?] vel corruptam, quam putat esse c stam[?] vel virginem, non potest eam dimittere.
units.tr: The punishment of harlots sufficiently shows how great a crime it is to play the whore, especially among the people of God, among whom so great a sin ought not even to be named, much less to be rampant (Eph. 5; Deut. 23). A wife who is not found to be a virgin, although she sold herself to her husband as one, is stoned to death. The law orders that the harlot be brought to the door of her father's house and killed there, so that parents, warned by so severe a punishment, might take greater care to bring up their children in honour, lest they be forced to bear such shame, as the Wise Man admonishes (Eccl. 7; 26, 42), and so that other women, moved by this example, might guard their chastity more diligently. Concerning such a marriage case, Ivo, in his Letter 69 to Rudolf, archbishop of Reims, writes as follows (as it is cited in the Ecclesiastical Centuries, II, ch. 4): "Your prudence has asked me whether a woman who, after the sacraments and rites of marriage have been completed, is found to have given birth within two or three months, ought to remain in the marriage because of the bonds of wedlock, or whether, because of the shameful deed committed before marriage, she loses the dignity of matrimony, since the law of Moses orders such women to be stoned. I do not recall having found a canonical judgment on this matter. Nevertheless I say this, without prejudice to a better opinion: if the baseness of the woman had been known before the celebration of the marriage sacrament, then according to the severity of the laws she should not have been honoured with marriage, but severe correction should have been applied with harsh rebukes, like a shower of stones. But since the covenants of marriage were contracted simply with prior consent, since the marriage documents have been given and the other sacraments of marriage completed, the man and the woman have become one body through the union of the flesh. I do not see how the marriage can be dissolved, unless adultery intervenes as the cause of divorce. Although, as the Gospel teaches, a woman can be reconciled to her husband after adultery, how much more so after simple fornication, which was committed when she was not yet bound by the law of marriage, and so on." Lombard, Book 4, distinction 30, seems to agree with this opinion, where he says: "An error about the person one marries does not exclude consent, nor does an error about quality; so that if someone takes as his wife a harlot or a corrupted woman whom he thinks to be chaste or a virgin, he cannot put her away."

units.la: 3 Ex contrario iam intelligitur, quid probos viros deceat, & honestas puellas. Illi enim diligere debent suas vxores, & non repudiare: studere veritati, & non mendacio. Hæ vero scortationem fugere, virginitatem suam vsque ad nuptias seruare: id quòd & iuuenes facere debent: quemadmodum D, Augustinus monet, in Ser. 244. de Temp.
units.tr: From the opposite side it is now clear what befits upright men and honest girls. For men ought to love their wives and not repudiate them, to pursue the truth and not lies. Women ought to flee fornication and keep their virginity until marriage, which young men too ought to do, as Augustine admonishes (Sermon 244, On the Times).

units.la: Nam si ante legitimam coniunctionem per adulterium corrupti fuerint, ad nuptias corpore quidem viui veniunt, sed in anima mortui: comprobantur: quia scriptum est, Anima quae peccauerit, ipsa morietur. Chrysostomus Hom. 9. in ep. ad Tim. 1. dicit: Idcirco quippe coronæ imponuntur capiti, vt victoriæ signa sint, quòd scilicet antea libidini impenetrabiles, ita demùm cubiculum ingrediantur, quia scilicet à voluptate superati nō sunt. Quòd si libidine superatus quispiam seipsum scortis addixerit: citius[?] iam rei gratia coronatus incedat, qui tam fœdæ libidini colla subdiderit?
units.tr: For if they have been corrupted by adultery before lawful union, they come to the wedding indeed alive in body, but dead in soul, because it is written: "The soul that sins, it shall die." Chrysostom, Homily 9 on 1 Timothy, says: "Crowns are placed upon the head as signs of victory, because those who entered the bedchamber were previously impregnable to lust, that is, they had not been overcome by pleasure. But if someone overcome by lust has given himself over to harlots, why should he who has submitted his neck to so foul a lust walk about crowned, as if for some reward?"

units.la: Cæterùm de more explorandi virginalia, siue signa virginitatis, & ea probandi iudiciis, varia afferuntur à Lyrano, Luthero, Paulo Fagio, &c. Plerique per virginitatcs, siue signa virginitatis intelligunt lintea infecta sanguine rupti hymenis, in quibus congressus primum fuerat maritus cum virgine, quæ parentes seruare solebant. Allegoria huius loci sic habet: Vir ille qui vxorem diffamat non esse virginem, Christus est, qui synagogæ virginitatem operibus religiosam accusat per Euangelium, non esse integram fide. Sed parentes ei fortiter resistentes, significat pugnam illam, qua iustitia operum testibus scripturis & expansó vestimento defenditur (Expandere.n.vestem, signum est euidentis probationis, sicut excutere, comminationis: scindere, indignationis) Et Christus castigatur plagis.i. blasphemijs, & mulctatur, tandè eam retinere cogitur, quia oportet hypocritas in regno suo esse speciosos[?], quos alat, & magistros eorum sub nomine suo, qui vinci non volunt. Si autem conuincitur ista non esse virgo fidei, occiditur, id est, verbo Dei interficitur, ut viuat in spiritu, amissa gloria virginitatis legalis. Dominus adaugeat nobis fidem, quae sit efficax per dilectionem, per quam cognoscuntur discipuli Christi, Amen[?].
units.tr: Concerning the custom of examining the virginal signs, or tokens of virginity, and of proving them by judgments, various accounts are given by Lyra, Luther, Paul Fagius, and others. Most understand by the virginities, or tokens of virginity, the linens stained with blood from the broken hymen, on which the husband first lay with the virgin, and which the parents used to keep. The allegory of this passage runs thus: the man who defames the wife as not a virgin is Christ, who through the Gospel accuses the synagogue, religious in its works, of not being whole in faith. But the parents resisting him vigorously signify that battle in which the righteousness of works is defended by the witness of the Scriptures and by the spread-out cloth. (To spread out a garment is a sign of clear proof, as to shake it is a sign of threat, and to tear it a sign of indignation.) And Christ is chastised with blows, that is, with blasphemies, and is fined; finally he is compelled to keep her, because hypocrites must be showy in his kingdom, and he nourishes them, and their teachers under his name, who do not wish to be conquered. But if she is convicted of not being a virgin of faith, she is put to death, that is, slain by the Word of God, so that she may live in the Spirit, having lost the glory of legal virginity. May the Lord increase in us the faith that is effective through love, by which the disciples of Christ are known. Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XVIII.
units.tr: CONCIO XVIII.

units.la: Deut. 23.
units.tr: Deut. 23.

units.la: Non erit scortum de filiabus Israel, nec erit scortator de filiis Israel.
units.tr: There shall not be a whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a whoremonger of the sons of Israel.

units.la: 1 Cum Deus velit sanctum habere populum, prohibet non solum adulterium, sed etiam scortationem, quae contraria est sanctificationi, 1. Thessal. 4. & hominem inquinat, Marc. 7. Prohibet autem illam omni sexui, mulieribus & viris, puellis & juvenibus. Dicit enim, Non erit meretrix e filiabus Israel, neque erit scortum masculum, vel puer meritorius (ut quidam vertunt) e filiis Israel.
units.tr: 1 Since God wishes to have a holy people, he forbids not only adultery but also whoredom, which is opposed to sanctification (1 Thess. 4; and it defiles a man, Mark 7). He forbids it to every sex, to women and men, to girls and young men. For he says: There shall be no harlot of the daughters of Israel, nor shall there be a male whore, or a boy kept for hire (as some translate it), of the sons of Israel.

units.la: Errant igitur, qui in quaestionem vocant, sit ne scelus fornicatio? Si enim scelus & malum non esset, Deus non ita graviter vetuisset ac punivisset, tum hic, tum alibi, 1. Corinthiorum 6. Actor. 15. Ephes. 5. Hebr. 12. 13. Tob. 4. Sirac. 41.
units.tr: Those therefore err who call into question whether fornication is a crime at all. For if it were not a crime and an evil, God would not have forbidden and punished it so severely, both here and elsewhere (1 Cor. 6; Acts 15; Eph. 5; Heb. 12–13; Tob. 4; Sirach 41).

units.la: 2 Errant etiam qui quaerunt, quare Dominus prohibuerit simplicem fornicatione: quae quaestio & diabolica & stulta dignaq; irrisione[?] est: nam a diabolo primum talis quaestio proposita est, Gen. 3. Cur praecepit vobis Deus, inquit serpens ad mulierem, ut non comederetis ex omni ligno paradisi? Deinde si quis veniret ad aliquem nobilem, & diceret ei, quare non permittis filias tuas proftitui? cur vis eas maritari? Es ne fatuus, responderet utique ille. Quanto magis ergo fatuus reputari debet iste, qui de coelesti rege hoc audet quaerere, quare ipse filias suas non permittat fornicari, quare velit eas, vel castas permanere, vel nuptijs tradi?
units.tr: 2 Those also err who ask why the Lord forbade simple fornication. This question is both devilish and foolish and deserves to be mocked. For it was first put forward by the devil: Gen. 3, "Why did God command you," said the serpent to the woman, "that you should not eat of every tree of the garden?" Next, if someone came to a nobleman and said to him, "Why do you not allow your daughters to be prostituted? Why do you want them married?" the nobleman would surely reply, "Are you a fool?" How much more, then, ought he to be thought a fool who dares to ask the heavenly King this: why he does not allow his own daughters to fornicate, why he wants them either to remain chaste or to be given in marriage?

units.la: ʒ[?] Iuste autem Deus prohibuit scortationem, ac merito etiam illa quidem nobis est fugienda.
units.tr: Justly, then, has God forbidden whoredom, and rightly must we flee from it.

units.la: Primùm, quia placet diabolo autori omnis peccati, & daemonibus infestissimis Dei & nostris hostibus: nam Behemoth dormit in locis humentibus, id est, luxuriosis: Iob. 40. ac daemones de omni quidem peccato gaudent, praecipuè tamen de fornicatione & idolatria, quia ibi corpus & anima maculatur.
units.tr: First, because it pleases the devil, the author of every sin, and the demons, the most hostile enemies of God and of us. For Behemoth sleeps in moist places, that is, places of lust (Job 40). And the demons rejoice in every sin, but especially in fornication and idolatry, because in them body and soul are defiled.

units.la: Deinde quia displicet angelis bonis, & sanctis hominibus, ut Simeoni, Leui, Phinees, &c. Si enim filia regis Franciae, aut alterius cuiusdam principis tradita effet alicui, ut custodiret eam, non parum displiceret ei, si in eius custodia fornicaretur: quantum ergo angelis displicere potest, si filiae regis caelestis, quib. ipsi ad custodiam deputati sunt, fornicantur.
units.tr: Second, because it displeases the good angels and holy men, such as Simeon, Levi, Phinehas, and others. For if the daughter of the king of France, or of some other prince, were handed over to someone to guard her, he would be not a little displeased if she fornicated under his guard. How much, then, can it displease the angels if the daughters of the heavenly King, whom they have been appointed to guard, fornicate?

units.la: Tertiò, quia Deo est contumeliosa, quia templum eius polluit: membrum Christi tollit, nomen eius prophanat: 1.Cor.6.Amos 2. Quarto, quia proximo est iniuriosa, 2.Reg. 11. 12. Denique ipsi scortatori nociua. Aufert enim ei cor, sicut & ebrietas, Hose.4. priuat eum opibus, Prou. 29. Luc. 15. Eccles. 9. honore, Leuit. 21.1. Cor. 5. vita, Num. 25. Deut. 22.2. Reg. 13. regno Dei, Gal. 5. Apoc. 21.
units.tr: Third, because it is insulting to God, since it pollutes his temple, takes away the member of Christ, and profanes his name (1 Cor. 6; Amos 2). Fourth, because it is injurious to our neighbour (2 Sam. 11–12). Finally, it is harmful to the fornicator himself. For it takes away his heart, as drunkenness does (Hos. 4); it deprives him of wealth (Prov. 29; Luke 15; Eccles. 9); of honour (Lev. 21; 1 Cor. 5); of life (Num. 25; Deut. 22; 2 Sam. 13); and of the kingdom of God (Gal. 5; Rev. 21).

units.la: Hæc cūm omnes, tum præcipuè iuuenes diligenter considerare debent, ut cogitatione magnitudinis peccati, & grauitatis supplicij assuescant turpes motus cordis compescere. Deus pater noster cœlestis creet in nobis corda munda, & abluat, sanctificet, iustificet nos per nomen Domini Iesu, & per spiritum suum sanctum, ut eum in corpore nostro, & in spiritu nostro glorificare possimus, nunc, & semper, & in secula seculorum, AMEN.
units.tr: All of us, but young people above all, ought to consider these things carefully, so that by thinking on the greatness of the sin and the gravity of the punishment they may accustom themselves to restrain shameful movements of the heart. May God our heavenly Father create clean hearts in us, and wash, sanctify and justify us through the name of the Lord Jesus and through his Holy Spirit, so that we may be able to glorify him in our body and in our spirit, now and always, and for ever and ever. AMEN.

units.la: CONCIO XIX. Judic. 3.
units.tr: CONCIO XIX. Judges 3.

units.la: HAbitauerunt autem filii Israel inter Chananæum, Hittheum, Aemoræum, Pherizæum, Huæum & Jebusæum. Duxeruntq; filias eorum sibi in uxores, & filias suas dederunt filiis eorum, seruieruntq; diis eorum. Et fecerunt filii Israel malum in oculis Domini, obliitque sunt Domini Dei sui, colentes Bealim & Aferoth. Iratus autem est Dominus contra Israel, & vendidit eos in manus Chusan Riseathaym regis Mesopotamiae, seruiqe erunt; filii Israel Chusan Riseathaym octo annis. Et cùm clamassent filii Israel ad Dominũ, suscitauit Dominus saluatorem filiis Israel, atque liberauit eos, nepe Othniel filium Kenaz fratris Caleb, qui illo minor erat. Factusq; est super eum spiritus Domini, & iudicauit Israelem: & egressus in praelium tradidit Dominus in manu eius Chusan Riseathaym regem Syriae, praevaluitq; manus eius contra Chusan Riseathaym. Et quieuit terra quadraginta annis, mortuusq; est Othniel filius Kenaz.
units.tr: Now the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite. They took their daughters to be their wives, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods. The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the Lord and forgot the Lord their God, serving Baalim and the Asheroth. So the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, and the children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years. When the children of Israel cried to the Lord, the Lord raised up a saviour for the children of Israel and freed them, namely Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb. The Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel; he went out to battle, and the Lord delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Syria into his hand, and his hand prevailed against Cushan-rishathaim. And the land had rest forty years, and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

units.la: 1 Historia haec probat veritatem verborum Dei,id est, omnium praeceptorum, minarum & promissionum eius. Sicuti enim praedixit Deut. 7. ita factum est, vt hic legimus. Nam vt multa bona nascuntur ex coniugio recte, & in nomine ac timore Dei initio: sic plurima mala ex coniugio prauo & impio .i. contra mandatum Dei contracto, veluti sunt, seruitus deorum alienorum, in quibus recensentur non solum Baalim & Aseroth, sed etiam Mammona, venter, &c. item obliuio veri Dei: ira Dei, bellu, seruitus, &c. Exod.23. Iosu.23.
units.tr: This history proves the truth of the words of God, that is, of all his precepts, threats and promises. For just as he foretold in Deuteronomy 7., so it came to pass, as we read here. For as many good things are born from a marriage contracted rightly and at the outset in the name and fear of God, so many evils arise from a wicked and impious marriage, that is, one contracted against the command of God: such as the service of strange gods, which includes not only Baalim and Asherah but also Mammon, the belly, and so on; likewise forgetfulness of the true God, the wrath of God, war, servitude, and so on. Exodus 23.; Joshua 23.

units.la: 2 Igitur non temerè veteres quatuor obferuanda esse ijs dixerunt, qui matrimoniū contrahere volunt. Primò enim debent Deum, eiusq; verbum ponere in conspectu suo, & non excludere à mente sua, Tob. 6. sequi ipsius voluntatem, non suam, vt scilicet contrahant desiderio generandi filios secundum carnem, qui possit fiant filij Dei per adoptionem, Gen. 1. Tob. 8. Verisimū est enim quod Hebraei dicunt: vt si ex vocibus וּשְׁמוֹ[?] & הַשֵּׁם[?] abstuleris sacras literas vel י[?] vel ה[?] nihil manet nisi יהוה[?] ignis temporalis & æternus: ita si auferas ex coniugio Deum, nil nisi maximus cruciatus remanet.
units.tr: Therefore the ancients did not rashly say that four things are to be observed by those who wish to contract marriage. First, they ought to set God and his word before their eyes, not exclude them from their mind (Tobit 6.), and follow his will, not their own; so that they marry not from a desire of begetting children according to the flesh, but so that they may become children of God through adoption (Genesis 1.; Tobit 8.). For what the Hebrews say is true: just as if you removed the sacred letters from the words [...] and [...], either the yod or the he, nothing remains but the fire, temporal and eternal, so if you take God out of marriage, nothing remains but the greatest torment.

units.la: Deinde debent eligere similes sibi ac pares, præsertim quod religionem attinet, Genes. 24. vide Lombardum lib. 4. Dist. 29. & Rodolphum Gualtherum Hom. 6. in Malachiam, vbi septem grauissimis rationibus demonstrat in coniugio religionis quoq; causam agi, & proinde huius præcipuam curam esse habendam. Quid enim communicabit cacabus ad ollam? Sirac. 13. aut quæ pars fideli cum infideli? 2.Corinth.6.1.Corinth.7. Paritas ista bene in annulo ostenditur, qui si strictior fit, digito non congruit: si latior, decidit. Sic se habet inter coniuges, si sint dispares: quia vel sint u[?] manentes non sunt concordes: vel unus ab altero discedit. Pessimum est, quando corporum coiunctionem, animorum ad vitia coniunctio sequitur, vt in Salomone & eius uxorib. accidit, 3. Reg. 11. Domicilla, neptis Domitiani Cæsaris ex sorore, quum Aureliano Flavio Clementis Domitiani fratris filio nubere nollet, putans sibi Christianæ cum gentili viro non bene conventurum, in Pontiam insulam pro confessione nominis Christiani deportata, longum ibi martyrium (teste Hieronymo, Tom. I. Pa.8.) duxit: & tandem à Luxurio, fratre Aureliani, sub Traiano, cum sacrificare idolis noluit, unà cum suis famulis, in urbe Tarracina, in cubiculo cremata est.
units.tr: Second, they ought to choose those like and equal to themselves, especially in respect of religion (Genesis 24.; see Lombard, book 4, distinction 29, and Rudolf Gualther, homily 6 on Malachi, where in seven most weighty reasons he shows that in marriage the question of religion is also at stake, and that therefore this must be the chief care). For what will the pot communicate to the kettle? (Sirach 13.) Or what fellowship has the faithful with the unfaithful? (2 Corinthians 6.; 1 Corinthians 7.) This equality is well shown in a ring: if it is too tight it does not fit the finger, if too loose it falls off. So it is between spouses if they are unequal: either they remain unlike and not in agreement, or one departs from the other. The worst is when the joining of bodies is followed by a joining of souls in vices, as happened with Solomon and his wives (1 Kings 11.). Domitilla, the niece of the emperor Domitian through his sister, when she was unwilling to marry Aurelius Flavius, the son of Domitian's brother Clement, thinking that a Christian woman would not agree well with a heathen husband, was deported to the island of Pontia for confession of the Christian name, and endured a long martyrdom there (as Jerome testifies, vol. I, p. 8). At last, under Trajan, when she refused to sacrifice to idols, she was burned in a chamber at the city of Terracina, together with her servants, by Luxurius, the brother of Aurelius.

units.la: Tertiò, debent contrahere cum istiusmodi personis, quæ sunt de progenie bona & honesta, non Caina, Genes.6.aut Chananæa, Genes.24.28. aut Achabæa,4. Reg.8. id est, impia & iniusta, Exod.34.
units.tr: Third, they ought to marry persons who are of a good and honest stock, not Cainite (Genesis 6.) or Canaanite (Genesis 24., 28.) or Ahabite (4 Kings 8.), that is, impious and unjust (Exodus 34.).

units.la: Quartò, eligere magis animæ pulchritudinem & morum integritatem, quàm opes, formam, &c. Eccles.7.
units.tr: Fourth, they ought to prefer beauty of soul and integrity of character to wealth, appearance and the like (Ecclesiastes 7.).

units.la: 3. Quid autem agendum iis qui perperâ contraxerunt matrimonium, & ob id iustè à Deo puniuntur? Israelitæ ingemuerunt ac invocarunt Deum (quem historia illa nobis ostendit non solùm veracem, iustum, iratum, sed etiam bonum & misericordem) Hic misit illis salvatorem, nomine Athniel, qui præfigurauit Christum Iesum verum liberatorem, de quo Ioannes 8. Ac vide, ut Origenes monet, quàm larga sit divina clementia. Octo annis filii Israel seruierant pro multorum delictis. Quadraginta annis per unius iustitiam in pace perdurant. Hunc igitur[?] Dominum Deum invocet omnis in tribulatione constitutus. Quisquis enim invocaverit eum in veritate, salvus erit. Ipsi ergo debetur benedictio, honor, potestas in secula seculorum, Amen.
units.tr: 3. But what is to be done by those who have contracted marriage wrongly, and are therefore justly punished by God? The Israelites groaned and called upon God (whom that history shows us to be not only true, just and angry, but also good and merciful). He sent them a saviour named Othniel, who prefigured Christ Jesus the true deliverer, of whom John 8. And see, as Origen warns, how great the divine clemency is: for eight years the children of Israel served for the sins of many; for forty years they continued in peace through the righteousness of one. Therefore let everyone who is in tribulation call upon this Lord God. For whoever calls upon him in truth will be saved. To him therefore be blessing, honour and power, for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XX.
units.tr: SERMON XX.

units.la: Judic. 14.
units.tr: Judges 14.

units.la: Escendens[?] autem Simson in Thimnath, vidit mulierem in Thimnath de filiabus Phelistæorum. Et ascendens indicavit patri suo atq; matri suæ, dicens: Mulierem vidi in Thimnath de filiab. Phelistæorum: nunc itaq; accipite eam mihi in uxorem. Ad quem autem pater suus atque mater sua: Nunquid non est in filiabus fratrum tuorum, & in omni populo meo mulier, quod tu vadis accipere uxorem de Phelistæis incircumcisis? respondit Simson patri suo: Hanc mihi accipe, quoniam recta visa est in oculis meis. Pater autem eius & mater eius nesciebant, quod à Domino hoc esset, quodq; occasionem quæreret contra Phelistæos, cum illo tempore Phelistæi dominarentur Israeli. Descendit itaq; Simson & parentes tius in Thimnath, veneruntq; ad vineas Thimnath,& ecce catulus ex leonibus rugiebat in occursum eius. Et irruens super eum spiritus Domini, discerpsit ille eum, perinde quasi discerpsisset hœdum, nihil habens in manu sua, nec indicauit patri suo aut matri hoc quod fecerat. Descendens autem loquutus est ad mulierem, rectaq; ipsa visa est in oculis Simson. Et reuersus post aliquot dies vt illam acciperet, declinauit vt videret cadauer leonis: & ecce examen apum erat in corpore leonis,& mel. Et accipiens in manus suas abijt, eundo & comedendo, peruenitq; ad parentes suos, & dedit eis: qui & ipsi comederunt: non autem indicauit eis, quòd de corpore leonis accepisset mel illud. Descendit itaque pater eius ad mulierem: & Simson parauit ibi conuiuium: sic enim iuuenes facere solent. Factumq; est cum illi vidissent eū, tulerunt triginta socios,qui essent secum. Et dixit ad eos Simson: proponā nunc vobis aenigma: si indicando indicaueritis ipsum mihi septem conuiuij diebus, & inueneritis (solutionem eius) dabo vobis triginta sindones, atq; triginta mutatiorias vestes. Sin autem non potueritis indicare mihi, dabitis vos mihi triginta sindones, & triginta mutatorias vestes: qui responderunt ei: Propone aenigma tuum, ut audiamus ipsum. Et ait ad eos: De comedente exiit cibus, & de forti egressa est dulcedo: nec potuerunt indicare aenigma tribus diebus. Factum q; est in die septimo, ut dicerent ad uxorem Simson: Persuade viro tuo, ut indicet nobis aenigma, ne forte incendamus te & domum patris tui igne: num quid ut pauperes faceretis nos, vocastis nos huc? &c.
units.tr: And Samson went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath, of the daughters of the Philistines. And he came up and told his father and his mother, saying: I have seen a woman in Timnath, of the daughters of the Philistines; now therefore take her for me to wife. And his father and his mother said to him: Is there not a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, and among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said to his father: Take her for me, because she pleaseth me well. But his father and mother knew not that this was of the Lord, and that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel. So Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnath, and they came to the vineyards of Timnath; and behold, a young lion roared against him. And the spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he tore him as one tears a kid, having nothing in his hand; and he did not tell his father or mother what he had done. And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she pleased Samson well. And after some days, when he returned to take her, he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion; and behold, a swarm of bees was in the body of the lion, and honey. And he took it into his hands and went on, eating as he went, and came to his father and mother and gave them some, and they ate; but he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the body of the lion. So his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there, for so the young men used to do. And when they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him. And Samson said to them: I will now put forth a riddle to you; if you tell it me within the seven days of the feast, and find out the solution, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment. But if you cannot tell me, you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment. And they answered him: Put forth your riddle, that we may hear it. And he said to them: Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not tell the riddle in three days. And on the seventh day it came to pass that they said to Samson's wife: Persuade your husband to tell us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you invite us here to make us poor? etc.

units.la: 1 Legimus in hoc capite Samsonem duxisse uxorem: Vbi considerandum primo quis quam duxerit, quare, quando, vbi, cuius consilio: quomodo celebrari[?] sint nuptiæ: quæ nihil aliud sunt quàm coniugum inauguratio & publica matrimonii professio. Duxit aut Samson Nazaraeus, filius Manoah, de gnatione Dan, in uxorem filiam de Philistim, qui incircumcisi sunt i. non in foedere Dei, ex voluntate Dei, quaerentis occasionem contra Palaestinos, qua in Samsonem committentes punirentur: tempore quo Palaestini dominabantur Israelitis, qui malum fecerat in conspectu Domini: cuius iam crevisset Samson & grandis factus esset, Iud. 14[?]. in vr be Thimnath, quae à Iosua Daniae tribui ascribitur, sed quae nondum ab ea occupata tempore Samsonis esset: consilio Dei, & consensu parentum: quibus non consultis (sunt.n. honorandi) fas non erat liberos matrimonia inire.
units.tr: 1. We read in this chapter that Samson took a wife. Here we must consider first who he took, why, when, where, and at whose counsel the wedding was celebrated; for a wedding is nothing other than the inauguration of the spouses and the public profession of marriage. Samson the Nazarite, son of Manoah, of the tribe of Dan, took as his wife a daughter of the Philistines, who were uncircumcised, that is, not in the covenant of God. It was by the will of God, who sought an occasion against the Palestinians, so that they might be punished for what they committed against Samson, at a time when the Palestinians ruled over the Israelites, who had done evil in the sight of the Lord. Samson had now grown up and become a man (Judg. 14). He took her in the city of Timnath, which is assigned by Joshua to the tribe of Dan, but which had not yet been occupied by it in Samson's time. It was done by the counsel of God and with the consent of his parents; for without consulting them (since they are to be honoured) it was not lawful for children to enter into marriage.

units.la: Sic parentum consilio vxores duxerunt Isaac, Gen.24. Ismael, Gen.21. Iacob, Gen.29. Sichem, Gen.28. Her, Gen.38. Dauid, 1.Reg.18. Tobias, idq; iussu angeli, Tob.7.8. & hoc loco Samson, & alij pij homines. Et eam auctoritatem, vt ex parentum iudicio & voluntate liberi vxores ducant, Moses parentibus quoq; tribuit, cum Exod.34. cap. inquit: Nec vxores de filiabus eorum accipies filijs tuis. Et Paulus 1.Corin.7. Qui matrimonio iungit virginem suam, bene facit. Apparet quoq; ex Ecclesiasticis scriptoribus hunc morem à patrib. receptum, semper in Ecclesia & populo Dei obseruatum, ne liberi sine parentum consensu connubia inirent. Sic enim Tertul. lib.2. ad vxorem scribit: Nā nec in terris, filij sine consensu patrum rite & iure nubent. Et Ambrosius citans Euripidis versus in Andromacha, cum Orestes Hermionis connubium petit, ostendit hanc rem non ad suum, sed patris arbitrium pertinere. Ad legitimam ergo coniunctionem vnius maris & vnius fœminae non solum necesse est, vt earum personarum coniunctio fiat, quae sit nepharia & legibus prohibita (id quod & exemplum Corinthij monet 1. Cor.5.) & vt contractus fiat vtriusque[?] partis consensu (non quolibet, sed per verbâ expresso: nec de futuro, sed de præsenti) qui maximè de substantia matrimonij est: sed requiritur etiam parentum, in quorum potestate sunt liberi, consensus. Hortatur enim primum præceptum in secunda tabula Mosis liberos, ut & in nuptijs, re omnium maxima, parentes eo honore afficiant, ne sine illorum consensu & consilio connubia contrahant. Rursus autem oportet parentes non tyrannos esse, sed similes parentibus Simsonis, qui diuinum consilium ut cœpére agnoscere, secuti sunt, cui primo ignorantes repugnabant, dicentes: Nunquid non est mulier in filiabus, &c. quæ quidem reprehensio æqua erat, ut quàm probat lex illa, Deuter. 7. Neque sociabis cum eis connubia. Atqui ut interpretatio legis [illegible, ~10 letters] fieri non debet, literarum angustijs obseruatis, sed ex sententia legislatoris: ita etiam lex illa Mosaica ex sententia divini spiritus explicari debuit. Quo spiritu Samson incitatus, ea quæ fecit, ex voluntate Dei fecit, non humanâ.
units.tr: So with the counsel of their parents they took wives: Isaac (Gen. 24), Ishmael (Gen. 21), Jacob (Gen. 29), Shechem (Gen. 34), Er (Gen. 38), David (1 Sam. 18), Tobias, and that by the command of an angel (Tob. 7, 8), and in this place Samson, and other godly men. Moses also gives this authority to parents, that children take wives by their judgement and will, when in Exodus 34 he says: "Neither shalt thou take of their daughters for thy sons as wives." And Paul (1 Cor. 7): "He who marries his virgin does well." It also appears from the ecclesiastical writers that this custom was received from the Fathers, always observed in the Church and among the people of God, that children should not enter into marriages without the consent of their parents. For Tertullian writes thus in his second book To His Wife: "For not even on earth do sons marry rightly and lawfully without the consent of their fathers." And Ambrose, citing the verses of Euripides in the Andromache, when Orestes asks for the marriage of Hermione, shows that this matter pertains not to his own will but to the decision of the father. Therefore for a lawful union of one man and one woman it is not only necessary that the persons joined be not closely related and prohibited by law (which the example of the Corinthian also warns against, 1 Cor. 5), and that the contract be made by the consent of both parties (not any consent whatever, but expressed in words, and spoken in the present, not the future, which is of the very substance of marriage), but the consent of the parents is also required, in whose power the children are. For the first commandment of the second tablet of Moses urges children to honour their parents in this matter, the greatest of all, so that in marriage they do not contract unions without their consent and counsel. Again, however, parents ought not to be tyrants, but like the parents of Samson, who, once they began to recognise the divine counsel, followed it, though at first, not knowing, they resisted it, saying: "Is there not a woman among the daughters...?" This objection was indeed reasonable, as that law of Deuteronomy 7 proves: "Neither shalt thou make marriages with them." Yet just as the interpretation of a law must not be confined to the narrowness of the letters, but must follow the intention of the lawgiver, so that Mosaic law too ought to be explained according to the meaning of the divine Spirit. Samson, moved by this Spirit, did what he did by the will of God, not by human will.

units.la: De nuptijs dicitur in textu: Descendit itaque pater eius ad mulierem: & Simson parauit ibi conuiuium, lætitiæ symbolum. Etenim exordium matrimonij spem pollicetur prouehendi generis humani. Nam huius gratia status hic diuinitus institutus est, & cœlesti benedictione donatus. Vetus ergo consuetudo est, habere nuptialia conuiuia: vocare ad ea amicos & vicinos. Ut sponso ac sponsæ congratulentur, ac omnia prospera precentur, &c. Neque Christus, istius modi externos ritus usitatos & honestos in contrahendis matrimonijs, improbat. Nam Joan. 2. commemoratur, quod ipsemet unà eum Maria matre, & discipulis, conuiuio nuptiali inter fuerit, quod procul dubio præcessit quædam inuitatio, quædam ceremoniæ copulationis sponsi ac sponsæ, ne coniunctorum cohabitatio ulli sit offensaculo, ac malæ suspicioni obnoxia: postea & conuiuium sequutum est. Id quod etiam ex Apoc. 19. & parabola Matth .21. apparet, vbi regnum cælorum comparatur nuptijs, in quib. per seruos, homines prius inuitantur, nec accedit quisquam nisi vocatus. Testatur eadem parabola homines vestib. etiam mundioribus in conuiuijs nuptialibus vsos esse. Ad quod & Paulus alludit Eph.5. Idem & Chrysostomus testatur in cap. 4. ad Colos. Debet autem nuptiarum conuiuium cum gratiarum actione & timore Domini exerceri, Tob. 9. In hoc conuiuio, de more gentis Syrorum, ænigma, seu obscurum dictum propositum est: quod cùm triginta iuuenes arte soluere nequiuissent, eius soluendi rationem dolo & minis consequuti sunt. Ænigma tale fuit: De comedete exivit cibus, & de forti egressa est dulcedo, quod quid aliud significat, teste Augustino Ser. 107 de Tem: quàm Christũ à mortuis resurgentem? De edente vtique, id est, de morte, quæ cuncta deuorat atque consumit, exiuit cibus ille, qui dixit: Ego sum panis viuus, qui de coelo descendi: quem humana exacerbauit iniquitas, eique aceti & fellis amaritudinem propinauit, atque ab eo plebs gentium vitae dulcedinem conuersa suscepit: ac sic de mortui leonis ore, id est, de Christi morte, qui accubás dormiuit ut leo, [?]apum, id est, Christianorum processit examen. Chrysostomus Tom. 2.Hom. 41. Samson, inquit, de ore leonis fauum mellis abstraxit, Dominus de faucibus diaboli plebem suam, quae sibi per viam facta est dulcis, eripuit. Borrhaus scribit super hunc locum: Subducto velo, ut in occiso leone Satana & filio eius Antichristo, a Samsone Mesia inueniatur mel dulcissimum partae victoriae de peccato, morte & inferno, notum pijs est: Qui sentiunt Deum pro sua bonitate in morte vitae, in peccato gratiae, in inferni tenebris cœlestis lucis suaue & amabile mel suis parari. Qui cœlestis Samson etiam ipse maledicti serpentis & leonis habitum induit. peccatum & maledictum factus, ut nos a serpentis maledictione & leonis crudelitate vindicaret. de quo illud: Vicit leo de tribu Iuda: in cuius mortuo corpore dulcissimum euangelij mel inuenitur, de quo vates: Iura Domini dulciora melle. Nam non prius Euangelij fauus ex hoc mellario exprimi depromique coepit, quam leo is mortuus esset. De cuius melleo spiritu apud Ioannem capite septimo: Et spiritus nondum erat datus, quia qu'a Christus nondum erat glorificatus.
units.tr: Concerning the wedding it is said in the text: "So his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there," a symbol of joy. For the beginning of marriage promises the hope of propagating the human race; for this estate was instituted by God for its sake and endowed with heavenly blessing. It is therefore an ancient custom to hold wedding feasts, and to invite friends and neighbours to them, so that they may congratulate the bridegroom and bride and wish them every prosperity, etc. Nor does Christ disapprove of such external rites, customary and honourable in contracting marriages. For it is recorded in John 2 that he himself was present at the wedding feast with Mary his mother and his disciples; without doubt there had preceded some invitation and some ceremonies of the joining of bridegroom and bride, so that the living together of those joined might be no offence and liable to no evil suspicion; afterwards the feast followed. This also appears from Revelation 19 and from the parable in Matthew 22, where the kingdom of heaven is compared to a wedding, in which people are first invited by servants, and no one comes unless called. The same parable testifies that people used even cleaner garments at wedding feasts, to which Paul also alludes in Ephesians 5. Chrysostom likewise testifies this in his commentary on Colossians 4. The wedding feast ought to be held with thanksgiving and the fear of the Lord (Tob. 9). At this feast, after the manner of the Syrian people, a riddle, or obscure saying, was proposed; and when the thirty young men could not solve it by skill, they obtained the solution by guile and threats. The riddle was this: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness." What else does this signify, as Augustine witnesses (Sermon 107, On the Time), than Christ rising from the dead? Out of the eater, that is, out of death, which devours and consumes all things, came forth that meat which said: "I am the living bread which came down from heaven"; which human wickedness embittered, offering him the bitterness of vinegar and gall, and from whom the people of the Gentiles, turned to him, received the sweetness of life. And so out of the mouth of the dead lion, that is, from the death of Christ, who slept as a lion lies down, came forth a swarm of bees, that is, the Christians. Chrysostom (Vol. 2, Homily 41): "Samson," he says, "drew a honeycomb out of the lion's mouth; the Lord snatched his people from the jaws of the devil, which had been made sweet to him by the way." Borrhaus writes on this place: when the veil is drawn back, it is known to the godly that in the slain lion, Satan, and his son Antichrist, the most sweet honey of victory won over sin, death and hell is found by Samson the Messiah. They perceive that God, by his goodness, prepares for his own the sweet and lovely honey of heavenly light, out of death life, out of sin grace, out of the darkness of hell. This heavenly Samson also put on the form of the cursed serpent and of the lion, made sin and a curse, so that he might deliver us from the curse of the serpent and the cruelty of the lion. Of him is that saying: "The lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered" (Rev. 5). In his dead body the sweetest honey of the gospel is found, of which the prophet says: "The judgements of the Lord are sweeter than honey" (Ps. 19). For the honeycomb of the Gospel did not begin to be squeezed out and drawn from this honey-store until the lion was dead. Of this honeyed Spirit John speaks in chapter 7: "And the Spirit was not yet given, because Christ was not yet glorified."

units.la: 3 Plura hic latent adhuc mysteria. Sanson enim Christum significabat, [illegible, ~5 letters] illum iustitiæ, de quo Malach. 4. Is sponsam[?] ex gentibus sibi iunxit in matrimonium: rugientem leonem Satanam interfecit: victoriam de leone sponsæ suæ patefecit, &c. Huic igitur sit gloria in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: 3. Many more mysteries lie hidden here. For Samson signified Christ, [illegible] that Sun of righteousness, of whom Malachi 4 speaks. He joined to himself a bride from among the Gentiles in marriage; he slew the roaring lion Satan; he revealed the victory over the lion to his bride, etc. To him therefore be glory for ever, Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XXI.
units.tr: SERMON XXI.

units.la: Pfalm. 127.
units.tr: Psalm 127.

units.la: Anticum graduum Salomenis: Si Dominus non ædificet domum, frustrà laborant qui ædificant eam: & si Dominus non custodiat civitatem, frustrà vigilat custos. Vanum est vobis ut maturetis mane surgendo, & moram faciatis sedendo, comedentes panem dolorum: sic dabit dilecto suo somnum. Ecce hæreditas Domini, filij sunt: & merces fructus ventris. Sicut sagittæ in manu fortis, sic sunt filij iuventutis. Beatus vir ille, qui ex his adimpleuit pharetram suam: non pudefient, quando loquentur cum hostibus in porta.
units.tr: A song of degrees of Solomon. Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labour in vain; unless the Lord keeps the city, the watchman keeps watch in vain. It is vain for you to rise early and sit up late, eating the bread of sorrows; so he gives sleep to his beloved. Behold, children are the heritage of the Lord, and the fruit of the womb is his reward. As arrows in the hand of a strong man, so are the sons of youth. Blessed is the man who has filled his quiver with them; they shall not be ashamed when they speak with their enemies in the gate.

units.la: {1} Titulus huius Psalmi est: Canticu Maaloth.i. graduum, vel ascensionu, Salomonis Is enim Psalmum hunc vel ipse fecit, vel alii, us propter ipsum. Reputabat enim se & totum populum suum non sufficere ad ædificationem domus Domini, 2. Paral. 2.
units.tr: {1} The title of this Psalm is: A song of the ascents, or of the degrees, of Solomon. For either he himself wrote this Psalm, or another wrote it on his account. For he judged that he and all his people were not sufficient for building the house of the Lord, 2 Chron. 2.

units.la: Fuit autem Salomon figura Iesu Christi verè pacifici, qui ædificat civitatem Dei: ad quam suspirare & ascendere debemus, amando[?] Deum.
units.tr: Now Solomon was a type of Jesus Christ, the truly peaceable one, who builds the city of God; towards it we ought to long and ascend, loving God.

units.la: Sunt qui dicant in hoc Psalmo primum agi de domus Dei ædificatione corporali: inde de spirituali: ibi, Cùm dederit dilectis suis somnum.
units.tr: Some say that in this Psalm the building of God's house is first treated in a bodily sense, and then in a spiritual sense; the latter is where it says: "When he gives his beloved sleep."

units.la: Alij dicunt duplicem hic describi populum: veterem (cuius vani sunt omnes conatus & vires) & novum, qui sunt dilecti Dei, & filij renati, quos Deus ipse possidet & regit suo spiritu, suntque hæreditas Christi, à patre sibi tradita.
units.tr: Others say that two peoples are described here: the old, whose efforts and strength are all vain, and the new, who are God's beloved and reborn children, whom God himself possesses and rules by his Spirit, and who are the inheritance of Christ, handed to him by the Father.

units.la: Alij hunc Psalmum docere aiunt, œconomias & politias non posse gubernari & defendi, nisi benedicente Domino, probarique hoc exemplo: Sic enim & cætera omnia benedictionis esse, sicut procreationem sobolis. Ac videtur nonnullis hunc psalmum esse specialiter ad hoc deputatum, ut in dedicationib. ædium, quæ Iudæis in usu fuerunt, caneretur, quo mentes ædificantium ac laborantium ad providentiæ Dei fidem dirigerentur.
units.tr: Others say that this Psalm teaches that households and commonwealths cannot be governed and defended unless the Lord blesses them, and they prove this by the example that all other things are likewise a matter of blessing, as the procreation of offspring is. And it seems to some that this Psalm was specially set aside for this purpose, to be sung at the dedication of houses, which was the custom among the Jews, so that the minds of those who build and labour might be directed to trust in God's providence.

units.la: 2 Propositionem in primo & secundo versu amplificat antithesi. Benedictione Domini omnia fieri, non labore & conatu nostro, fro,Sirac.ii.i.Cor.ʒ.Rom.9 Proue.10. Ergo laborandum quidem est, sed fructus laboris à Deo sperandus. Ergo nemo confidat in propria sapientia & fortitudine:Ierem.9. Sine Domino enim nihil possumus. Vt autem nobis adsit, inuocandus erit, Psal.145. Vt nos custodiat, Israel esse debemus, Psal.12. Vt nos benedicat, iustitiæ studendum fuerit, Prou. 3. Vt domum & familiam nostram instruat, aedificatio illius in nomine Christi incipienda, Matth.18. non in nomine Veneris, aut Mammonæ, Tob.6.1.Tim 6. Qui hæc faciunt, sunt dilecti & amici Domini: quibus Dominus dat somnum, id est, iucundam ac tranquillam quietem, cor liberum à nimia cura: & omnia necessaria quasi per somnum, sine vlla praeuia cura & solicitudine, sine vllo anxio labore & negotio. Si autem Dominus dormientibus benedicit, multò magis verbum eius audientibus.
units.tr: 2 The proposition in the first and second verses is amplified by antithesis: all things are done by the blessing of the Lord, not by our labour and effort, Sir. 2; 1 Cor. 3; Rom. 9; Prov. 10. Therefore we must indeed labour, but the fruit of our labour is to be hoped for from God. Therefore let no one trust in his own wisdom and strength, Jer. 9. For without the Lord we can do nothing. And that he may be with us, he must be called upon, Ps. 145. That he may keep us, we ought to be Israel, Ps. 12. That he may bless us, we must strive for righteousness, Prov. 3. That he may guide our house and family, its building must begin in the name of Christ, Matt. 18, not in the name of Venus or Mammon, Tob. 6; 1 Tim. 6. Those who do these things are the beloved and friends of the Lord, to whom the Lord gives sleep, that is, a pleasant and tranquil rest, a heart free from excessive care, and all necessary things as if through sleep, without any prior care and anxiety, without any anxious toil and business. If the Lord blesses those who sleep, how much more those who hear his word.

units.la: ʒ Porrò fi donant Dei sunt liberi, vt tertius versus docet, vbi hæreditas & merces Domini vocantur: & rex Dauid coram populo suo confitetur, dicens: siquidem multos filios dedit mihi Dominus: 1. Paral. 28. malè agunt istæ mulieres, quæ impatienter ferūt, quando sobole à Deo donantur. Peius hæ, quæ pharmacis arcessunt sterilitatem, ne parturiendi nutriendiue laborem ferant, aut ne quid seni: formæ conciliant. Pessime illæ, quæ fœtum iam viuum in vtero necant, aut pharmacis eijciunt. Olim ignominiam & maledictionem interpretabantur fœminæ, carere liberis, Genes.30. 1.Reg.1. Luc.1. Ergo abundare. pro'e, benedictionis est: unde Moses in benedictione filiorum Israel dicebat ad Asser: Benedictus ob filios Asser. Idemque testatur in Genesi, sanctas mulieres, vt Liam, & Rachelem, pro singulis partubus Deo gratias egisse, nimirum intelligentes & sterilitatem & fœcunditatem arbitrio numinis immitti. Huc etiam facit dictum Benfyrae[?]: Cui nō sunt liberi, reputatur tanquam mortuus. Cui vero sunt liberi, perinde est ac si adhuc viuat, & nomen eius non est deletum. Debent autē opera dare qui liberos habent, vt illos timorem Domini doceant, Sirac.30. & iuxta D. Basilium in 1. Serm. exercitam[?]: adducant ad Dominum eos, qui dati sunt ab ipso. Tunc videbunt eos prudenter omnia administrare & fortiter agere, tanquam robustos iuuenes. Deus enim fortissimus dat illis viuacē valetudinem & alia munera sua, id quod similitudine sagittarum in manu potentis existentium explicatur. Et beatus est vir ille, cui tales contingunt sagittæ, id est filij qui sint parentibus ad manum, sicut viro potenti ad manum sunt sagittæ: nam non pudefiunt, cum in portis ad iudicium venerint, disceptaturi cum hostibus suis. Sunt enim prudenter educati, ideo prudenter omnia administrabunt. Deo, qui dat liberis nostris animas & corpora, & addit nobis & illis omnia neceffaria, sit honor & gloria in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: 3 Moreover, if children are gifts of God, as the third verse teaches, where they are called the inheritance and reward of the Lord; and King David confesses before his people, saying: "Since the Lord has given me many sons," 1 Chron. 28. Those women act badly who bear it impatiently when they are granted offspring by God. Worse are those who seek barrenness by drugs, so as not to bear the labour of childbirth and nursing, or so as not to lose their looks. Worst of all are those who kill a child already alive in the womb, or expel it with drugs. In former times women regarded being without children as a shame and a curse, Gen. 30; 1 Sam. 1; Luke 1. Therefore abundance is a blessing; hence Moses, in blessing the sons of Israel, said to Asher: "Blessed above the sons is Asher." And he testifies in Genesis that holy women, such as Leah and Rachel, gave thanks to God for each birth, clearly understanding that both barrenness and fruitfulness are sent by the will of the divine power. The saying of Ben Sira also applies here: he who has no children is reckoned as dead; but he who has children is as if still living, and his name is not blotted out. Those who have children ought to take pains to teach them the fear of the Lord, Sir. 30; and according to St Basil in his first sermon, they should bring to the Lord those who have been given by him. Then they will see them manage everything prudently and act bravely, like strong young men. For God, the strongest, gives them lively health and his other gifts, which is explained by the likeness of arrows in the hand of a mighty man. And blessed is the man to whom such arrows fall, that is, sons who are at hand to their parents as arrows are at the hand of a powerful man; for they will not be ashamed when they come to judgment in the gates, to contend with their enemies. For they have been prudently brought up, so they will prudently manage everything. To God, who gives our children souls and bodies, and adds to us and to them all necessary things, be honour and glory for ever, Amen.

units.la: CONCIO XXII
units.tr: SERMON XXII

units.la: Pfal. 128.
units.tr: Psal. 128.

units.la: Anticum graduum : Beatus quicunque timet Dominum, qui ambulat in vijs eius. Si quidem laborem manuum tuarum comedes : beatus ( eris ) tu : & bene tibi erit. Vxor tua vt vitis frugifera erit in lateribus domus tuæ, & filij tui sicut plantulæ oliuarum in circuitu mensæ tuæ. Ecce sic benedicetur vir, qui timuerit Dominum. Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Zion, & videas bonum Ierusalem, cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ. Et videas filiorum tuorum filios: pax super Israel.
units.tr: A song of ascents. Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways. For you shall eat the labour of your hands: you are blessed, and it shall be well with you. Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine in the sides of your house, and your sons like olive plants round about your table. Behold, thus shall the man be blessed who fears the Lord. May the Lord bless you out of Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life. And may you see your children's children: peace upon Israel.
