Nor was this vow in vain, for he did win the victory over his enemies, and he himself became the author for the Franks of receiving the Christian religion.

units.la: Declarat autem nonnihil causam istam, quomodo sine sermone, consuetudine mulierum aliqui lucrifieri queant: nempe, inquit, spectando mulierum timorem Dei ac mariti, castitatemque earum. Per hasce autem præcipuas intelligit etiam alias virtutes illis adjunctas, non exclusis earum pki[?] colloquiis.
units.tr: He also explains somewhat the cause of this, namely how some may be gained without speech, through the habit of women: that is, he says, by looking at the fear of God and of the husband in women, and at their chastity. By these chief things he also understands the other virtues joined to them, not excluding their pious conversations.

units.la: Porrò confirmata subjectione mulierum erga maritos, describit etiam ornatum eis convenientem, tanquam partem honestae sanctaeq; conversationis, & boni exempli maritos ad pietatem permoturi. Siquidem non parum momenti habet, qua quis sit veste amictus. Neq; enim temere apud veteres & nostri aevi homines Adagium increbuit, Ex veste aestimari hominem. Unde & Ecclesiasticus cap.19.inquit: Suus cujusq; habitus, aut ristum[?] diducens, rifio[?], incessusq; hominis, quomodo sit animatus arguunt. Credimus enim plerique varii & inconstantioris animi indicium esse vestem varicolorem, corrupti aut lacerandi cupidi laceratam five conscissam, arrogantis & impudentis plus nimio exquisitam & procacem. Proinde Petrus adversus muliebrem luxum (quem sibi velut cognatū habens) disserit: modestiam & vitae sanctimoniam commendat. Ac primum quidem ostendit, sicut & Paulus 1.Tim.2. à quo fortasis (ut Marloratus ex Bullingero refert) hæc verba mutuatus est Petrus (& quod sanctos Dei viros nunquam puduit, inter sua retulit) ostendit, inquam, qualis non debeat esse ornatus sanctarum matronarum, nempe ille externus nimiusq; in contextu, five crispatura capillorum, in preciositate vestitus, & aliorum ornamentorum positus. Certum enim est argumentum, parum admodum spiritus eam assequutam esse, quae in externum ornatum multum insumit. Nam si fides ac spiritus vere adessent, citius calcarent eum pedibus, quam eo oblectarentur, ut Helther[?],cap. 14. Deinde vero positive indicat, piarum mulierum ornatum esse illum internum novumque hominem, ad imaginem Dei regeneratum, reformatumque. Hunc etiam expressius describens vocat incorruptum (opponitur autem incorruptio rebus fluxis & caducis, quae ad corporis ornatum serviunt) mansuetumque & quietum spiritum. Talis enim debet esse pia mens aut anima renata piorum (quam hic vocat occultum hominem cordis) praesertim autem mulierum, quas etiam magis modestia & mansuetudo simplicitasque decet, quam viros.
units.tr: Having confirmed the subjection of wives to their husbands, he also describes the adornment fitting for them, as part of an honest and holy way of life and a good example that will move husbands to piety. For it matters not a little what clothing a person wears. Indeed, the saying "A man is judged by his clothing" has become common among the ancients and among people of our own age. Hence Ecclesiasticus 19 also says: "A man's bearing, the laughing of his teeth, and his gait reveal what he is like." For most people believe that a many-coloured garment is a sign of a changeable and inconstant mind, a torn or ragged garment that of one who desires corruption, and an overly elaborate and showy dress that of one who is arrogant and shameless. Accordingly Peter argues against female luxury, which he has as a kinswoman, as it were: he commends modesty and holiness of life. First he shows, just as Paul does in 1 Tim. 2 (from which perhaps, as Marlorat reports from Bullinger, Peter borrowed these words, and what never shamed the holy men of God he included among his own), he shows, I say, what the adornment of holy matrons should not be: that is, external and excessive adornment, in the braiding of hair, in the costliness of clothing, and in the placing of other ornaments. For it is a certain sign that one who spends much on external adornment has attained very little of the Spirit. For if faith and the Spirit were truly present, they would sooner trample such things under their feet than take delight in them, as Helther says, ch. 14. Then, positively, he indicates that the adornment of pious women is that inner, new man, renewed and reformed according to the image of God. Describing this more expressly, he calls it incorruptible (incorruption is opposed to fleeting and perishable things, which serve bodily adornment), and a meek and quiet spirit. For this is what the pious mind or regenerate soul of the godly ought to be (which he here calls the hidden man of the heart), and especially that of women, whom modesty, gentleness and simplicity become even more than men.

units.la: Hunc igitur talem internū hominem, ornatum, aut spiritum, dicit esse preciosum coram Deo, quod est primum argumentum hujus hypothesis, de forma modoq; ornatus mulierum. Omnes enim pii ea debent spectare & sectari, quae sint preciosa, quaeq; eos reddant formosos acceptosq; coram Deo, non quae coram stultis hominibus. Estque haec antithesis exterioris & interioris hominis diligenter notanda. Dicebat Cato, qui anxie occupantur in corporis cultu, animi cultum negligere: ita Petrus cohibendę mulierum cupiditati hoc remedium affert, ut excolendis animis studio potius suum addicat. Quod fiet si foemina fit animo meteq;incorrupta, nihil agat ex affectibus muliebribus, nihil intemperantiæ, iracundiæ, rixis, ambitioni, arrogantiæ vel procacitati tribuat: sed mitis, placida, tractabilis, & mansueta fit. Nihil enim est quod huic sexum magis deceat, quàm placidum & sedatum ingenium. Scimus enim quàm importunum sit animal imperiosa & refractaria mulier.
units.tr: He therefore says that this inner man, this adornment or spirit, is precious before God. This is the first argument of this thesis concerning the form and manner of women's adornment. For all the pious ought to look to and pursue what is precious, and what makes them beautiful and acceptable before God, not what is so before foolish men. And this contrast between the outer and the inner man is to be carefully noted. Cato used to say that those who are anxiously occupied with care of the body neglect care of the soul. So Peter offers this remedy for restraining women's desires: that they devote themselves rather to cultivating their souls. This will happen if a woman is unspoiled in mind and character, does nothing out of feminine passions, attributes nothing to intemperance, anger, quarrels, ambition, arrogance or shamelessness, but is mild, calm, tractable and gentle. For nothing suits this sex better than a placid and settled disposition. We know how unmanageable a creature a domineering and obstinate woman is.

units.la: Secunda ratio sumpta est in genere ab exemplo veterum sanctarum mulierum (at exemplis ad permovendum auditoris animum nihil evidentius) quarum duo primaria spiritualiaque ornamenta nominat, spem in Deum, & subjectionem erga maritos.
units.tr: The second reason is drawn generally from the example of the holy women of old (and nothing is more telling for moving the mind of the hearer than examples). Of these he names two chief and spiritual adornments: hope in God, and subjection to their husbands.

units.la: Nominatim vero producit exemplum Sarae, quæ cùm sit mater fidelium, præsertim apud suum sexum, honore & imitatione digna est, Ief.51[?]. Hujus tres primarias virtutes nominat: primùm, quòd maritum ut suum dominum, non solùm nominavit (Gen.18.) sed etiam reipsa coluit. Non enim moratur Deus istos titulos sinere: & fieri interdum potest, ut quæ maximè petulans fuerit & immorigera, hanc appellatione lingua usurpet, ut regina Vasthi, Esther 1. Secundò, quòd fuit benefica: tertiò, quòd fidens Deo, non muliebriter trepidaverit in tot illis mariti peregrinationibus, jactationibus & cruciatibus: sicut alioqui illæ plerunque solent in adversis nimium pavidæ impatientesque esse, & etiam ipsos maritos languefacere, & trepidos impatientesque reddere, ac excruciare, ut Iobum sua uxor. Præterea quum superstitio solum sit genus muliebre, & idcirco in rebus nihili frequenter exanimetur (timens sibi ubi nihil periculi, & credens, quæ sunt superstitiosa minimeque credenda) jubet ut posito illo inani pavore, totas sese Deo dent. Sexus enim imbecillitas facit, ut magis suspiciosæ ac timidæ sint mulieres, ideoque magis morosæ: quia verentur ne, si viris se subijciant, magis contumeliosè ab illis tractentur. Hunc pavorem Petrus abesse cupit. q. d. Libenter subijcite vos virorum imperio, nec vos timor ab obsequio impediat, quasi deterior futura sit vestra conditio, si patientes sitis.
units.tr: Specifically, he brings forward the example of Sarah, who, as the mother of believers, especially among her sex, is worthy of honour and imitation (Isa. 51). He names three of her chief virtues. First, that she called her husband her lord, and not only in word (Gen. 18) but also in deed she honoured him. For God does not allow those titles to be used in vain, and it can sometimes happen that a woman who has been most wanton and disobedient uses such a form of address in speech, as Queen Vashti did (Esther 1). Second, that she was kind. Third, that trusting in God she did not tremble womanishly through all those wanderings, tossings and torments of her husband. Otherwise women are usually too fearful and impatient in adversity, and even weaken their husbands, making them timid, impatient and wretched, as Job's wife did to Job. Moreover, since superstition is a feminine failing alone, and therefore is often thrown into alarm over trifles (fearing where there is no danger, and believing what is superstitious and least to be believed), he bids them, with that empty dread laid aside, to give themselves wholly to God. For the weakness of their sex makes women more suspicious and timid, and therefore more peevish, because they fear that if they submit to their husbands they will be treated more contemptuously by them. Peter wishes this fear removed, as if to say: gladly submit yourselves to the authority of your husbands, and let no fear hinder your obedience, as though your condition would be worse if you were patient.

units.la: Posset etiam magis generalis esse sententia, ne turbas domi concitent. Nam ut sunt ad consternationem proclives, sæpe ob rem frivolam tumultuantur, seque & familiam frustra turbant.
units.tr: The sentence could also be taken more generally: that they should not stir up disturbances at home. For since they are prone to consternation, they often make an uproar over a trifle, and vainly disturb both themselves and their household.

units.la: ʒ Cæterum Apostolus Petrus non modò uxores instruit, verumetiam vicissim quoque maritis, quid facto opus sit, præscribit. Sunt enim qui abutuntur authoritate sua, putantes, viri in uxorem imperium esse tyrannidem. Hi clamitant, Scriptum est, uxoris caput est maritus, 1. Corint.11. Equidem; sed numquid caput in reliquum corpus tumultuatur? An non magis cæteris membris servit omnibus? an non regit & consulit omnibus? Ita & maritus uxoris caput esse debet, id est, jucundus convictor, consultor, & vitæ dux commodus. Id si negligat, non magis titulo capitis dignus est, quàm patris nomine, qui in filios carnificem potius agit quàm patre: aut capitis quidem nomine dignus existit, sed ita, quemadmodum caput illud, quod, ut in fabulis est, vulpes inventum isto notavit dicterio, O quale sine cerebro caput! Petrus itaq; importunam quorundam refrenans audaciam & intemperiem, unico verbo istud negocium totum copleċtitur, & dicit, Viri cohabitate uxoribus cum scientia: id est, sind vernünfftig vnd verstendig ge- gen jhnen. Exigit enim à viris prudentiam, quæ opponitur affectibus, tyrannidi, irę, & morositati. Et sanè multæ ineptiæ viris ferendę sunt, devoranda multa tædia, & simul cavendum ne sua indulgentia stultitiam foveant: sed in pietate uxores instituant, errantesq; moderatè corrigant: quemadmodum Iob, cap. 2. uxorem suam sibi exprobrantem miserias suas, reprehendit, inquiens, Quasi una de stultis mulieribus locuta es: Si bona suscepimus de manu Domini, mala cur non sustineamus? Quare non est supervacua Petri admonitio, ut scienter cohabitent viri, nō stultè. Hæc verò scientia solida & justa facilè restinguit intemperiem animi: contrà verò, tyrannidis, arrogantiæ & injuriarum causa est barbaries illa quæ nihil rectè finit sapere, imprudentia adeoq; stultitia & stupiditas, quæ facit ne ulla quidem beneficia agnoscamus, imò ne nos quidè noverimus amplius. Alii illud συνοικᾶν κατὰ γνῶσιν[?] ita exponunt, quasi Petrus dicere velit: Vos viri cohabitate uxoribus nō simpliciter, sed secundū scientiam, id est, non secundū passiones & sensum, tantummodo voluptatis causa (ut septem primi mariti Sarræ, quam postea in uxorem duxit Tobias) nihil discernentes inter uxorem & meretricem: nam sic & bestiæ cohabitant, & gentes, quæ non noverunt Deum, 1. Thef. 4.
units.tr: Yet the Apostle Peter does not only instruct wives; in turn he also prescribes to husbands what must be done. For there are those who abuse their authority, thinking that a husband's rule over his wife is tyranny. These men cry out, "It is written: the husband is the head of the wife" (1 Cor. 11). Indeed; but does the head rage against the rest of the body? Does it not rather serve all the other members? Does it not rule and counsel all of them? So too a husband ought to be his wife's head, that is, a pleasant companion, counsellor and sound guide of life. If he neglects this, he is no more worthy of the title of head than of the name of father, who acts more like an executioner than a father toward his sons. Or, if he does deserve the name of head, it is in the way that the head in the fable was described by the fox, who, seeing it, made that jibe: "O what a head without a brain!" Peter, therefore, restraining the unruly audacity and intemperance of some, sums up this whole matter in a single word and says: husbands, live with your wives with knowledge, that is, be reasonable and understanding toward them. For he requires of husbands prudence, which is opposed to passions, tyranny, anger and peevishness. Indeed many follies must be borne by husbands, much tedium must be swallowed, and at the same time care must be taken lest by their indulgence they foster foolishness. Rather, they should instruct their wives in piety and gently correct those who err, as Job, ch. 2, rebukes his wife, who reproached him for his miseries, saying: "You have spoken like one of the foolish women: if we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, why should we not endure evil?" Therefore Peter's admonition that husbands should live with their wives wisely, not foolishly, is not superfluous. This solid and just knowledge easily quenches intemperance of mind. On the contrary, the cause of tyranny, arrogance and injuries is that barbarism which allows nothing to be rightly understood, that imprudence, and hence folly and stupidity, which makes us recognise no benefits, indeed not even to know ourselves any longer. Others explain the phrase to live together according to knowledge [συνοικᾶν κατὰ γνῶσιν] as if Peter wished to say: you husbands, live with your wives not simply, but according to knowledge, that is, not according to passions and the senses, merely for the sake of pleasure (as the seven first husbands of Sarah did, whom Tobias afterwards married), discerning nothing between a wife and a harlot. For thus beasts live together, and the nations who do not know God, 1 Thess. 4.

units.la: Inspicite igitur uxores vestras non oculo concupiscentiæ, sed scientiæ ac cognitionis: scitote illas quoque esse & Dei vasa instrumentáve, & Dei filias hæredesque. Oecumenius duplicem interpretationem affert, inquiens: Viri in cognitione cohabitantes, hoc est, experimento discentes fœmineam levitatem ac vecordiam in omnibus ac lubricitatem in pusillanimitate, patientes estote erga illas, non exactè rationem repetentes eorum, quæ circa familiam tradita illis erant in custodiam. Hoc autem, quo liberalius perseverent in largiendo erga pauperes, admonet viros ne sint exacti disquisitores. Mihi tamen profundius aliquid videtur per hoc inducere, & venustius ac castius, quā Paulus innuere de actu conjugali. Siquidè Paulus apertè clamat, 1. Cor. 7. Ne fraudetis invicem, nisi si quid ex consensu, &c. hic autem magis pudicè, ut diximus, cognitionem dicens, & per hoc rem ipsam designans, admonet, quò magis ad hoc lubricus fit sexus muliebris, ne per abjurgatione cum asperitate ab ipsis discedant, sed primum quidem clementer eis utantur tanquam imbecillioribus: deinde suadeant, ut cum aliqua parcitate abstinentiam à talibus suscipiant, &c. Hæc ille.
units.tr: Therefore look upon your wives not with the eye of lust, but with knowledge and understanding. Know that they too are vessels and instruments of God, and daughters and heirs of God. Oecumenius offers a double interpretation, saying: "Husbands, living together in knowledge, that is, learning by experience the feminine lightness and folly in all things and the wantonness that goes with timidity, be patient with them, not demanding a strict account of the things entrusted to them for keeping in the household." He adds that this admonishes husbands not to be exacting investigators, so that wives may persevere more generously in giving to the poor. Yet it seems to me that Peter is here hinting at something deeper, and more graceful and chaste, than Paul's reference to the marital act. For Paul plainly says, "Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by consent," and so on (1 Cor. 7). Here Peter, speaking more modestly, as we said, calls it "knowledge" and by this word indicates the act itself. He admonishes that the female sex, being so prone to slipping, should not be dismissed harshly or with roughness. Rather, husbands should first treat their wives gently, as the weaker sex, and then persuade them to undertake abstinence from such things with some restraint, and so on. So far he.

units.la: Sed videamus argumenta, quibus Petrus utitur, ut viris persuadeat, scienter, honestè & comiter tractandas esse uxores, inquì convenienti ipsis honore (quæ pars est ejus prudentiæ, de qua meminit) habendas. Nihil enim est quod magis dirimat vitę societatem quàm contemptus: nec possumus verè amare, nisi quos habemus in precio. Primum ait: Muliebri vasi, ut infirmiori, tribuentes honorem. Hoc argumentum ductum est ab imbecillitate muliebri, quam is ipse sexus fatetur apud Græcum vatem his verbis: [?]γυναικες[?] ἰσχὺν[?] ἀσθενέστερον[?] φυτόν[?]. Eandem innuit etiam Moses, quū testatur in adjutorium viri conditam esse mulierem. Huc etiam videtur facere, quòd apud Hebræos appellatione viri est littera Iod, quæ decem valet, qui numerus est perfectissimus: in nomine verò mulieris est tantùm He, quinarium numerum repræsentans, qui ad decem in proportione relatus, imperfectionem mulieris denotat. Propria enim appellatio viri est [?]אִישׁ[?] & mulieris [?]אִשָּׁה[?], quæ vox à masculino abiecto Iod, & repræsentante Dages defectum ejus, derivatur. Quamvis illud Dages secundum alios repræsentet literā Nun, ut dicant [?]אִשָּׁה[?] quasi [?]אנוש[?] à radice [?]אנש[?] quæ significat infirmitatē ac imbecillitatē: quod & ipsum appellationi fœminæ bene quadrat. Porrò vasis nomine quodvis organum in scriptura designatur: eidem quoque perusitatum, ut & homines, præsertim ipsa corpora, vocet vasa. Ergo vir organum & vas Dei est, sed fortius: unde & vir (à quo virtus) nominatus, teste Lactantio, quod in eo major vis est, quàm in fœmina: quæ quidem etiam vas & instrumentum est ipsius Dei, at imbecillius, non id corpore tantum, verumetiam animo, quo est infirmiore atque timidiore. Proinde ita tractanda est, sic cum ea agendū, ut possit ferre. Hic non secus res temperanda est, atque oportet & circa alia instrumenta, quibus ad efficiendum aliquid utimur: ut si quis acutum velit fervare cultellum[?], certè nullos lapides eo secuerit. Si igitur etiam mortua externaque vasa aut instrumenta, quantò sunt infirmiora, tantò sunt magis scienter cauteque contrectanda, qualia sunt vitrea vel testacea, ne frangantur: utique & uxori, tanquam sexui infirmo ac imprudenti, variisq; affectibus nimium abnoxio, nimia rigiditate, importunitate & imprudentia, aut contrà etiā nimis remissa lentitudine negligentiaque regiminis, non est conversandum. Sic Paulus Roman.12.& 1.Corinth.12. ait, Infirmiora membra (quæ plerunque omnium utilissima magisq; necessaria sunt cæteris) tantò magis honoranda foveda-q; esse. Nec mihi dicas (inquit Theophyl.in cap.5.ad Ephef.)Hunc & hunc [?]defe &ctum habet uxor mea. Nam & tu in carne [?]tua defectus habes,veluti manum mutilam, pedem claudum, oculum strabum: sed minimè abscindis hæc, sed majore illa cura dignaris. Grave pondus uxorum est(ut Hieronymus scribit in cap. 19. Matth.) si excepta causa fornicationis eas dimittere non licet. Quid enim si temulenta fuerit, si iracunda, si malis moribus, si luxuriosa, si gulosa, si vaga, si jurgatrix, si maledica, tenéda [?]erit istiusmodi [?]volumus,nolumus, sustinenda est. Cū enim liberi essemus, voluntarie nos subjecimus servituti. Ac quemadmodum facilius pueris ignoscimus, si quid per ætatis imperitiam delinquunt: ita sexus infirmitas facere debet, ne tam rigidi & austeri simus erga uxores. Porrò hac de re nulli possut certi canones dari, ut Lutherus scribit, Deus cujuslibet prudentiæ id committit, ut uxorem tractet cum ratione, ut ingenium cujuslibet requirit.
units.tr: But let us look at the arguments by which Peter urges husbands to treat their wives knowledgeably, honourably and courteously, and to hold them in the fitting honour (which is part of that prudence he mentions). For nothing dissolves the fellowship of life more than contempt, and we cannot truly love those whom we do not value. First he says: "Giving honour to the female vessel, as to the weaker." This argument is drawn from female weakness, which that sex itself confesses in the words of the Greek poet: "Women, a weaker plant in strength" [γυναῖκες ἰσχὺν ἀσθενέστερον φυτόν]. Moses also hints at the same thing when he records that the woman was made as a help for the man. This also seems to support the point that among the Hebrews the letter Yod, which has the value of ten, the most perfect number, belongs to the name of man, while the name of woman has only He, which represents the number five. Related to ten, five denotes the imperfection of the woman. For the proper word for man is ['ish] [אִישׁ] and for woman ['ishah] [אִשָּׁה], and the latter word is derived from the masculine form with the Yod removed and a Dages standing in for its missing part. Some, however, say that this Dages represents the letter Nun, so that ['ishah] is as if it came from ['enosh] [אנוש], from the root [anash] [אנש], which signifies infirmity and weakness; and this too suits the name of woman well. Moreover, in Scripture any instrument is designated by the word "vessel," and it is also a common usage to call men, especially their bodies, vessels. Man, then, is an instrument and vessel of God, but a stronger one; and so man (from whom virtue is named) is called vir, as Lactantius testifies, because there is greater force in him than in woman. Woman too is a vessel and instrument of God Himself, but a weaker one, not only in body but also in mind, in which she is more feeble and timid. Therefore she must be treated and dealt with in such a way that she can bear it. Here the matter must be handled no differently than with other instruments that we use to accomplish something. If someone wishes to keep a sharp knife, he will certainly not cut with it on stones. If inanimate and external vessels or instruments, the weaker they are, must be handled all the more knowingly and cautiously, such as glass or earthenware vessels, so that they are not broken, then certainly a wife, as the weak and imprudent sex, too prone to various passions, must not be dealt with by excessive rigidity, harshness and imprudence, nor on the other hand by excessive laxity and neglect in governing. So Paul says in Romans 12 and 1 Corinthians 12 that the weaker members (which are often the most useful and most necessary to the rest) ought to be honoured and cherished all the more. Do not say to me, says Theophylact on Ephesians 5, "My wife has this or that defect." For you too have defects in your flesh: a maimed hand, a lame foot, a squinting eye. But you do not cut these off; rather you give them greater care. The burden of wives is heavy (as Jerome writes on Matthew 19) if it is not permitted to dismiss them, except for the cause of fornication. For what if she is drunken, if angry, if of bad morals, if lustful, if gluttonous, if wandering, if quarrelsome, if slanderous? She must be kept, whether we want it or not, and must be borne. For when we were free, we voluntarily made ourselves subject to servitude. And just as we more easily pardon children when they offend through inexperience of age, so the weakness of the sex ought to make us not so rigid and severe towards our wives. Moreover, as Luther writes, no fixed rules can be given on this matter; God entrusts it to the prudence of each man, that he should treat his wife reasonably, as the nature of each requires.

units.la: Sequitur alterum argumentum,quod ducit Petrus à dignitate mulierum,seu honore quo dignatur eas Deus. Ait enim:Tanquam etiam cohæredibus gratiæ vitæ,vel ut alii legunt, ut multiplicis beneficii & vitæ cohæredes. Propter communem ergo illum herum aut patrem,communemq; dignitatem & communem spem æternæ beatitatis,in honore & precio habendæ sunt uxores, & familiarius tractandæ. Etsi enim peccavit mulier, & peccatum in mundum induxit: tamen sanguine Christi mundata est: in quo omnes unus sumus, 1. Tim. 2. Gal. 3. Non est ergo quod ob sexu contemnat uxorem, aut lapsum imputet maritus. Tametsi autem aliquę mulieres à spe salutis alienæ sunt, quia tamen ipsis non minus ac viris à Domino offertur, hoc ad sexus honorem sufficit.
units.tr: There follows the second argument, which Peter draws from the dignity of women, or the honour with which God regards them. For he says: "As also fellow-heirs of the grace of life," or as others read it, "as heirs of the manifold gift and of life." Therefore, because of that common Lord or Father, and their common dignity and common hope of eternal blessedness, wives are to be held in honour and esteem, and treated more familiarly. For although the woman sinned, and brought sin into the world, yet she has been cleansed by the blood of Christ, in whom we are all one (1 Tim. 2; Gal. 3). There is therefore no reason for a husband to despise his wife because of her sex, or to impute to her a fall. And although some women are estranged from the hope of salvation, yet, since it is offered to them by the Lord no less than to men, this is enough to establish the honour of the sex.

units.la: Tertium argumentū ab utili trahitur: quia dicit, Ne interrumpantur aut impediantur preces vestræ. Quid sibi vult D. Petrus his verbis? Hoc, si nolis cū ratione omnia, sed ut libuerit importunè & cōmotè agere, ac præfractus semper cuncta pro tuo arbitrio exigere, proq; levisimis rebus tragœdiam excitare: tum uxor quoq; suos morbos habeat, & neuter alteri aliquid condonare aut concedere sustineat, vel boni consulere, quod sibi ab altero facto fuerit: haud poteritis precari & dicere: Remitte nobis debita nostra, sicut & nos remittimus. Hac precatione contra dæmonem nobis pugnandum est: ideo oportet, ut inter nos coveniat. Nam rite invocari Deus nequit, nisi tranquillis ac sedatis animis. Ubi jurgia, lites, verbera: ibi nullę preces purę. Proinde maxima concordia inter maritū & uxorem fovenda est. Hos enim alloquitur hic Petrus, dum jubet concordes esse, ut simul Deum uno animo precetur. Origenes lib 8. in Epist. ad Rom. orationes sanctorum conjugum hostias vocat Deo placentes. His bona cojugii, liberi, domus, impetratur, Genef.17.30. 1. Regum 1. Tob. 6. Luc.i; Pfalm.61. Sed generalis hinc doctrina colligi potest, neminem ad Deum accedere posse,nisi qui fratribus suis conjunctus est,Matthaei 5. 6. Marc.11. Ergo sicuti haec ratio domesticas omnes turbas & jurgia debet componere, ut in singulis familiis invocetur Deus: ita in communi omnium vita ad rixas omnes cohibendas quasi frænum esse debet. Sumus enim plus quàm insani,si viam nobis ad invocandum Deum scientes ac volentes præcludimus: quum sit hoc unicum salutis nostræ asylum. O Iesu Christe fili Dei unigenite, qui vis cunctos homines salvos fieri, & jubes nos invocare nomen tuum, da quod jubes, ac doce nos orare,& effunde super nos spiritum gratiæ & precum, ut tum precari, tum salvari possimus in nomine tuo sancto & salutifero,
units.tr: The third argument is drawn from usefulness, since he says: "So that your prayers may not be interrupted or hindered." What does Peter mean by these words? This: if you do not wish to act reasonably in all things, but to act unreasonably and with agitation as you please, and to be always stubborn, demanding everything according to your own judgment, and stirring up a tragedy over the lightest matters; if the wife too has her own faults, and neither party can bear to grant or concede anything to the other, or take in good part what has been done to him by the other, then you will not be able to pray and say: "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive." We must fight against the devil by this prayer, and therefore it is necessary that we agree among ourselves. For God cannot be invoked properly except with tranquil and calm minds. Where there are quarrels, strife and blows, there are no pure prayers. Therefore the greatest concord must be cherished between husband and wife. For Peter addresses these very persons here, when he bids them be of one mind, so that they may pray to God with one soul. Origen, in book 8 on the Epistle to the Romans, calls the prayers of holy spouses sacrifices pleasing to God. By these prayers the blessings of marriage, children and household are obtained (Gen. 17; 1 Kings 1; Tob. 6; Luke 1; Ps. 61). But a general doctrine may be gathered from this: no one can approach God unless he is joined to his brothers (Matt. 5; Mark 11). Therefore, just as this principle ought to settle all domestic disturbances and quarrels, so that God may be invoked in each household, so in the common life of all it ought to be like a bridle for restraining all brawls. For we are more than mad if, knowingly and willingly, we shut ourselves off from the way to invoke God, since this is the one refuge of our salvation. O Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son of God, who wish all men to be saved and bid us call upon your name, grant what you command, teach us to pray, and pour out upon us the spirit of grace and of prayers, so that we may both pray and be saved in your holy and saving name. Amen.

units.la: Amen Amen.:
units.tr: Amen, amen.

units.la: Sequuntur porrò XL themata ejufdem argumenti cum LX præcedentibus partim ex vetere, partim ex novo Testamento deprompta: sicuti conversa leguntur in Latinum à M. Sebastiano Castalione: in quo legendo majorem fe percipere fructum olim dicebat Joannes Checus, vir doctus, & equestris ordinis (teste Christophoro Carleilo Anglo) quàm in evolvendis omnium scriptorum commentariis.
units.tr: Moreover, there follow forty themes of the same subject, drawn partly from the Old Testament and partly from the New, to accompany the sixty preceding ones; they are read in the Latin rendering of Master Sebastian Castellio. Joannes Checus, a learned man of the equestrian order (according to Christopher Carleill, an Englishman), used to say that he derived greater fruit from reading this than from working through the commentaries of all the writers.

units.la: THEMA LXI.
units.tr: THEME LXI.

units.la: ADamus autem cum Eva uxorem habuit, quæ gravida facta Cainum peperit: sic ideo nominatum, quod illa eum enixa dixisset, Adepta sum virum à Jova. Peperit praterea ejus germanum Abelem. Hic Abelopilio, Cainus fuit agricola. Aliquanto tempore post, cum Jova munus libavisset Cainus de terra frugibus: Abel autem de pecorum suorum primigenis, & max.mè[?] optimis, respexit Jova Abelem, & ejus munus: Cainum,ejusq; munus non respexit, quam rem ita acerbè tulit Cainus, ut ei facies sublabaretur. Genes. 4.
units.tr: Adam also had a wife, Eve, who became pregnant and bore Cain. He was so named because she said at his birth, "I have gotten a man from Jehovah." She also bore his brother Abel. Abel was a shepherd, Cain a farmer. Some time later, when Cain offered Jehovah a gift of the fruits of the earth, and Abel offered the firstlings of his flocks, the best of them, Jehovah looked upon Abel and his gift but did not look upon Cain and his gift. Cain took this so bitterly that his face fell. Gen. 4.

units.la: LXII.
units.tr: LXII.

units.la: Judas autem aliquando à fratribus suis digressus, recepit se ad quendam Adulamitam nomine Hiram:ubi cùm vidisset Chananæi cujusdam [?] nomine Suæ filiam, eam duxit. & ex ejus congressu filium iustulit, quem Erem nomine appellavit. Deinde alterum, quæ ipsa Onanem nuncupavit. Tertium item, quem Selam vocavit, cujus in nativitate erat ipse Chezibi. Eri autem, qui erat natu maximus, Thamarem quandam nomine in matrimonium tradidit. Sed Er Jovæ displicuit, itaque Jova eum interfecit. & Judas Onani imperavit, ut cum fratris uxore congrederetur, & suam fratris iurefaceret, fratriq; prolem suscitaret. Sed Onan, qui sciret non suam futuram esse prolem, cum fratris uxore rem habiturus, semen in terram effundebat, ne fratrem progenie donaret. Quo facto offensus Jova, eum quoque necavit: Tum Judas Thamarem nurum suam jußit vi-duam domi paterna manere, donec Iudæ filius Sela adolevisset, veritus ne & is moreretur sicut ejus fratres. Igitur Thamar domum paternam se recepit, ibiq; fuit. Genes 38.
units.tr: Judah, having once separated from his brothers, went to live with a certain Adullamite named Hirah. There he saw the daughter of a certain Canaanite named Shua, and took her as his wife. From their union he begot a son whom he named Er, then a second, whom she herself named Onan, and a third, whom he called Shelah, at whose birth he himself was at Chezib. Judah gave a woman named Tamar in marriage to Er, the eldest. But Er displeased Jehovah, so Jehovah killed him. Judah then ordered Onan to go in to his brother's wife, to perform the duty of a brother-in-law and raise up offspring for his brother. But Onan, knowing that the child would not be his own, when he was to have relations with his brother's wife, spilled his seed on the ground, so as not to give his brother offspring. Offended by this deed, Jehovah killed him too. Then Judah ordered his daughter-in-law Tamar to remain a widow in her father's house until his son Shelah grew up, fearing that he too might die like his brothers. So Tamar withdrew to her father's house and stayed there. Gen. 38.

units.la: LXIII.
units.tr: LXIII.

units.la: Tum Moses inde digressus, ad Iethronem socerum suum reversus est, & ab eo petivit, ut sibi ad consanguineos suos, qui essent in Aegypto, redire liceret, & providere, utrum adhuc viverent: quem Iethro cum bona pace dimisit. Moses igitur à Iova in Madiania admonitus, ut Aegyptum repeteret (mortuos enim esse omnes illos qui ejus vitam petebant) uxorē suam adhibet, & filios, eisq; in asinum illatis, in Aegyptum redire contendit, divinam illam virgam secum ferens. E-xodi 4.
units.tr: Then Moses departed from there and returned to his father-in-law Jethro, and asked him whether he might go back to his kinsmen who were in Egypt, and see whether they were still alive: Jethro let him go in peace. Moses, therefore, admonished by Jehovah in Midian to return to Egypt (for all those who sought his life were dead), took his wife and sons, set them on a donkey, and hurried toward Egypt, carrying that divine staff with him. Exod. 4.

units.la: LXIIII.
units.tr: LXIIII.

units.la: Ad consanguineum suum ne quis vestrum accedito, ut ejus naturam detegat. Hæc ego Iova, Patris aut matris tua naturam ne detegito: mater tua est, ejus naturam ne detegito. Nouercæ tuæ naturam ne detegito: nam patris natura est. Sororis tua sive ex patre, sive ex matre, sive domi, sive foris nata, naturam ne detegito. Neptis tua, tum ex filio, tum ex filia, naturam ne detegito: nam natura tua est. Filiæ nouercæ tuæ, patre tuo nata, naturam ne detegito: soror tua est.
units.tr: Let none of you approach a close relative to uncover that person's nakedness. I am Jehovah. Do not uncover the nakedness of your father or your mother; she is your mother, do not uncover her nakedness. Do not uncover the nakedness of your stepmother, for it is your father's nakedness. Do not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether she is born of your father or of your mother, whether born at home or abroad. Do not uncover the nakedness of your granddaughter, whether through your son or through your daughter, for it is your own nakedness. Do not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your stepmother, born to your father; she is your sister.

units.la: Amitæ tuæ naturam ne detegito, nam paternæ consanguinitatis est: ejus naturam ne detegito.
units.tr: Do not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is of your father's blood; do not uncover her nakedness.

units.la: Matertera tua naturam ne detegito, nam maternæ confanguinitatis est. Tui ex patre avunculi naturam ne detegito, id est, ad ejus uxorem ne accedito, amita tua est. Nurus tuæ naturam ne detegito: filii tui uxor est, ejus natura ne detegito: Vxoris fratris tui naturam ne detegito: fratris tui natura est. Cum muliere, & cum ejusdem filia rem ne habeto. Tui privigni aut privignæ filiam ne ducito, ut cum ea rem habeas: nam L. ejus H. consanguineæ sunt, incestus est. Vxoris sororem, ea vivente ne ducito, ut cum ea rem habeas: quæ res uxori dolorem faciat.
units.tr: Do not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is of your mother's blood. Do not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, that is, do not approach his wife; she is your aunt. Do not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife, do not uncover her nakedness. Do not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife; it is your brother's nakedness. Do not have relations with a woman and with her daughter. Do not take the daughter of your stepson or stepdaughter to have relations with her, for they are of your own blood; it is incest. Do not take your wife's sister while your wife is living, to have relations with her, for this would cause your wife grief.

units.la: Ad mulierem menstruis laborantem ne accedito, ut cum ea rem habeas. Alterius uxori stuprum & corruptelam ne inferto. Progeniem tuam ne dato traijciendam Molocho, neve meum Jova Dei tui nomen profanato. Marem ne fœmineo concubitu comprimito: nefas est. Ne te ullius bestiæ concubitu contaminato, neve mulier bestiæ prostrato ad coeundum: flagitium est. Ne vos ullo horum scelerum contaminatote. Nam his omnibus sese contaminarunt gentes, quas ego vobis abigo. Itaque si polluta terra scelera hujusmodi pœnis persequor, ut incolas terra suos evomat. Levit. 18.
units.tr: Do not approach a woman who is suffering her menstrual period, to have relations with her. Do not inflict adultery or corruption on another man's wife. Do not give your offspring to be passed through the fire to Molech, nor profane the name of Jehovah your God. Do not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination. Do not defile yourself with the intercourse of any beast, nor let a woman offer herself to a beast to mate with it; it is a perversion. Do not defile yourselves with any of these crimes, for by all these things the nations whom I drive out before you have defiled themselves. So if the land is polluted, I punish such crimes, so that the land vomits out its inhabitants. Lev. 18.

units.la: LXV.
units.tr: LXV.

units.la: Si qua hominis sacerdotis filia scortari ausa fuerit, patrem suum profanavit, igni cremator. Levit.21.
units.tr: If the daughter of any priest has dared to play the harlot, she has profaned her father; she shall be burned with fire. Lev. 21.

units.la: LXVI.
units.tr: LXVI.

units.la: Tum Moses Jsraelitis ex Jovæ mandato præcepit, in hunc modum: Recte dicunt Josephi natorum tribules, atque hoc est, quod Jova circa Salphaadi filias præcipit: Suo arbitratu nubunto, dum in tri[?]bus paterna gentem nubant. Ita non transferetur Israelitarum hæreditas de tribu in tribum, dum quisque in sua patria tribus hæreditate hærebit. Atque omnis filia hæres instituta, ex quacunque Israelitarum tribuum, alicui tribui suo nuptum locetur, ut Israelitarum quisque paternas hæreditates possideant, ne hæreditates ex aliis in alias tribus transeant, dum Israelitarum quisque in sua tribu hæreditate hærebit. Numeri 36.
units.tr: Then Moses, by Jehovah's command, instructed the Israelites in this manner: "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speak rightly. This is what Jehovah commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: let them marry whom they choose, provided they marry within the families of their father's tribe. Thus the inheritance of the Israelites will not pass from tribe to tribe, since each will cling to the inheritance of his own tribe. Every daughter who inherits, from whatever tribe of the Israelites, shall be given in marriage to a man of her own tribe, so that each Israelite may keep his fathers' inheritance, and inheritances may not pass from one tribe to another, since each Israelite will cling to the inheritance of his own tribe. Num. 36.

units.la: LXVII.
units.tr: LXVII.

units.la: Ne cum eis (gentibus) fœdus initote: néve earum miserti[?] fueritis: néve affinitatem cum eis contrahitote, aut filias vestras illorum filiis locando, aut illorum filias vestris filiis conjungendo. Alioqui filios vestros à Iova ad peregrinorum deorum cultum abducent: ita fiet, ut iratus Iova vos brevi perdat. Deuteron.7.
units.tr: Make no covenant with those nations, nor show them mercy, nor contract marriage with them, either by giving your daughters to their sons or by taking their daughters for your sons. Otherwise they will turn your sons away from Jehovah to the worship of foreign gods, and so Jehovah in anger will soon destroy you. Deut. 7.

units.la: LXVIII.
units.tr: LXVIII.

units.la: Si quis deprehensus fuerit concubuisse cum fœmina maritum habente, ambo juxtà moriuntor, tum vir qui fœminam constuprarit, tum fœmina: idq; nefas ex
units.tr: If anyone is caught lying with a woman who has a husband, both shall be put to death at once, both the man who violated the woman and the woman herself; and this wickedness you shall remove from

units.la: Israelitis tollitote. Si quis puellam virginem viro pastam nactus in oppido copresserit, ambos ad illius oppidi portam eductos lapidatote, & necatote puellam, quia in oppido non clamaverit: virum, quia alterius uxorem subegerit: id nefas de medio vestrum tollitote. Sin autem ruri puellam desponsatam nactus vir, ei vim intulerit, eamq; compresserit, mor tor vir ille tantum, qui eam compressit: puella autem nihil nocetote, neq; enim in capitali crimine est: hoc enim perinde est, ac si quis alterū aggressus vita privet. Nam ruri eam reperit, neque clamanti puella desponsa adfuit, qui succurreret. Si quis puellam virgine non desponsam nactus, ei stupru intulerit, & deprehensi fuerint, vir ille patri puellae quinquaginta argenteos dato, eamq; uxorem habeto, quod eam subegerit, neq; unquam repudiare liceto. Deuter.22.
units.tr: the Israelites. If anyone finds a virgin girl betrothed to a husband in a town and lies with her, lead both of them to the gate of that town and stone them: the girl, because she did not cry out in the town, and the man, because he has forced another man's wife. Remove this wickedness from among you. But if a man finds a betrothed girl in the countryside, forces her, and lies with her, only that man shall die who lay with her; do nothing to the girl, for she is not guilty of a capital crime. This is just as if someone should attack another and take his life. For he found her in the open country, and though the betrothed girl cried out, there was no one present to help her. If anyone finds a virgin who is not betrothed, seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered, the man shall give fifty silver pieces to the girl's father, and she shall be his wife, because he has violated her; he may never divorce her. Deut. 22.

units.la: LXIX.
units.tr: LXIX.

units.la: Si quis uxorem duxerit, fœminamq; fecerit, si contigerit eam illi non placere, quòd aliquid in ea offenderit inhonestum,scribito et libellum divortii, eumq; illi in manum dato,& eam e domo sua dimittito. Quod si ex illius domo egressam alteri nubere contigerit,si ille alter eam invisam habebit,scribito ei libellum divortii, eumq; illi in manum dato, atq; eam ex domo sua dimittito. Aut si decefferit vir ille, qui secundus eam duxerit, ne esto potestas marito priori, qui eam repudiaverit, eam iterato in matrimonium ducere, postquam illa polluta est (nam id quidem Iova habetur nefarium) ne terram, quam vobis possidendam vester Deus Iova dat, polluatis. Cùm quis uxorem novam duxerit, ne militato, nulliq; muneri obnoxius, immunis domi esto unum annum, & cum ducta uxore laetator.
units.tr: If a man has taken a wife and has been intimate with her, and it then happens that she does not please him, because he has found something indecent in her, let him write her a bill of divorce, put it into her hand, and send her out of his house. And if, after she has left his house, she marries another man, and that second husband comes to hate her, let him write her a bill of divorce, put it into her hand, and send her out of his house. Or if that second husband, who took her as his wife, dies, the first husband, who sent her away, shall not have the power to take her again as his wife after she has been defiled (for that is held to be an abomination before Iova), so that you do not pollute the land which your God Iova gives you to possess. When a man has taken a new wife, he shall not go to war, nor be bound to any public duty; he shall be free at home for one year and rejoice with the wife he has taken. Deuteronomy 24.

units.la: Deuteron.24.
units.tr: Deuteronomy 24.

units.la: LXX.
units.tr: The Septuagint.

units.la: Quamobrem curate diligenter, si salvi esse vultis, ut Iovam Deum vestrum ametis. Nam si mutati, cum reliquis his nationibus apud vos relictis cohaseritis, cumq; eis connubia miscueritis, & mutuam necessitudinem habueritis, scitote Iovam Deum vestrum non jam vobis istas omnes nationes expulsurum esse. Sed eas vobis fore tanq̄ decipulam quandam & obicem, & laterum stimulum, & oculos spinas, eosq;, ut auferamini ex hac tam bona terra, vobis à Iova Deo vestro data. Iosu.23.
units.tr: Therefore take diligent care, if you wish to be safe, to love Iova your God. For if you turn aside and cleave to the remaining nations left among you, and make marriages with them, and enter into mutual alliance, know that Iova your God will no longer drive out all these nations before you. But they will be to you a snare and a trap, a whip at your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this very good land given to you by Iova your God. Joshua 23.

units.la: LXXI.
units.tr: LXXI.

units.la: Aliquanto post, messis tritici tempore Samson visit uxorem suam, caprum ferens, & ad eam admitti se in cubiculū postulat. Sed mulieris pater eum prohibuit, dicens sese, cum eam illi invisam esse putaret, eam ejus familiari locasse: esse tamen ei sororem, ut natu minorem, sic forma venustiorem, eam pro illa duceret.
units.tr: Some time later, at the season of the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife, bringing a young goat, and he asked to be admitted to her room. But the woman's father forbade him, saying that, since he thought she was hateful to him, he had given her to his companion; yet she had a younger sister, who was more beautiful, and he might take her instead.

units.la: Tum Samson apud illos præfatus, sese tum non esse Palæstinis injuriam facturum, si eus[?] malum inferret, discedit: captisq; trecentis vulpibus, & earum caudis inter se obversis, singulas faces binis caudis interponit, ijsq; incensis, vulpes in Palæstin. segetes laxat, atque ita & metas, & segetes, & vineas, & oliveta combussit. Hujus facinoris authorem Palastini cum Samsone esse Thamnathensis illius generum, inquirendo comperissent, quoniam ille ereptam ei uxorem ejus familiari dedisset, invadunt illos, & mulierem, ejusq; patrem igni comburunt. Iudicum 15.
units.tr: Then Samson, having said beforehand among them that he would not then be doing wrong to the Philistines if he inflicted harm on them, departed. He took three hundred foxes, turned their tails toward each other, put a torch between each pair of tails, and when these were lit, let the foxes loose into the Philistine crops; so he burned the sheaves and standing grain, the vineyards and the olive groves. When the Philistines discovered by inquiry that the author of this crime was Samson, son-in-law of the Timnite, because he had given his wife to his companion after taking her away from him, they attacked them and burned the woman and her father with fire. Judges 15.

units.la: LXXII.
units.tr: LXXII.

units.la: Per eadem tempora, quibus nullus in Israelitis rex erat, Levita quidā in lateribus montis Ephraimitarū peregrinans, uxorem duxerat concubinam à Bethlehema Iudaeae: quae concubina cum parum pudica erga illum fuisset, discessit ab eo, domum patris sui, Bethlehemam Iudaeae. Ibi cum per quatuor menses fuisset, secutus est eam maritus, ut eam blandis illectam verbis reduceret, famulū secum & par asinorum ducens.
units.tr: In those times, when there was no king over Israel, a certain Levite, travelling on the slopes of the mountain of the Ephraimites, had taken as his wife a concubine from Bethlehem of Judah. This concubine, not being chaste toward him, left him and went back to her father's house in Bethlehem of Judah. When she had been there four months, her husband followed her, intending to win her back with flattering words, taking with him a servant and a pair of asses.

units.la: Atq; illa eum domum sui patris introduxit, qui puellae pater, hominis adventu delectatus, generi retinuit, secumq; triduo per convivia & noctes habuit.
units.tr: She brought him into her father's house. The girl's father, delighted at the man's arrival, kept his son-in-law, and he stayed with him three days, with feasting and nights.

units.la: Quarto die mane cum gener discessum pararet, persuasit socer ut vires cibo recrearet ante discessum.
units.tr: On the fourth morning, when the son-in-law was making ready to leave, the father-in-law persuaded him to refresh his strength with food before he set out.

units.la: Deinde cum ambo accubuissent, cibumq; unà sumpsisset, suadebat homini socer, ut ibi pernoctare, animumq; recreare vellet, &c. Iudic. 19.
units.tr: Then, when both had reclined and had eaten together, the father-in-law urged the man to stay the night there and cheer his spirits, etc. Judges 19.

units.la: LXXIII.
units.tr: LXXIII.

units.la: Qua tempestate praesides procurabat, vir quidam à Bethlehema Iudæa, orta in finibus illis fame profectus est ad peregrinandum in agrū Moabiticum, unà cum sua coniuge, duobusq; filiis. Viri nomen erat Elimelechus, mulieris Noemi: duorum filiorū Mahalon & Chelion, Ephratæi, ex Bethlehema Iudæae. His in agrum Moabiticum profectis, ibiq; degentibus, moritur Elimelechus, uxore Noemi & duob. filiis superstitibus. Filii uxores Moabitidas duxerunt, quarū uni Orpha, alteri Rhuta nomen fuit: atq; illic circiter decem annos commorati, moriuntur & ipsi ambo, Mahalon, & Chelion. Mulier autē duobus natis & viro superstes, cum apud Moabitas agens, audivisset Iovam suis subvenisse, eisq; annonam levasse, illinc digressa, comitibus duabus nuribus, in Iudæam reverti contendit, easq; in itinere sic admonuit: Revertimini traque in suæ matris domum: rependat vobis Iova pietatem, qua tum erga mortuos, tum erga me usæ estis. Faxit Iova ut quietem suum utraque apud maritum nanciscamini[?]. Hæc cùm locuta, eas deoscularetur, illa in lachrymas erumpentes, affirmabant, sese cum ipsa ad ejus populares esse reversuras. Sed Noemis eas ita hortata est: Revertimini meæ filiolæ, cur me comitemini? Nunquid ego adhuc in utero gesto filios, qui vobis futuri sint viri? Revertimini meæ filiolæ, discedite: nam ego quidè grandior sum, quàm ut sim apta viro. Quod si maximè spem esse putarem, virōq; vel in proximam noctem tradita, filios gignerem, an estis expectatura, donec adoleverint, & tam diu sine viris duratura? Non ita, meæ filiæ. Equidem valde vestra causa doleo, sed me Iova manus urget. Tum illa ploratum integrant, & Orphasocrum suam osculata, ei valedicit. At Rutha cum ea harebat, &c. Ruth.I.
units.tr: In the time when judges ruled, a certain man from Bethlehem of Judah, because a famine had arisen in those regions, set out with his wife and two sons to sojourn in the land of Moab. The man's name was Elimelech, the woman's Naomi; the two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. When they had gone into the land of Moab and were living there, Elimelech died, leaving Naomi his wife and the two sons alive. The sons took Moabite wives, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. After they had lived there about ten years, both Mahlon and Chilion also died. The woman, bereaved of her two sons and her husband, and staying among the Moabites, heard that Iova had visited his people and given them food. So she departed from there, with her two daughters-in-law as companions, and set out to return to Judah. On the way she spoke to them thus: "Go back, each of you, to her mother's house. May Iova repay you with the kindness you have shown both to the dead and to me. May Iova grant that each of you find rest with a husband." When she had said this and kissed them, they broke into weeping and declared that they would return with her to her people. But Naomi urged them thus: "Go back, my daughters; why do you come with me? Do I still carry sons in my womb who could be husbands for you? Go back, my daughters, depart; for I am too old to be fit for a husband. Even if I thought there were any hope, and I were given to a husband this very night and bore sons, would you wait until they grew up, and remain so long without husbands? No, my daughters. I grieve greatly on your account, but the hand of Iova is heavy upon me." Then they wept again; Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and bade her farewell. But Ruth clung to her, etc. Ruth 1.

units.la: LXXIII.
units.tr: LXXIII.

units.la: Interea dum apud socrum manet, Noemis cum ea sic locuta est: Requiem tibi, mea filia, volo quærere, ut benefit tibi: Est Boozus cognatus noster, cum cuius tu puellis fuisti. qui quidem hordeum in area sub noctem ventilaturus est. Tu lava & unge te, ornatuq; adhibito, ad aream descende: sed noli te homini aperire, donec cibum jam, potionemq; sumpserit. Cumq; discedet cubitum, observato locum in quo cubabit, eumq; adito, & detectis ejus pedibus cubato. Ipse tibi quid facto sit opus ostendet. Et illa: Quicquid tu mihi mandas, exequar. Hac locuta descendit ad aream, & omne socrus mandatum executa est. Cumq; Boozus cibo & potione exhilaratus, ad finem metæ cubitum ivisset, illa pedetentim accessit, illiusq; detectis pedibus, accubuit. Media nocte exterritus homo, tactu explorat, & mulierem animadvertens sibi ad pedes adjacentem, inquit: Qua tu es? cui illa: Ego sum Rutha, inquit, ancilla tua, quæ peto ut tu in me gremium tuum exporrigas: nam propinquus es. Et Boozus: Jovam tibi, filia, opto propitium, inquit: tu priorem pietatem hac posteriore superasti, quæ juvenes sive pauperes sive divites secuta non sis. Quamobrem bonō animo, filia: quicquid postulas, tibi faciam. Scit enim cuncta meorū popularium civitas, te mulierem esse virtute praeditam. Ruth 3.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while she remained with her mother-in-law, Naomi said to her: "My daughter, I want to find rest for you, so that it may go well with you. Boaz, our kinsman, with whose maidservants you have been, is going to winnow barley on the threshing floor tonight. Wash and anoint yourself, put on your finery, and go down to the threshing floor; but do not reveal yourself to the man until he has finished eating and drinking. When he goes to lie down, mark the place where he lies, go to him, uncover his feet, and lie down. He himself will show you what you must do." And she said, "Whatever you command me, I will do." Having said this, she went down to the threshing floor and carried out all her mother-in-law's instructions. When Boaz, cheered with food and drink, had gone to lie down at the end of the heap of grain, she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down. At midnight the man, startled, felt about, and noticing a woman lying at his feet, said: "Who are you?" She answered: "I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your garment over me, for you are a near kinsman." And Boaz said: "May Iova, daughter, be gracious to you. You have surpassed your former kindness with this later one, in not following young men, whether poor or rich. Therefore take heart, daughter; whatever you ask, I will do for you. For the whole city of my people knows that you are a woman of virtue. Ruth 3.

units.la: LXXV.
units.tr: LXXV.

units.la: Nabalis audita morte, David Iová[?] gratias egit, qui suam contumeliam in Nabalem animadvertisset, seque a scelere prohibuisset, et Nabalus scelus in ipsius caput retorsisset: misitque qui cum Abigaile de ea ad se in matrimonium ducenda agerent. Cum igitur Davidis servi ad Abigailem in Carmelū venissent, eiqué retulissent, se ad eam missos esse a David, quo eam uxorem duceret: surrexit illa, & honore demisse prabito[?], respondit, se illius esse servam, parata velut servorum eius lavare pedes. Deinde protinus proficiscitur, & asino insidens, comitantibus quinque pedissequis, nuncios Davidis subsequitur, illique nu-bit. 1.Reg.25.
units.tr: When Nabal's death was heard, David gave thanks to Iova, who had avenged the insult done to him by Nabal and had kept him from crime, and had turned Nabal's wickedness back on his own head. He then sent men to speak with Abigail about taking her as his wife. So when David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and told her that they had been sent to her by David, that she should become his wife, she rose, bowed low in respect, and replied that she was his servant, ready to wash the feet of his servants. Then at once she set out, mounted on an ass, attended by five maidservants, and followed David's messengers, and became his wife. 1 Samuel 25.

units.la: LXXVI.
units.tr: LXXVI.

units.la: Sed offensus Davidis facinore Iehova[?], misit ei Nathanè, qui eum aggressus est his verbis: Duo homines erant in quadi urbe,alter dives,alter pauper. Dives majorū minorumq; pecudum magnā copiam habebat. Pauper unam omnino habebat oviculā, à se emptam et enutrita, quæ u-nā cum ipso ejusq; filiis adoleverat, ejus cibo vescēs[?], ex ejus calice bibens, in ejus sinu quiescēs: breviter erat ei pro filia. Ad illum diuitē venit hospes quidam, quem accepturus ille, parsit de suis minoribus majoribus ve sumere pecoribus:& captā illam pauperis oviculā, hospiti mactavit. Hic David in homine magna ira percitus, Nathani sic dicit: Per Iovam immore[?] tale, morte dignus est istius autor facinoris, ovemq; quadruplo pensabit, qui istud cōmittere non dubitaverit. Et Nathan: Tu ille es, inquit. Ego te (inquit Iova Deus Israelitarū) regem in Israelitas unxi: ego te ab injuria Sauli defendi: tibi Domini tui domum, tibi domini tui uxores cōplectendas, tibi Israeliticam Iudaamq; stirpē dedi: alia atq; alia insuper daturus, si ea parum essent. Cur tu Iovam, contemptis ejus præceptis, scelere tuo offendisti? dum Uriam Hettæum ferro trucidati, ejusq; uxorem, eoper te Ammonitārum telis interfecto, in matrimonium duxisti. Itaque à domo tua nunquam abfuturum est bellum: quoniam tu contempto me, Vriae Hettaei uxorem tibi matrimonio copulasti. Scito, me tibi(inquit Iova) conflaturum esse malum domesticum, tuasq; coniuges in oculis tuis alteri traditurum, qui cum eis in hujus congrediatur conspectu solis. Tu quidem occulte fecisti: sed ego hoc coram omnibus Israelitis luce palam facturus sum. Tum David: Peccavi in Iovam, inquit. Et Nathan: Iova quoque remittit ille quidem tibi peccatum, neque morieris. Veruntamen, quoniam tu ista re Iovae inimicis maledicendi occasionem dedisti, filius, qui tibi natus est, morietur. 2. Regum 12.
units.tr: But Iova, offended by David's deed, sent Nathan to him, who confronted him with these words: "There were two men in a certain city, one rich and one poor. The rich man had a great number of flocks of larger and smaller cattle. The poor man had only one little ewe, which he had bought and raised, which had grown up along with him and his sons, eating of his food, drinking from his cup, resting in his bosom; it was to him like a daughter. A traveller came to the rich man, and he, wishing to entertain him, would not take from his own flocks, large or small, but seized the poor man's little ewe and slaughtered it for his guest." Then David, greatly enraged against the man, said to Nathan: "As Iova lives, the author of this deed deserves death, and he shall pay fourfold for the ewe, since he did not hesitate to do this." And Nathan said: "You are that man. I (says Iova, God of Israel) anointed you king over Israel; I defended you from the injury of Saul; I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives to embrace, and the house of Israel and Judah; and I would have given you more besides, if these had been too few. Why, despising his commands, have you offended Iova by your wickedness? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and took his wife as your wife after killing him with the weapons of the Ammonites. Therefore war shall never depart from your house, since you have despised me and joined the wife of Uriah the Hittite to yourself in marriage. Know that I (says Iova) will raise up evil against you from your own household, and will give your wives to another in your sight, who will lie with them in the sight of this sun. You did it in secret, but I will do it openly before all Israel." Then David said: "I have sinned against Iova." And Nathan said: "Iova also forgives you that sin; you shall not die. Nevertheless, because by this matter you have given occasion for the enemies of Iova to blaspheme, the son who was born to you shall die." 2 Samuel 12.

units.la: LXXVII.
units.tr: LXXVII.

units.la: Sed amavit Solomo rex multas praeter Pharaonis filiam mulieres alienigenas, Moabitidas, Ammonitidas, Idumaeas, Sidonias, Hettaas: de quibus nationibus Iova Israelitis interdixerat, ne vel ipsi ad illas, vel illæ ad ipsos venirent: a. lioquin[?] fore, ut eorum mentes ab illis ad ipsarum pellicerentur deos. Illis amore iunctus Solomo, uxores habuit principes septingentas, & concubinas trecentas, per quas uxores alienatus est ejus animus, & sub tempus senectutis deflexa mens ejus est per illas ad alienos deos: non modo ut animo erga Iovam Deum suum sincero non esset, ut ejus pater David fuerat, sed etiam Astorethum Sidoniorum, L. & Chamosum Moabitarum H.deum & Melcomum Ammonitarum nefas sequetur. Adeoq; Iovam offendit Solomo, adeoq; ei suum officium non praestitit, sicut ejus parens David fecerat: ut etiam Chamofo Moabitarum flagitio fanū in monte Hierosolymis objacente construxerit, & Molocho Ammonitarum flagitio: idemq; fecerit omnibus suis uxoribus alienigenis, quae suffitus & sacra suis faceret diis. Itaq; incensus contra Solomonem Iova, quoniam mente a Iova Deo Israelitarum deflexisset, qui ei semel atque iterum apparuerat, atque hoc praeceperat, ne deos sequeretur alienos, cui Iova praecepta ille non optemperasset, minatus est ei in hunc modum: Quoniam tu commisisti ut fœdus meum & instituta tibi à me tradita non conservares, eripiam ego tibi regnum, idq; servo tuo dabo. 3. Regum 11.
units.tr: But King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter: Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites. Of these nations the LORD had forbidden Israel that either they should go to them or they to Israel, lest, as he said, their hearts be turned away after their gods. Solomon, bound to them by love, had seven hundred princesses as wives and three hundred concubines. Through these wives his heart was turned away, and in the time of his old age his mind was bent by them to strange gods. He not only was not sincere toward the LORD his God, as his father David had been, but also followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh, the god of the Moabites, and Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites. So Solomon offended the LORD and did not render him his duty, as his father David had done. He even built a shrine on the mountain opposite Jerusalem for Chemosh, the abomination of the Moabites, and one for Molech, the abomination of the Ammonites. He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods. Therefore the LORD was kindled against Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him once and again and had commanded him not to follow other gods; and since he had not obeyed this command, the LORD threatened him in this manner: Because you have not kept my covenant and the statutes I gave you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant. 3 Kings 11.

units.la: LXXVIII.
units.tr: LXXVIII.

units.la: Sed Regina Vasti ad regis mandatum per spadones perlatum venire recusavit. Quare vehementi incensus ira Rex, sapientes rerum peritos (solebat enim rex omnibus legis iurisq; prudentibus negocia proponere: et erant tũ ei proximi Charsena, Sethar, Admatha, Tharsis, Mares, Marsana, & Mamuchan, septem Persarum Medorumq; principes, cum rege versantes, et in regno primum dignitatis locum obtinentes) hos inquam interrogat, quid fit Regina Vasti faciendum, quæ Regis Assueri mandato a spadonibus perlato non paruerit. Tum Mamuchan apud regem et proceres verba facit in hanc sententiam: Non solum in regem peccavit regina Vasti, sed etiam in omnes vel principes vel plebeios, qui sunt in omnibus regis Assueri provinciis. Omnes enim mulieres, divul-gata [?]ata hac de regina fama, suos habebunt despectui maritos, cum diceretur reginam Vastim ab Assuero rege accersitam, non venisse: atque hoc regina factum obiicient aliquando primariae Persidis et Mediae mulieres, quae id audiverint, omnibus regiis proceribus, quae res magnum contemptum pariet, & indignitatem. Quamobrem si tibi Rex ita placet, promulgetur regium à te decretum, idq; irrevocabili Persica & Medica lege scriptum, ne regina Vastis in conspectu regis Assueri veniat, ejusq; regnum alteri ea meliori tradas. Hac tua, rex, audita sententia, & per totum imperium tuum quàm late patet publicata, nulla mulier erit, quae non in precio suum habeat conjugem: sive is magnus sit, sive parvus. Placuit & regi & proceribus ea sententia: Mamuchanisq; consilium secutus rex literas dimisit in omnes suas provincias, &c. Esther 1.
units.tr: But Queen Vashti refused to come when the king's command was brought to her by the eunuchs. Therefore the king was greatly enraged, and he consulted the wise men who knew the law and the times (for the king was accustomed to lay matters before all who were skilled in law and judgment). Those nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of the Persians and Medes, who had access to the king and held the first place of dignity in the kingdom. I say he asked them what should be done to Queen Vashti, who had not obeyed the command of King Ahasuerus brought by the eunuchs. Then Memucan spoke before the king and the nobles to this effect: "Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also all the princes and the common people in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. For when the report about the queen becomes known, all the women will hold their husbands in contempt, saying that Queen Vashti was summoned by King Ahasuerus and did not come. And the noble women of Persia and Media who hear of this deed will one day cite it to all the royal nobles, and this will bring great scorn and dishonour. Therefore, if it pleases the king, let a royal decree be issued by you, written in the irrevocable law of Persia and Media, that Vashti may never come into the presence of King Ahasuerus, and that you give her royal position to another who is better than she. When your sentence, O king, is heard and proclaimed throughout your whole realm, however wide it extends, no woman will fail to hold her husband in honour, whether he is great or small." The king and the nobles were pleased with this counsel. Following Memucan's advice, the king sent letters into all his provinces, etc. Esther 1.

units.la: LXXIX.
units.tr: LXXIX.

units.la: Pactionem feci cum meis oculis nequaquam aspicere virgines. Nam quá[?] me fors & conditio ab omnipotente Deo superne maneret? nimirum pernities & interitus, improbos manet & maleficos.
units.tr: I made a covenant with my eyes that I would not look upon a virgin. For what portion or inheritance would I have from God Almighty above, or what reward from the Almighty on high? Surely destruction and ruin await the wicked and the workers of evil.

units.la: Nimirum videt ipse meas vias, omnesq; meos gressus numeratos habet. Si me gessi[?] nequiter, & ad fraudem pedibus festinavi, ponderet me iusta statera, cognoscat Deus integritatem meam. Si gressu de via deflexi, & oculos meos mente secutus sum, aut adhæsit manibus meis macula, quod seminavero comedant alii, meiq; fœtus eradicentur.
units.tr: Surely he sees my ways and counts all my steps. If I have walked in falsehood and my foot has hastened to deceit, let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my integrity. If my step has turned from the way, and my heart has followed my eyes, or if any stain has clung to my hands, let another eat what I have sown, and let my offspring be uprooted.

units.la: Si mentem habui ad mulieres proclivem, aut pro foribus alterius insidiatus sum, molat mea coniunx alteri, eiq; incubent alii. Est enim hoc flagitium crimenq; puniendum, est ignis ad interitum usque edax, qui omnem meum proventum extirparet. Iob.31.
units.tr: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, or if I have lain in wait at my neighbour's door, let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her. For this is a shameful crime that must be punished; it is a fire that devours even to destruction and would root out all my increase. Job 31.

units.la: LXXX.
units.tr: LXXX.

units.la: Fili mi, attende sapientia mea, accommoda aurem meam prudentiam, ut industriam custodias, & tuis labiis tueare scien-tiam. Nam favo fluunt aliena labra, ejusq; fauces oleo sunt molliores: sed ejus exitus tam est amarus quàm absynthium,tamq; acutus,quàm gladius anceps: Ejus pedes ad mortem descendunt, ejus vestigia tendunt in Orcum. Vita viam non librat,errantibus nescio quò ejus itineribus. Quare,nati,audite me⌣[?],& ab oris mei dictis ne recedite⌣[?]. Procul ab ea iter facito, néve ad ejus adium fores accedito, ne honorem tuum aliis, ne tuos annos addicas crudelibus, ne tuis facultatibus satientur alieni, sintq; tui labores in peregrina domo, & tu postremò tuo corpore⌣[?], victuq; consumpto gemas, atque ita dicas: Curodi disciplinam,& castigationem animo fastidivi: nec magistrorum meorum dictis obtemperavi: nec præceptoribus aurem præbui: propemodum sum in omnibus malis, in medio vulgo atque cætu. Bibe ex tuis cisternis aquam & latices, & ex medio tuo puteo: scateant aquæ rivis fontes tui foris vicatim, quos tu solus habeas, non etiam alieni tecum. Sit tuus fons felix,& fruere tua juventutus uxore, amabili cerva, lepidaq; dama, cujus te omni tempore⌣[?] irrigent ubera, cujus amore potiare semper. Cur autem potiare, mi fili, alienâ? cur in gremio non tua hæreas? cùm ob oculos positas habeat Iova vias hominis, & eius gressus libret omnes. Ipse suis criminibus capitur impius, suorumq; peccatorum restibus implicatur, moriturus sine correctione, & suam tantam luiturus insaniam. Proverb.5.
units.tr: My son, attend to my wisdom, incline your ear to my understanding, that you may keep discretion and your lips may guard knowledge. For the lips of a strange woman drip honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil; but her end is as bitter as wormwood and as sharp as a two-edged sword. Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold of hell. She does not weigh the path of life; her ways wander, and she does not know where they lead. Therefore, sons, hear me, and do not depart from the words of my mouth. Keep your way far from her, and do not come near the door of her house, lest you give your honour to others and your years to the cruel, lest strangers be filled with your wealth, and your labours be in a foreign house, and you groan at last when your flesh and your body are consumed, and say: "How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof! I did not obey the voice of my teachers, nor incline my ear to those who instructed me. I was almost in all evil, in the midst of the people and the assembly." Drink water from your own cisterns and the streams from your own well. Let your springs flow abroad, and your rivers of water in the streets; let them be yours alone, not shared with strangers. Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth, a lovely hind and a graceful doe, whose breasts satisfy you at all times and whose love keeps you always enraptured. Why, my son, should you be ravished by a stranger and embrace the bosom of another? For the LORD sees the ways of man and weighs all his steps. The wicked is caught in his own iniquities and is held fast by the cords of his sins; he will die without correction and will bear the weight of his great folly. Proverbs 5.

units.la: LXXXI.
units.tr: LXXXI.

units.la: Qui uxorem (scilicet bonam) invenit, bonum invenit, & Iova favorem obtinuit. Proverb.18.
units.tr: He who finds a wife (namely a good one) finds a good thing and has obtained favour from the LORD. Proverbs 18.

units.la: LXXXII.
units.tr: LXXXII.

units.la: Domus & opes sunt hæreditas patria: sed intelligens uxor à Iova est. Proverbior. 18.
units.tr: House and wealth are an inheritance from the fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD. Proverbs 19.

units.la: LXXXIII.
units.tr: LXXXIII.

units.la: Præbe mihi, mi fili, tuam mentem, oculique tui meis delectentur institutis. Nam profundus gurges est meretrix, angustaq; scrobs mulier aliena. Ea sanè latronum more insidiatur, & hominum perfidos conficit. Cui heu? cui heu? cui jurgia? cui solicitudo? cui vulnera impune? cui oculorum rubor? Vini sectatoribus, compotationes rimatum euntibus. G. Nolite vino inebriari, sed cum bonis viris H. & se probè gerentibus, G. consuetudinem habete ac versamini. Vinum ne aspice quia rubeat, quia in poculo colorem suum ostentet, & specie sua blandiatur. Ejus exitus mordet ut coluber, & vipera modo pungit. Et oculi tui absurdè videbunt, & animus ineptè loquetur. Erisque quasi qui in medio mari, aut quasi qui in mali navis vertice cubet. Verberatus non doleo, i[?]ctus non sentio, experrectus idem iterum requiram. Proverb.23.
units.tr: Give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes delight in my ways. For a harlot is a deep pit, and a strange woman is a narrow well. She lies in wait like a robber and makes many faithless among men. Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaining? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes? Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed wine. G. Do not be drunk with wine, but keep company with good men, H. and those who conduct themselves well. G. Do not look at wine when it is red, when it shows its colour in the cup and flatters with its appearance. Its end bites like a serpent and stings like a viper. Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perversely. You will be like one lying in the midst of the sea, or like one sleeping on the top of a ship's mast. "They struck me, but I was not hurt; they beat me, but I did not feel it. When shall I wake up? I will seek it again." Proverbs 23.

units.la: LXXXIIII.
units.tr: LXXXIIII.

units.la: Stillicidium pluvio tempore perfluens, & uxor rixosa similia sunt. Eam qui recondit, ventum recondit, aut clamaturum in dextera sua unguentum. Proverb.27.
units.tr: A dripping roof in rainy weather and a quarrelsome wife are alike. Whoever hides her hides the wind, or grasps oil in his right hand. Proverbs 27.

units.la: LXXXV.
units.tr: LXXXV.

units.la: Strenuam mulierem quis inveniat: cujus precium gemmas longè superat. Ei confidit ex animo maritus, nec cibariorum est indigus. Ipsa de eo bene, non male meretur per omnem vitam suam. Lanam quaerit & lina, & manibus libenter operatur. Similis est mercatoriae navis, victum suum procul advehens. Surgitq; de nocte, & familiae suae cibum, ancillisq; pensum distribuit. Cogitat de fundo, eumq; comparat, & suarum manuum quaestu pangit vineam, sua latera fortiter succingit, suaq; brachia confirmat. Sentit quam bonum sit suum negotium, inextincta noctu ejus lucerna.
units.tr: Who can find a woman of strength? Her price is far above rubies. The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will have no lack of gain. She does him good and not evil all the days of her life. She seeks wool and flax and works willingly with her hands. She is like a merchant ship, bringing her food from afar. She rises while it is still night and gives food to her household and portions to her maidservants. She considers a field and buys it; with the earnings of her hands she plants a vineyard. She girds her loins with strength and makes her arms strong. She perceives that her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.

units.la: Admovet colo manus, fusumq; manibus tenet.
units.tr: She puts her hands to the distaff and holds the spindle in her hands.

units.la: Manus inopi pauperiq; praebet ac porrigit. Non metuit suam familiam a nive, quippe cum sit omnis ejus familia vestita cocco. Stragulam vestem sibi facit: lineum purpureumq; vestitum habet. Conspicuus est in curiis maritus ejus, dum sedet in civium senatu. Lintea facit ac vendit, & cingula mercatoribus suppeditat. Praeclare & honeste vestita futurum tempus eludit. Os suum sapienter aperit, pietatis disciplinam habens in lingua. Familiæ suæ statum considerat, nec pigritiæ cibo vescitur. Assurgunt liberi qui eam beatam ferant: ejus quoque maritus eam laudat. Multa fœmina rem fecerunt: sed tu eas omnes transcendis. Fallax gratia, vana pulchritudo, mulier Jova metuens laudabilis est. Huic detur manuum suarum fructus, eamq; in curiis sua laudent opera. Proverb.31.
units.tr: She stretches out her hands to the poor and needy. She does not fear for her household from the snow, since her whole household is clothed in scarlet. She makes coverings for herself; she has clothing of linen and purple. Her husband is conspicuous in the courts, while he sits in the senate of the citizens. She makes linen and sells it, and supplies belts to merchants. She is clothed with excellence and honour, and she laughs at the time to come. She opens her mouth wisely, having the teaching of kindness on her tongue. She watches over the state of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness. Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband too praises her. Many women have done well, but you surpass them all. Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised. Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the courts. Proverb.31.

units.la: LXXXVI.
