units.tr: LXXXVI.

units.la: Possumne tibi istud ignoscere? tui nati, relicto me per non Deos jurant, & a me satiati, adulterant, inq; lupanar sese cuneant. Equi sunt saginati, matutini, alii in aliorum uxores adhinnientes. In istáne ut ego non animadvertā? inquit Jova: aut ab istiusmodi gente pœnas non repetam? Scandite muros ejus, & vastate, sic tamen ut ad internecionem non agatis: detrahite ejus palmites, quoniam Jova nō sunt. Nam mihi fide fregerunt Israelita, Judæaq; domus, inquit Jova. Jovam abnegant, eumq; esse, aut sibi malum eventurum, aut se arma famém ve visuros negant. Vates autem ventosi sunt, nec est eorum quisquam qui quid sit eis futurum, ante denunciet. Ierem.5.
units.tr: Can I pardon you for this? Your sons swear by those who are not gods, forsaking me; when I have satisfied them, they commit adultery and crowd into the brothel. They are well-fed horses, roaming in the morning, each neighing after another's wife. Shall I not take notice of such things? says the LORD. Or shall I not exact punishment from such a nation? Climb her walls and lay them waste, but do not bring about complete destruction; strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken faith with me, says the LORD. They deny the LORD, and say that he is nothing, and that no evil will come upon them, and that they will not see sword or famine. The prophets are windbags, and not one of them can foretell what will happen to them. Jer.5.

units.la: LXXXVII.
units.tr: LXXXVII.

units.la: En vos falsis confiditis, rebus nihil juvatibus, furari, occidere, adulterare, pejerare, suffire Baali, alienos q; sequi Deos, vobis ignotos: & postea venitis, in meoq; stantes conspectu, in hac à me denominata ade[?], defendi postulatis, ut ista tot scelera committatis? Pro spelunca grassu[?]torum habetis hanc à me nuncupatam ædem, id quod ego quoque (ut sciatis) inquit Iova, video. Adite enim locum meum, qui est Silunte, ubi ego meum nomen primo collocaveram, & videte quo pacto eum tractaverim ob Israelitarum meorum improbitatem. Quamobrem quoniam vos ista tot patratis facinora, inquit Iova, mihique vos sedulo admonenti non auscultatis, neque vocantem auditis, faciam adi(quae à me nomen habet, cuique vos confiditis) & loco (quem vobis, vestrisq; dedi majoribus) quomodo feci Silunti, vosq; à meo reiciam conspectu[?], quemadmodum reieci vestros omnes fratres, scilicet omnem Ephraimi progeniem. Ierem.7.
units.tr: Look, you trust in false words that profit nothing: to steal, to murder, to commit adultery, to swear falsely, to burn incense to Baal, and to follow other gods unknown to you. And then you come and stand before me in this house named after me, and ask to be defended, so that you may commit all these crimes? You have made this house named after me a den of robbers; I too see it, as you know, says the LORD. For go to my place at Shiloh, where I first set my name, and see how I treated it on account of the wickedness of my people Israel. Therefore, since you commit all these deeds, says the LORD, and do not listen when I urgently admonish you, nor answer when I call, I will do to the house that bears my name and in which you trust, and to the place I gave you and your fathers, just as I did to Shiloh; and I will cast you out of my sight, as I cast out all your brothers, that is, the whole offspring of Ephraim. Jer.7.

units.la: LXXXVIII.
units.tr: LXXXVIII.

units.la: Sic dicit armipotens Iova, Deus Israelitarum, omnibus exulibus, quos ipse Hierosolymis in Babyloniam relegavit. Ædificate quas habitetis domos, & hortos, quorum fructu vescamini, conserite: ducite uxores, liberosq; gignite, & filiis vestris uxores capite, & filias nuptum locate, quae liberos pariant, atq; ibi crescite, neve decrescite, & salutistudete[?] urbis, quò vos ego relegavi, Iovam q; pro ea orate: nam in ejus salute vobis sita salus est. Ierem.29.
units.tr: Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, to all the exiles whom he sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon: Build houses to live in, and plant gardens, and eat their fruit; take wives and beget sons and daughters, and take wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they may bear children; and there increase, and do not decrease. And seek the welfare of the city to which I have sent you, and pray to the LORD for it, for in its welfare your welfare lies. Jer.29.

units.la: LXXXIX.
units.tr: LXXXIX.

units.la: Item me affatus est his verbis Iova: Tu vero, homo, scilicet patrocineris, scilicet patrocineris urbi cruenta[?]simò ei demōstra ejus tot scelera, & dicito: Sic dicit Dominus Iova: O urbs q[?] in medio tui sanguine fudisti, ut tuū tempus veniat, stercoreos q; divos contra temetipsam fecisti, ut polluaris: tu isto, quem fudisti, cruore, noxam contraxisti, istisq; quos fecisti, stercoreis divis polluta es, & diem tuam adduxisti, ad annosq; pervenisti tuos, quam ob causam ego te gentium terrarumq; omnium ostentui & ludibrio exponam, ut te & propinquæ & à te remotæ, illudant, & nomine pollutam, & turbis insignem. Equidem in te principes Israelitarum, pro suis quisque viribus, in ea fuerunt ut sanguinem funderent: in te patres matresq; contempti sunt: in medio tui peregrinus facta injuria est: in te oppressi sunt pupilli & viduæ, tu meum sanum despicata es, meaq; polluisti Sabatha. In te calumniatores fuerunt causa fundendi sanguinis: in te per montes pol luctum[?] est: in medio tui facta sunt incesta: in te verenda patrum retecta sunt: in te polluta menstruales cōpreffæ sunt: in te & vir cum alterius uxore flagitium commisit, & socer nurum incesto polluit, & sororem srater eodem patre natam compressit. In te dona accepta sunt ob fundendum sanguinem: tufœnus ufuramq; cepisti, & alios avare per injuriam fruaudasti, oblita mei, inquit Dominus Iova. Ezech.22.
units.tr: Moreover the LORD spoke to me in these words: And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? Show her all her abominations, and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: O city that sheddest blood in the midst of you, so that your time may come, and that makes idols against yourself to defile yourself; you have become guilty by the blood you have shed, and defiled by the idols you have made; you have brought near your days and reached your years; therefore I will make you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all lands. Those near and far from you will mock you, you who are infamous and full of turmoil. Behold, the princes of Israel, each according to his power, have been in you to shed blood. In you father and mother have been despised; in your midst the stranger has been wronged; in you the fatherless and widow have been oppressed. You have despised my holy things and profaned my sabbaths. In you are slanderers who shed blood; in you they eat on the mountains; in your midst they commit lewdness. In you they have uncovered their fathers' nakedness; in you they have defiled women in their uncleanness. In you one has committed abomination with his neighbour's wife, another has defiled his daughter-in-law with incest, and another has violated his sister, his father's daughter. In you they have taken bribes to shed blood; you have taken usury and interest, and have greedily gained from your neighbours by oppression, and you have forgotten me, says the Lord GOD. Ezek.22.

units.la: X C.
units.tr: XC.

units.la: Nónne patrem unum habemus nos omnes? nónne nos Deus unus creavit? cur prodit frater fratrem, profanando nostrum fœdus patrium? Proditor est Iudaus, fitq; nefas in Israelitis ac Hierosolymis: siquidem profanat Iudaus fanum Iovæ quod amavit, peregriniq; Dei puellam maritat. Evertet Iehova virum qui id fecerit, vigilantem & respondentem ex Iacobæis tabernaculis, & fertum armipotenti Iovæ obmoventem. Adde quod efficitis, ut obtegatur lachrymis ara Iovæ ploratu ac suspiriis, ita ut non amplius ferta respiciat, neque placamina ex vestra manu admittat. Quaretis, quamobrem? quoniam Iova tibi & tuæ juventutis uxori conscius est, in quam tu perfidiosus es, cùm sit tua socia, & tibi fœderata conjunx. Quod si unus fecit qui spiritu abundabat, quorsum allegatur unus ille[?], qui divinam progeniem quærebat? at vos animis cavete[?],ne in vestra juventutis uxores agatur perfide. Qui odit, repudiet, inquit Iova Deus Israelitarum: & tegat iniquitatem veste sua, inquit armipotens Iova: & cavete animis, ne perfidè agatis. Malach. 2.
units.tr: Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Why does a brother betray a brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers? Judah is a traitor, and an abomination is done in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah profanes the sanctuary of the LORD which he loved, and marries the daughter of a foreign god. May the LORD cut off the man who does this, both the watchman and the answerer from the tents of Jacob, and the one who offers gifts to the LORD of hosts. Moreover, you do this: you cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and sighing, so that it no longer looks upon the offering or accepts favour from your hand. You ask, why? Because the LORD is witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant. But if one who had a remnant of spirit did so, why was that one sought, who sought a godly offspring? But take heed in your spirits, that you do not deal faithlessly with the wife of your youth. Whoever hates and divorces, says the LORD God of Israel, covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts; so take heed in your spirits, that you do not act faithlessly. Mal.2.

units.la: X C I.
units.tr: XCI.

units.la: Congrediar autè vobiscum judicio, e-roq; celer testis in præstigiatores, in adulteros, in perjuros, in eos quì mercede fraudant mercenarios, qui viduas, qui pupillos, qui peregrinos labefactant, neque me timent, inquit armipotens Iova. Malach. 3.
units.tr: I will draw near to you in judgment, and will be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers, those who defraud hired labourers of their wages, who oppress widows, orphans and strangers, and do not fear me, says the LORD of hosts. Mal.3.

units.la: X C II.
units.tr: XCII.

units.la: Tu ergo, nate[?], corpus tuum ab omni fœditate & impudicitia tuere, L. neve committito ut omissa uxore tua flagitium admittas: H. & uxorem ducito de cognatione tua, non ullius generis, quod à majorum tuorum stirpe sit alienum. Nos enim de vatum progenie sumus. Memoria repete, fili, Abrahamum, Isacum, tum,& Iacobum, qui uxores de sua sibi gente asciverunt, extraneorum affinitate repudiata, eóque liberis fortunati fuerunt: G. eorumque posteri terram obtinuerunt. Quamobrem, nate, dilige tuos consanguineos, néve eos aut tuorum popularium filios, aut filias ita animo fastidiveris, ut ex eis uxorem non ducas. Tob. 4.
units.tr: Therefore, my son, guard your body from all filthiness and immodesty, and take care not to commit a crime by neglecting your wife; and take a wife from your own kin, not from any stock alien to your ancestors. For we are the offspring of the prophets. Remember, son, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who took wives for themselves from their own people, rejecting marriage with foreigners, and so were blessed in their children, and their descendants obtained the land. Therefore, my son, love your kinsmen, and do not in your heart despise your kinsmen or the sons and daughters of your people, so as to refuse to take a wife from among them. Tob.4.

units.la: XCIII.
units.tr: XCIII.

units.la: Cui angelus: L. Attende & ostendam tibi in quos potestatem habeat daemon. Qui in matrimonium ita conveniunt ut expertes & immemores Dei, more equi aut muli brutorum animalium, vacent libidini, in hos potestatem habet daemon. H. Verere modo Iovam, inquit, ejusque memor esto, patrisque tui praeceptum recordare, a quo jussus es uxorem ejusdem tecum paterna stirpis ducere: tum me authore nihil daemonem timueris. Nam satis exploratum habeo, te eam hac nocte in matrimonium esse ducturū[?]. Igitur ubi in cubiculum cum ea introieris, (L. per tres dies ab ea te abstinebis; & nihil aliud quàm precibus eum ea vâ cabis. Secunda noćte in sanćtorum patriarcharum consortium admitteris. Tertia noćte eam consequêre felicitatē, ut ex vobis liberi prosperè gignantur,) H. sumito corpiscis, & inde suffitum sub ejus vestes facito, eo nidore olfacto, dæmon puellam fugiet: nec eam unquam postea repetet. Sed cùm tibi cum ea congredi libebit, surgitote de lecto, Iovamq; supplicite r oratote, ut sua in vos clementia & medicina utatur, puellaq; medeatur. Tum demum cum ea rem habebis, L. liberorum amore magis, quàm libidine dućtus: H. ex qua liberos mares procreabis. Sed metum abjce: nam ea tibi destinata est ante orbem conditum, eámque tua opera Iova à damone vindicabit. Tob.6.
units.tr: The angel said to him: Listen, and I will show you over whom the demon has power. Those who enter marriage so that they are without God and forgetful of him, given over to lust like horses or mules, the brute animals, over these the demon has power. Only fear the LORD, he said, and be mindful of him, and remember your father's command, by which you were ordered to take a wife of your father's own stock; and with me as your witness, fear the demon not at all. For I am well assured that you will take her in marriage this very night. So when you have gone into the bedchamber with her (for three days you shall abstain from her and do nothing but pray with her; on the second night you shall be admitted to the fellowship of the holy patriarchs; on the third night you shall attain the blessing that children be born to you both in prosperity), take the heart and liver of the fish and make a smoke under her clothes; when the demon smells the odour he will flee from the girl and never return to her. But when you wish to lie with her, rise from the bed, and pray and beseech the LORD that he may use his mercy and healing upon you, and heal the girl. Then at last, when you have intercourse with her, be led more by love of children than by lust; from her you will beget male children. Put away fear, for she was destined for you before the world was made, and by your labour the LORD will deliver her from the demon. Tob.6.

units.la: XCIIII.
units.tr: XCIIII.

units.la: Igitur Raphael adhibitis duobus camelis, & quatuor famulis, Ragem domum Gabelis ire contendit, eiq; ipsius marsupium tradit, & Tobiam Tobaei filium duxisse Sarā Raguelis filiam nunciat, ciat, eumque ad illius nuptias invitat. Tum Gabel impositio camelis argento, ad nuptias venit, & Tobiam nactus asidentem mensæ amplectitur, & præ gaudio lachrymans, ei gratulatur huiusmodi verbis: Gratias ago Iova Israelitarum Deo, qui te cum hoc viro lætè conjunxerit. Is tibi pro sua misericordia det exista mares liberos, qui Iovæ legi dent operam: L. nam viri optimi, justi, religiosi, & benefici filius es. Felix dicatur uxor tua, parentesque vestri, ita ut natos vestros, & natorum natos, ad tertiam usque quartamque stirpem videatis, sitque vestra progenies Israelitarum Deo, qui regnat in sempiternum, chara. Hic cum omnes Amen fuccinuissent, inierunt epulas, & cum Domini reverentia nuptiarum convivium celebrarunt, G. suaq; uxori fausta precatus est Tobias. Tob.9.
units.tr: Therefore Raphael, taking two camels and four servants, hastened to Gabael's house at Rages, handed over to him his money-bag, and announced that Tobias, son of Tobias, had married Sara, daughter of Raguel, and invited him to the wedding. Then Gabael loaded the silver onto the camels and came to the wedding. Finding Tobias sitting at table, he embraced him and, weeping for joy, congratulated him in these words: "I give thanks to Iova, the God of the Israelites, who has joined you happily with this man. May he in his mercy give you male children who will serve the law of Iova, for you are the son of a most excellent, just, devout and beneficent man. Happy be your wife, and happy your parents; may you see your sons and your sons' sons to the third and fourth generation, and may your offspring be dear to the God of Israel, who reigns forever." When all had said Amen, they began the feast and celebrated the banquet of the wedding with reverence for the Lord; and Tobias blessed his wife with good fortune.

units.la: XCV.
units.tr: XCV.

units.la: Nullum caput serpentis capite nocentius est: nulla ira, mulieris iram superat. Cum leone malim & dracone degere, quàm cum mala muliere habitare.
units.tr: No head of a serpent is more harmful than a woman's head; no wrath surpasses a woman's wrath. I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon than live with a wicked woman.

units.la: Mulieris nequitia ejus aspectum immutat, & vultum tanquam saccum infuscat. Ea efficit ut vir ejus cogatur inter alios sedere, & acerbè gemere. Parva est quævis pravitas, præ mulieris pravitate, in quam precor improbi sorte cadant. Quod scrupulosius ascensus est pedibus senis, id est linguax mulier quieto viro. In fœmina pulchritudinem ne offenditò, neve mulierem voluptatis causa concupiscito. Ingens pœna, & impudentia & turpitudo est mulier, si suo viro imperat.
units.tr: A woman's wickedness changes her face and darkens her countenance like sackcloth. It makes her husband be forced to sit apart from others and groan bitterly. Any other wickedness is small beside a woman's wickedness, into whose lot I pray the wicked may fall. What is more troublesome than an old man's climbing on foot is a talkative woman for a quiet husband. Do not be offended by a woman's beauty, nor desire a woman for the sake of pleasure. A woman who commands her husband is a great punishment, a shamelessness and a disgrace.

units.la: Afflicta mens, & mœsta facies, & animi vulnus est, & remissa manus resolutaq; genua, ubi mala mulier est, quæ virum suum nequaquam beat. A fœmina initium peccati, per eamq; morimur omnes.
units.tr: A troubled mind, a sad face, a wound of the spirit, and slack hands and loosened knees: this is where a woman is wicked and does not make her husband happy. From a woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.

units.la: Nec aqua L. vel tantillum G. exitum dederis, nec mala mulieri potestate. Nisi tibi sub manu obsequitur, L. te in inimicorum conspectu pudore afficiet: G. abscinde eam à tuo corpore, amanda ac repudia, L. ne te semper abutatur. G. Ecclesiastici [?] 25.
units.tr: Give water no outlet, and a wicked woman no power at all. If she does not obey your hand, she will shame you before your enemies; cut her off from your body, let her go and put her away, lest she abuse you always. Ecclesiasticus 25.

units.la: XCVI.
units.tr: XCVI.

units.la: Post obitum Iuda prodierunt in omnibus Israelitarum finibus homines nesarii: omnesque exorti sunt malefici, ad quos, ut[?] iisdem temporibus fame gravissima, perfugerunt incolæ. Tum Bacchides delectos homines impios regionis administrationi prapofuit, qui conquisitos & pervestigatos Iuda amicos ad ipsum perducerent, quos ille cum omni ludibrio afficiebat supplicio: tantaque fuit ea Israelitarum calamitas, quanta nulla fuerat, ex quo tempore nullus apud eos vates extiterat.
units.tr: After the death of Judas, wicked men appeared in all the territories of the Israelites, and all the evildoers arose, and because of the very severe famine in those same times, the inhabitants fled to them. Then Bacchides set ungodly, chosen men over the administration of the region, who sought out and tracked down Judas's friends and brought them to him, and he punished them with every mockery and torture. Such was the calamity of the Israelites, greater than any before, from the time when no prophet had arisen among them.

units.la: Tum omnes Iuda amici ad Ionathanem conveniunt: demonstrant, ex quo Iudas eius frater oppetierit, neminem esse Ionathani parem, qui se hostibus & Bacchidi, reliquisque gentem suam infestantibus opponat. Itaque se eum jam deligere, qui eis pro illo & dux & ad bellum gerendum imperator esset. Tum Ionathan principatum accepit, & Iuda fratri suo successit. Quod ubi resciuit Bacchides, eum conatus est interficere. Hac re cognita Ionathan & Simon ejus frater, omnésque comites, in Thecua solitudinem profugerunt, & ad aquas lacus Asphar castra fecerunt. Quod postquam intellexit Bacchides, die sabbathi venit cum exercitu suo trans Iordanem. Tum Ionathan fratrem suum Iohannem imbellium turbæ præfectum misit ad Nabathæos amicos suos, oratum ut liceret apud eos impedimenta sua, quæ multa erant deponere. Sed Iambris nati Medaba ingressi, Iohannem, & quæ habebat omnia, ceperunt atque abduxerunt. Postea nunciatur Ionathani & Simoni ejus fratri, Iambrinos insignes nuptias celebrantes, sponsam ducere ex Nadabatha, magno cum apparatu, filiam cujusdam de præcipuis Chananeæ primatibus. Itaque memores Iohannis fratris sui, eò profecti sunt: & montis objectu occultati, cùm magnam turbam & apparatum animadvertissent, sponsúmque cum suis amicis & consanguineis obviam illis progressum, cum tympanis, musicisq;et armis multis, prodierunt in illos ex insidiis, eorumque stragem ediderunt: & multis interfectis, reliquis in montem fuga dilapsis, omnia diripuerunt, atque ita nuptias in luctum, & cantum musicum in lamentationem converterunt, suique fratris ulti sanguinem in Iordanis paludem redierunt. Hac audita revenit die sabbathi Bacchides ad ripam Iordanis, cum multis copiis. Tum Ionathan suos sic adhortatus est: Agite jam, pugnemus pro vita nostra. Non enim sic se res habet hodie, ut superiaribus diebus: ecce enim nobis & a fronte hostes, & a tergo Iordanis aqua, & hinc atque hinc palus atque sylva, nec est ad declinandum locus. Quocirca clamate ad coelum, ut hostiles manus evadatis. Deinde commisso prælio, manum extulit Ionathan, ut Bacchidem feriret: atque illo in tergum cedente, insiluit Ionathan & ejus milites in Iordanem, atque ita tranarunt, nec adversarij secuti sunt.
units.tr: Then all Judas's friends came together to Jonathan. They showed him that since his brother Judas had fallen, there was no one equal to Jonathan to oppose the enemies, Bacchides, and the rest who were attacking his nation. So they now chose him to be leader in Judas's place and commander to wage the war. Then Jonathan took up the leadership and succeeded his brother Judas. When Bacchides learned of this, he tried to kill him. Having learned this, Jonathan and his brother Simon and all their companions fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and made camp by the waters of the pool of Asphar. When Bacchides understood this, on the Sabbath day he came with his army across the Jordan. Then Jonathan sent his brother John, prefect of the unarmed multitude, to his friends the Nabateans, asking that they might be allowed to store their baggage, which was large, with them. But the sons of Jambri from Medaba came out, seized John and everything he had, and carried them off. Afterwards it was reported to Jonathan and his brother Simon that the sons of Jambri were celebrating a splendid wedding and leading the bride from Nadabath with great pomp, the daughter of one of the chief nobles of Canaan. So, mindful of their brother John, they went there; and hidden by the cover of a mountain, when they saw the great crowd and display, and the bridegroom coming out to meet them with his friends and relatives, with drums, musicians and many weapons, they burst out upon them from ambush and made a great slaughter. With many killed and the rest scattered in flight to the mountain, they plundered everything, and so turned the wedding into mourning and the music into lamentation, and avenged their brother's blood, and returned to the marsh of the Jordan. When this was heard, Bacchides returned on the Sabbath day to the bank of the Jordan with many troops. Then Jonathan exhorted his men thus: "Come, let us fight for our lives. For things are not as they were on earlier days: behold, the enemies are before us and the waters of the Jordan behind us, and on either side marsh and forest, and there is no place to turn aside. Therefore cry out to heaven, that you may escape the hands of the enemy." Then, when battle was joined, Jonathan raised his hand to strike Bacchides; and as Bacchides gave ground, Jonathan and his soldiers leapt into the Jordan and swam across, and the enemies did not follow them.

units.la: Cùm esset desponsa mater ejus Maria Iosepho, priusquam convenissent, comperta est uterum ferre ex spiritu sancto. Iosephus vero vir ejus, qui justus esset, nec in eam vellet exemplum edere, statuit eam clam repudiare. Haec cum haberet in animo, ecce Domini angelus in somnis apparuit ei, et ita locutus est: Iosephe Davide prognate, ne metue asciscere Mariam uxorem tuam: nam quod in ea genitum est, ex sancto spiritu est. Pariet autem filium, quem Iesum nomine vocabis: is enim suos ab ipsorum peccatis vindicabit. Hoc autem totum factum est, ut confieret, quod a Domino dictum fuerat per vatem ita dicentem: Virgo ventrem latura est, et editura filium, qui nominabitur Emmanuel: quod perinde est ac si dicas, Nobiscum Deus. Igitur experrectus a somno Iosephus, fecit ut ei praeceperat Domini angelus, ascivitque suam conjugem: nec eam cognovit, donec ea peperit filium suum primogenitum, quem Iesum nomine vocavit.
units.tr: When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit. Joseph, her husband, being just and unwilling to make an example of her, decided to put her away secretly. While he had this in mind, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and spoke thus: "Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife; for what has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, whom you shall call Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. Now all this has happened so that what the Lord spoke through the prophet, saying, might be fulfilled: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, who shall be called Emmanuel, which means, God with us." So Joseph, awakened from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his wife; and he did not know her until she bore her firstborn son, whom he named Jesus.

units.la: Ut autem accidit tempore Noe, sic etiam erit adventus filii hominis. Ut enim tempore, quod fuit ante diluvium, comedebatur, potabatur, contrahebantur invicem matrimonia, usq; ad diem quo Noe in arcam ingressus est, nec ante cognitum est quàm venit diluvium, quod omnes sustulit: sic erit etiam adventus filii hominis. Tum ex duobus, qui ruri erunt, alter assumetur, alter relinquetur: ex duabus in pistrino molentibus, altera assumetur, altera relinquetur. Matth 24.
units.tr: As it was in the days of Noah, so also will be the coming of the Son of man. For as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, and marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away, so also will be the coming of the Son of man. Then of two men in the field, one will be taken and the other left; of two women grinding at the mill, one will be taken and the other left. Matthew 24.

units.la: Tertio autem die nuptiæ factæ sunt Cana in Galilæa, ubi & Jesu mater erat. Et Jesus, ejusque discipuli ad nuptias vocati sunt. Cumque defecisset vinum, Jesum mater sic alloquitur: Vinum non habent. Cui Jesus: Quid tum postea?[?] mulier, nondum venit hora mea. Mater ministros monuit, ut quod ille eis jussisset, facerent. Erant illic posita sex lapidea folia, ut ferebat Judæorum purificatio, binarum ternarúmve metretarum capacia. Ea folia ut aqua replerent, jußit eis Iesus. Cúmque ad summum usque replevissent, jußit ut nunc haurirent, & convivii magistro ferrent. Atque illi tulerunt.
units.tr: On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, where Jesus's mother was. Jesus and his disciples were invited to the wedding. When the wine ran short, his mother said to Jesus, "They have no wine." Jesus said to her, "What then? Woman, my hour has not yet come." His mother told the servants to do whatever he told them. Six stone jars stood there, as the Jewish purification required, each holding two or three measures. Jesus told them to fill the jars with water. When they had filled them to the brim, he told them to draw some out now and carry it to the master of the feast. And they carried it.

units.la: Vt vero gustavit convivii magister factum ex aqua vinum, ignarus unde esset (nam ministri quidā sciebant, qui aquam hauserant) sponsum accersit, & sic alloquitur: Cum omnes homines primum bonum vinum apponant, deinde potis convivis deterius, tu bonum vinum hucusque servasti. Hoc prabuit miraculorum initium Iesus Cana in Gallilaea, suamque gloriam ostendit, & ei fidem habuerunt ejus discipuli. Ioann.2.
units.tr: When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, not knowing where it came from (though the servants who had drawn the water knew), he called the bridegroom and said to him: "Everyone sets out the good wine first, and then the poorer wine when the guests have drunk freely; but you have kept the good wine until now." This was the beginning of the miracles that Jesus performed at Cana in Galilee, and he revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him. John 2.

units.la: Sunt autem manifesta carnis opera, videlicet adulterium, stuprum, impuritas, falacitas, deastrorum cultus, veneficium, inimicitia, lis, aemulationes, iracundia, contentiones, seditiones, sectae, invidia, homicidia, ebrietates, commessationes, & hisfimilia: qua qui faciunt
units.tr: Now the works of the flesh are plain: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, dissensions, factions, envy, murders, drunkenness, carousing, and things like these; of which I forewarn you, as I have also forewarned you, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

units.la: (hoc vobis praedico, quemadmodum jam praedixi) ij[?] divinum regnum non obtinebunt. At spiritus fructus, est charitas, gaudium, pax, clemētia, benignitas, bonitas, fides, lenitas, cōtinentia. Contra talia non est lex. Qui sunt autem Christi, ij[?] carnem una cum libidinibus & cupiditatibus crucifixerunt. Si spiritu vivimus, etiam spiritu gradiamur, ne simus gloriosi, invicem provocantes, invicem invidentes.
units.tr: (I tell you this beforehand, as I have already said) those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, clemency, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law. Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit; let us not be conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.
